the text of the parliament's resolution on the digital single market strategy contains many welcome slogans on competitiveness, consumer protection, jobs, trade development and gdp growth. of course it matters. i also want to draw attention to what is not in the document. these are the negative effects of the digitalisation of markets. i'm talking about the disappearance of local markets, the homogenization of products, the decline in quality, and of course the climate impact of human activities that are focused solely on gdp growth. of course, some may say that these are the natural consequences of globalization. and they will not be very wrong, but we should also, when we are considering a digital single market strategy, include measures to encourage consumers to make their online purchasing decisions with information about the impact of their decision on small producers and the climate.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the european parliament's examination of the immunity of mr czesław adam ascher. on 13 august 2015, the prosecutor general of the republic of poland forwarded to the president of the parliament a request from the polish road traffic inspectorate to authorise the prosecution of mr czesław adam askierski, member of the european parliament, for an administrative offence speeding. according to the polish road traffic inspectorate, at 20.22 on 10 january 2015, c. a. aszerski was driving a car at a speed exceeding the speed limit in the settlement and travelling at 77 km/h with a speed limit of 50 km/h. the general inspectorate further states that, in response to the summons sent to mr assierski on 19 january 2015, mr assierski sent copies of his mep identity card, his certificate of election to the european parliament and a statement acknowledging that he had driven the vehicle during the specified period. it is apparent from the file that mr askierskis admitted that he had driven the vehicle during the period prescribed, but did not indicate on the relevant form whether he agreed or disagreed with the imposition of the fine. it is clear from the circumstances of the case that the suspicion of having committed an administrative offence and the subsequent administrative prosecution had nothing to do with mr assierski's duties as a member of the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean. in order to ensure a uniform and effective application of all measures adopted in the 2012-2014 recovery plan throughout the european union, this proposal aims to incorporate them into a regulation. the proposal includes technical measures such as those related to the transfer and caging operations of live bluefin tuna, the catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the regional observer programme of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean. the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. iccat has the power to adopt decisions (recommendations) on the conservation and management of fisheries resources within its area of competence; these acts are binding; they must be transposed into european union law. bluefin tuna is the most important species to be regulated by iccat. in order to ensure a uniform and effective application of all measures adopted in the 2012-2014 recovery plan throughout the european union, this proposal aims to incorporate them into a regulation. the proposal includes technical measures such as those related to the transfer and caging of live bluefin tuna (including measures related to the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate the quantities of bluefin tuna and the quantities of fish released), the catch reporting requirements and the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the commission's plan. i would even say that the commission is proposing measures that are too regressive. many years of poorly controlled fishing in the atlantic, the mediterranean and other seas have meant that many of the fish that are nutritious and essential to our ecosystems will soon be seen only in textbooks and museums. it's time to curb your appetites, and especially those of industry. at least so we have something to fish for in the future. and it's time to think about more environmentally friendly and responsible food sources.
in writing. ‒ mr president, i voted in favour of the report because bluefin tuna is the most important regulated species. in order to restore tuna stocks, a gradual reduction in the allowable catch is envisaged. the recommendations presented are intended to be applied uniformly throughout the eu, rather than to re-launch discussions on decisions already taken after lengthy negotiations. the proposal includes technical measures such as rules on the transport of live bluefin tuna, as well as requirements relating to the reporting of catches and the implementation of the regional observer programme. these provisions are worth supporting.
in writing. ‒ i voted on this report, in which the european parliament expresses its opinion on the annual report on the european union's competition policy. in its 2014 competition policy report, the commission underlined that this was the year of a new start for europe, as commission president juncker stated in his commission's mandate letter for the new term that competition policy should also make an appropriate contribution to the implementation of the agenda for jobs and growth, including in the areas of the digital single market, energy policy, financial services, industrial policy and the fight against tax avoidance. the new eu competition policy guidelines could be applied as from november 2014, and this raises expectations that in the future not only the current competition policy will be developed, but also the priorities will be revised. the european parliament has so far only participated in competition law matters by means of the consultation procedure. its influence, compared with that of the commission and the council, is therefore unfortunately limited. for this reason, parliament has repeatedly called for the application of the ordinary legislative procedure and competition law under the lisbon treaty. this seems necessary because, in the rapporteur's view, the commission, as a competition authority with strong enforcement powers, cannot simultaneously provide a legal basis in the form of guidelines and then be responsible for implementing its own guidelines and applying heavy financial penalties.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to review the eu financial services regulation. the financial and debt crisis that erupted in 2007 and 2008 required comprehensive action by european legislators and international standard-setting bodies. since the financial and debt crisis of 2007 and 2008, a number of legislative initiatives have been launched in the eu financial services sector to restore financial stability, strengthen customer protection and build on lessons learned from the crisis. this report assesses this legislative work, addresses shortcomings in financial services legislation and raises concerns. i agree that financial services legislation must take account of proportionality, which needs to be given more attention. full implementation of existing legislation and strong enforcement in the member states are also needed. it is important that financial stability and customer protection remain priorities for the legislator, with a greater emphasis on a consistent and risk-based approach.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because the financial and debt crisis of 2007 and 2008 required a comprehensive response from european legislators and international standard-setting bodies. since then, a number of legislative initiatives have been launched in the eu financial services sector to restore financial stability, strengthen customer protection and build on lessons learned from the crisis. a number of legislative acts have already been successfully implemented within the deadlines for their implementation and application, which have already passed or are about to pass. this own-initiative report is a first step in assessing this legislative work, addressing the identified weaknesses in financial services legislation and reporting on the issues of concern that have emerged, in particular due to the insufficient analysis of the impact of the individual legislative instruments and their interaction, as well as the overall impact of all legislation not yet fully assessed. the european parliament believes that the implementation of important new commission initiatives such as the investment package and the capital markets union will be better served by building on existing financial services regulation, which is effective and efficient.
in writing. ‒ the financial services regulation is a highly sensitive area requiring careful and deliberate action. at the same time, we must not forget that one of the european union's core objectives - to create an area of free movement of capital - has not yet been fully achieved. at least as long as there are different restrictions on capital movements within the eu. this document is an important step towards creating a single european area for the movement of capital. the only point i would like to make to him is that the document conveys the idea that consumer protection does not require a lot of information. quality is not enough. but who will set the standards for the quality of that information? that is not the case. will the financial institution itself do this? if so, do we believe that they will ensure a high quality of consumer information? it is true that this provision of the regulation is purely informative and does not have legal force. that is why i am voting against and i want to believe that consumer protection standards will not be lowered in any way. this is particularly true in a sensitive and potentially loss-making sector such as financial services.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to carry out a european survey on women entrepreneurs. the eu is still lagging behind in terms of entrepreneurship: in 2009, the eu-27 entrepreneurship rate was 12%, while china and the us were 27% and 21% respectively. women's entrepreneurship deserves particular attention in this context, as the eu is still not achieving equality in economic independence and the employment rate of women, at 59.6% in the eu-28 in 2014, is neither in line with the europe 2020 employment target of 75% nor close to the employment rate of men (70.1%). unfortunately, the first obstacle to entrepreneurship is the difficult balance between work and personal life. women are also less likely to use external financing, such as bank loans and supplier credit, and are therefore more likely to be more expensive to finance. this is partly because women have less knowledge of available financing options, are more cautious than men about taking economic risks, or lack the financial management experience of their male counterparts. despite the enormous complexity of the problem, it is necessary to address the issue of women entrepreneurs who are discriminated against by financial service providers when trying to obtain credit.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report by the european parliament on entrepreneurship and career opportunities for european women. the differences between men and women in terms of career prospects in business are still evident. in 2012, women accounted for only 31% of all self-employed citizens in the eu-28. women entrepreneurs are likely to start their own companies with less experience than men. women tend to choose sectors related to human health and social work or education when starting their businesses, while men tend to work in construction, transport and ict sector groups. given that most of the latter sectors have a higher rate of entrepreneurship and all have a higher economic added value, it is not surprising that female entrepreneurs earned 6% less than men in 2012. in addition, their activity levels remain lower than those of men: 23% of women and 30% of men are employed in the eu-28. european women seem to choose entrepreneurship for other reasons as well. women often say they are forced to do this because entrepreneurship allows them to combine work and caring responsibilities, such as childcare or care of the elderly, and provides more opportunities to work at home.
in writing. ‒ the i want to point out that this question is not as one-sided as it may appear. i fully agree that more female entrepreneurship would make a significant contribution to our collective aim of making europe more competitive. on the other hand, why are we only talking about entrepreneurship? not everyone has the desire or ability to develop their own business, do they? many good and honest people do fine work for hire in public administration or in non-governmental organizations. and this is not a business. and the skills or abilities required are different. however, working in public administration or in non-governmental organisations also contributes to a better europe. i support this report, but i would like to point out that it is not in the right format. we should not just talk about women entrepreneurs. we need to talk about their greater participation in the labor market, in the aggregate, in the labor market, which includes both business and the public and the non-governmental sectors.

in writing. ‒ the commission has presented a final set of procedural rights, including three proposals for directives to strengthen the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings. these three directives will allow the completion of the existing eu legal framework relating to the right of defence of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings throughout the european union. these are the main measures to ensure that a case is heard fairly throughout the european union and that the rights of the defence are fully respected. the presumption of innocence is a fundamental right and an essential principle for preventing arbitrariness and any abuse in criminal proceedings. this proposal emphasises the need to refer to the european convention on human rights, the eu charter of fundamental rights, the international covenant on civil and political rights and the universal declaration of human rights. i also support the proposals to clarify the scope of the directive: the persons to whom it applies, the period of application and its material scope.

in writing. ‒ the since 1989, the placing of personal protective equipment on the eu market has been fully harmonised under council directive 89/686/eec. for the past 25 years, this directive has ensured the functioning of the single market. nevertheless, the existing legislation on personal protective equipment needs to be updated in line with the new legislative framework (nlf), which is a set of measures to rationalise and simplify the rules on goods in the single market. given the complexity and duplication of the current regulatory requirements, this regulation clarifies the role of economic operators, strengthens cooperation between operators and introduces common definitions. the powers of market surveillance authorities to monitor and return unsafe goods placed on the common market should also be clarified.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to update the personal protective equipment directive, which has been in force for the last 25 years. while the current legislative requirements are complex and duplicative, this regulation clarifies the role of economic operators, strengthens cooperation between operators and introduces common definitions. the european parliament's ex-ante impact assessment of this proposal noted that the commission's decision to adapt the scope of the original directive was of concern. parliament does not consider that a major adjustment of scope is necessary, as the main objective of this draft proposal is to ensure the proper functioning and implementation of the regulatory framework rather than to achieve its objectives. therefore, in order to ensure legal clarity for operators in this sector, the rapporteur sought to have a scope similar to that of the original directive. in order to ensure the swift conclusion of the negotiations on this document, parliament considers that it is necessary to accept the majority of the council's proposals for aligning the proposal with the new legal framework.
in writing. ‒ the since the scope and essential health and safety requirements and the conformity assessment procedures have to be uniform in all member states, they should be introduced by the method proposed in the report. directive 89/686/eec should therefore be replaced by a regulation, which would be an appropriate legal instrument to help establish clear and detailed provisions which do not give rise to different interpretations by the member states. our priority as parliament was to propose amendments to ensure that the existing directive does not give rise to interpretations which could in any way affect the effectiveness and reliability of the law. the basic premise is that only highly effective measures can ensure the safety of workers, taking into account that accidents at work are very often caused not only by the failure to use safety measures but also by their incorrect use. any proposal that can improve the safety of citizens, and in particular workers, is worthy of a vote of support.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament supports the proposal for a regulation on gaseous fuel burning appliances, which aims to replace directive 2009/142/ec. this directive, which ensures the free movement of gas appliances, is an example of union harmonisation legislation. this directive makes a significant contribution to the establishment and functioning of the common market and harmonises the conditions under which appliances burning gaseous fuels falling within its scope are placed on the market and/or put into service in view of the risks to gas safety and the rational use of energy. directive 2009/142/ec lays down the essential requirements with which appliances burning gaseous fuels must comply in order to be placed on the eu market. the gas sector plays an important role in the european union's economy, with 476 000 people employed in the gas appliance sector alone. gas appliances cover a wide range of products, from portable stoves to boilers for large buildings, and there are currently 470 million gas appliances in the eu and more are being sold every year, with more than 30 million units sold.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to harmonise the conditions for the placing on the market of subsystems and safety components for cableway installations and to ensure the free movement of these products within the eu. all safety components and subsystems shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements set out in this regulation. as regards rolling stock, this regulation also provides for full harmonisation of the essential requirements with which they have to comply. this regulation repeals and replaces directive 2000/9/ec of 20 march 2000 on the installation of a passenger line on a road.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament supports the proposal for a regulation on cableway installations, which is a model of european union harmonisation legislation. the proposal aims to harmonise the conditions for the placing on the market of subsystems and safety components for cableway installations and to ensure the free movement of these products within the eu. all safety components and subsystems shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements set out in this regulation. as regards rolling stock, this regulation also provides for full harmonisation of the essential requirements with which they have to comply. the change of legal instrument from a directive to a regulation is in line with the overall political commitment to better regulation and simplification of the regulatory environment. the decision to make this amendment was taken in view of the need to ensure uniform implementation throughout the european union. since this regulation provides for full harmonisation, member states may not impose stricter or additional requirements in their legislation. however, member states will continue to have the right to regulate other aspects of cableway installations, such as land use, regional planning and environmental protection. in this respect, the choice of a regulation is welcome, as it will avoid unnecessary costs of transposition into national law and will introduce clear and detailed rules that will apply uniformly throughout the european union.
in writing. ‒ the i voted against the delegated act on the system of preferences for the common customs tariff. the commission is empowered to provide that a requesting country is granted a special incentive arrangement for sustainable development and good governance by including it in the list of countries benefiting from gsp+. the applicant country has to fulfil certain conditions in order to become a gsp+ country and this status is not granted automatically. the committee on the application of standards of the international labour organisation, in its report, listed the kyrgyz republic among the countries whose competent authorities have still not fulfilled the necessary conditions. the government of the kyrgyz republic did not participate in the discussions on the implementation of the relevant commitments of its country. the main shortcomings are: persistent and widespread torture and ill-treatment of detainees, persistent failure to carry out prompt, impartial and thorough investigations, failure to provide all basic legal guarantees to all detainees, in particular those subject to remand in custody, etc. as the monitoring bodies of the relevant conventions have identified significant deficiencies in relation to certain bst+ relevant conventions, i therefore accept the objection to the commission delegated regulation of 25 november 2015 applying the gsp scheme.
in writing. ‒ the vote rejected the following resolution in which the european parliament examines the commission's mandate to grant a special incentive for sustainable development and good governance to a requesting country, in this case kyrgyzstan, by including it on the list of beneficiary countries. the european parliament notes that the monitoring bodies of the relevant conventions have identified significant deficiencies in relation to certain relevant conventions and considers that these deficiencies constitute a serious breach that impedes the effective implementation of the relevant conventions. both the committee against torture, the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination and the committee on the rights of the child all identified violations of human rights and freedoms and various shortcomings in their reports.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of rejecting the ec decision on the sugar content of baby food as it did not take into account the global recommendations. although the world health organisation recommends that sugar should not provide more than 10% of the energy content of infant formula, the use and distribution of infant formulae containing up to 30% of the energy content of sugar is currently permitted in the eu. i agree that the sugar content of baby food should be significantly reduced, in line with the who recommendation. i agree that the labelling and distribution of processed baby foods should clearly indicate that these products are not suitable for infants under 6 months of age, as it is recommended that such infants be fed exclusively on breast milk. i also support calls for a ban on the use of genetically modified organisms and nanotechnologies in baby food.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution in which the european parliament examines the composition and information requirements for processed cereal-based foods and baby foods. the commission has not submitted to parliament and the council a report on infant formula as provided for in article 12 of regulation (eu) no 609/2013, which is a prerequisite for the development of national strategies to reduce childhood obesity. the european parliament considers that this regulation does not provide for sufficient measures to protect infants and young children from obesity and that the maximum sugar levels should be significantly reduced, taking into account the recommendations of the world health organisation (who). in addition, the general principle of strict intolerance to pesticides should apply, taking into account the high endocrine vulnerability of infants and young children. any derogation from the principle of total intolerance to pesticides should be clearly listed in the annex to the regulation, which should be updated regularly in order to keep the maximum levels lower in the light of new scientific evidence on the health effects of the active substances and their metabolites. the european parliament also proposes that the labelling and distribution provisions should be reconsidered in the light of the world health assembly (who) recommendations on foods for infants and young children.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal for amendments to the 1998 protocol on heavy metals to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. this convention aims to protect human health and the environment from air pollution. studies carried out between 1972 and 1977 have shown that air pollutants can travel several thousand kilometres before they sink, and this problem must be addressed at international level. the convention, signed in 1979, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field. it has helped to create a system for controlling and reducing the harmful effects of transboundary air pollutant transfers on human health and the environment. the 1998 aarhus protocol on heavy metals, which supplemented the convention, aims to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury into the atmosphere. it requires the parties to reduce their combined annual emissions of these three metals to levels below their 1990 levels. the aim is also to reduce emissions from industrial sources, combustion processes and waste incineration. i support the amendments contained in the proposal, which aim to ensure a higher level of protection of human health and the environment against transboundary air pollutant transfers.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it supports parliament's amendments to the 1998 protocol on heavy metals to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect human health and the environment from air pollution. several studies carried out between 1972 and 1977 showed that air pollutants can travel several thousand kilometres before they settle. the problem of air pollution must therefore be addressed at international level. the convention, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field. the convention established a framework for controlling and reducing the harmful effects of transboundary air pollutant releases on human health and the environment. the amended protocol provides in particular for stricter limit values for dust emissions from certain large stationary sources and for more flexible transitional arrangements. this amendment to the protocol is already implemented in existing eu legislation and will be further transposed by the adoption of a new directive setting updated national emission limits for certain atmospheric pollutants and providing for annual national emission inventories of pollutants (including lead, cadmium and mercury).

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it supports the amendments to the 1998 protocol on heavy metals to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect human health and the environment from air pollution. the effects of air pollution are not local, but are constantly being transported by the wind. to date, the convention has been supplemented by eight protocols covering: the financing scheme for monitoring and evaluation activities in europe; emissions of sulphur, nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds, transboundary pollution flows, heavy metals and persistent organic pollutants; specific national emission limits; and reduction targets for different substances. the protocols set stricter emission limit values and provide for management measures, encouraging a gradual shift in production away from the use of environmentally harmful substances such as mercury.
in writing. the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect human health and the environment from air pollution. the problem of air pollution must therefore be addressed at international level. the aim is to reduce emissions from industrial sources (iron and steel, non-ferrous metals), combustion processes (energy generation, road transport) and waste incineration. it sets emission limit values for specific large stationary sources and requires the parties to apply best available techniques (bat). parties are also required to establish and maintain inventories of pb, cd and hg emissions to ambient air, to phase out ethyl gasoline and to reduce mercury in alkaline batteries.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal for amendments to the 1998 protocol on heavy metals to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. this convention aims to protect human health and the environment from air pollution. studies carried out between 1972 and 1977 have shown that air pollutants can travel several thousand kilometres before they sink, and this problem must be addressed at international level. the convention, signed in 1979, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field. it has helped to create a system for controlling and reducing the harmful effects of transboundary air pollutant transfers on human health and the environment. the 1998 aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants, which supplemented the convention, aims to limit, reduce or eliminate the release, ingress and discharge into the environment of pops. parties shall ensure that operators of large stationary emission sources apply the best available techniques, that certain waste incineration plants comply with the emission limit values, etc. i support the amendments contained in the proposal, which aim to ensure a higher level of protection of human health and the environment against transboundary air pollutant transfers.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it supports the adoption by parliament of the 1998 protocol on the modification of the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution to the protocol on persistent organic pollutants. i voted in favour of this report because it supports parliament's amendments to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution and the 1998 protocol on heavy metals. the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect human health and the environment from air pollution. several studies carried out between 1972 and 1977 showed that air pollutants can travel several thousand kilometres before they settle. the problem of air pollution must therefore be addressed at international level. the convention, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field. the convention established a framework for controlling and reducing the harmful effects of transboundary air pollutant releases on human health and the environment.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it supports the amendments to the protocol on persistent organic pollutants to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution of 1979 and the protocol of 1998. the 1998 aarhus protocol was designed to limit, reduce or eliminate emissions of persistent organic pollutants. parties to the protocol are obliged to cease the production and use of substances harmful to the environment, to restrict the use of dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, hexachlorcyclohexanes and polychlorinated biphenyls, and to reduce their total annual emissions of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, dioxins and hexachlorobenzene. in december 2009, the text of the protocol was amended to include seven new substances. most of these amendments to the protocol have already been implemented by existing eu legislation and will be further transposed by the adoption of a new directive which will set emission limits for these substances. in this context, this document is an important step towards reducing pollution.
in writing. the problem of air pollution needs to be addressed at international level. parties to the protocol are obliged to cease production and use of the substances concerned, to restrict the use of dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, hexachlorcyclohexanes and polychlorinated biphenyls and to reduce their total annual emissions of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, dioxins/furans and hexachlorobenzene (hcbs). parties are also required to establish and maintain inventories of the quantities of certain pops emitted and to collect information on the production and sales of other pops covered by the protocol.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is the report by which parliament decided to waive the immunity of the polish member of the european parliament, mr robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz. on 13 august 2015, the prosecutor general of the republic of poland forwarded to the president of the parliament a request from the central road transport inspectorate for the prosecution of mr robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz, member of the european parliament, for the infringement of the 29 km/h speed limit in the town of sklarów, poland. the facts alleged against mr iwaszkiewicz constitute an infringement under the polish code of administrative offences. the european parliament applies its established principles to decide whether or not to waive the immunity of a member of parliament, one of which is that immunity is normally waived unless there is evidence of fumus persecutionis, i.e. there is a sufficiently serious and clear suspicion that the member concerned is being prosecuted for political reasons. it is apparent from the circumstances of the case that the alleged administrative irregularity and the subsequent administrative prosecution have nothing to do with the duties of mr iwaszkiewicz as a member of the european parliament and therefore there is no evidence of fumus persecutionis.
in writing. ‒ i support the decision to waive the immunity of robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz, due to the fact that in similar cases involving article 9 of protocol no. 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, parliamentary immunity is usually waived. this is especially the case when there is no evidence of political motivation behind the prosecution, which there does not seem to be here. as a result, i am in favour of the conclusion made by the committee of legal affairs to waive parliamentary immunity for mr iwaszkiewicz, and have the criminal proceedings begin.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is the decision of the parliament not to waive the immunity of florian philippot, member of the european parliament from france. florian philippot is accused of defaming a non-eu state, namely qatar, in his radio broadcasts of 9 january 2015 and his television broadcasts of 19 january 2015, in which he alleged that the state financed terrorism. article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union and article 26 of the constitution of the french republic provide that members of parliament may not be subject to civil or criminal liability for opinions expressed in the performance of their duties. the provisions of the french system which protect the representatives of the people in the exercise of their functions date from 1789 and are based on respect for the expression of the will of the people and the need for elected representatives in a democratic state to be able to exercise their powers freely and without fear of being sued or of being prevented from doing so by the executive or the judiciary. this absolute immunity of a member of the european parliament covers not only the opinion expressed by a member in official sessions of parliament but also the opinion expressed elsewhere, for example in the media, where there is a link between the opinion expressed and the duties of a member of parliament, and the expression of opinions on the foreign policy of the eu and non-member states in the public sphere is one of the duties of a member of the european parliament. the parliament therefore decided that the conditions for waiving florian philippot's immunity were not satisfied for that reason.
in writing. ‒ i support the committee's decision to uphold mr. philippot's parliamentary immunity. this is because his alleged offence is an opinion he stated regarding a non-member state, and according to both the european parliament and french law, opinions and expressions cannot be challenged or face the threat of legal action.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to tackle the problem of undeclared work. this proposal would allow eu ministries, trade unions and employers' associations to cooperate more closely in the fight against undeclared work. undeclared work is any paid activity which is legal in nature but is not declared to the relevant public authorities. it accounts for as much as 18% of the eu's gross domestic product. such activities have very negative consequences: exploitation of millions of workers across the union, low-quality work, unfair competition and losses to member states' budgets and social security systems. i agree that in order to successfully tackle the multifaceted problem of undeclared work, it is necessary first of all to consider objectively its true nature. i support the commitment to create an eu-wide cooperation platform that will allow representatives of all the union's member states, the european commission and the social partners trade unions and employers to meet twice a year. they will be able to share information and suggest ways to tackle undeclared work. working groups will also be set up to address specific problems related to such work.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is the report which parliament has endorsed on the european platform for combating unemployment. this platform will strengthen cooperation between member states' labour ministries, trade unions and employers' organisations in identifying best practices in tackling undeclared work in the eu. it is estimated that the number of people in the eu who are unemployed is growing at a rate of about one in every five. the latest eurofound surveys show that, first, the size and growth of the undeclared economy and, second, austerity policies, with drastic budget cuts, increasingly reduced regulation and the role of the state, are closely linked. the same studies show that the alternative approach, whereby public expenditure on labour market and social assistance measures is encouraged, is closely linked to the much smaller undeclared economy. the platform will be the place to collect and share reliable information on best practices and lingering problems, and to cooperate in defining and implementing effective enforcement and enabling measures.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the eu-moldova association agreement. it provides for a bilateral safeguard clause allowing the suspension of preferences in the event of a sudden increase in imports which would cause economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing country. the agreement also provides for a so-called anti-circumvention procedure, which provides for the possibility of re-establishing the mfn duty rate for imports of certain agricultural products from moldova in excess of the threshold and in the absence of a proper justification of their precise origin. the proposed regulation aims to ensure the fulfilment of moldova's obligations under the agreement in order to protect eu producers where necessary. i support the proposal to introduce a reporting obligation requiring the commission to submit an annual report to the legislative authorities on the application and implementation of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it adopted parliament's position on the regulation implementing the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention procedure providing for the temporary suspension of the tariff preferences for moldova under the association agreement. the association agreement with moldova, like most of our trade agreements, includes a bilateral safeguard clause. this measure allows the suspension of preferences in the event of an unexpectedly high increase in imports, which would cause economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing country. the agreement also provides for a so-called anti-circumvention procedure, which provides for the possibility of re-establishing the mfn duty rate for imports of certain agricultural products from moldova in excess of the threshold and in the absence of adequate justification of their exact origin. in order to incorporate into eu internal law the measure allowing for the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention procedure, a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is necessary. the adoption of the proposed regulation is necessary in order to ensure compliance with the obligations of moldova arising from the agreement, in order to protect eu producers where necessary.

for the verts/ale group this is a very timely question. it will be extremely difficult to emerge from the economic crisis and to ensure long-term sustainable economic growth and the well-being of all europeans unless we harness the potential of our cities and regions. the european union does not have the power to determine the internal cohesion of the member states, but the commission has developed open coordination mechanisms, and it is precisely the error of good practice that in many cases becomes the factor that drives change. i would ask the commission to promote the exchange of experience on good governance, in particular by emphasising good practice in involving local and regional authorities in decision-making. i would also like to urge the commission to develop a methodology to assess the effectiveness of the internal administrative structure of the member states. it should focus on the qualitative involvement of local and regional authorities in the decision-making process at national level and on the extent to which local and regional authorities have sufficient and own resources and powers to implement autonomous regional policies or to adapt national regional policy solutions to specific internal needs. the proposal for a partnership is very important, as genuine partnerships between central, local and regional authorities, communities and social partners are still very scarce. it is more formal, despite the fact that local authorities and communities are the closest to the people and are the most able to identify the most urgent needs and plan actions, especially in the light of regional disparities that are only deepening as migration flows, globalisation and climate change take their toll.
in writing. eu cohesion policy remains the main instrument of investment for the 2014-2020 programming period, covering all eu regions. it is also an opportunity to better start a bottom-up process to ensure sustainable economic growth, support job creation, entrepreneurship and innovation at the level of the local and regional economy, as well as to improve the quality of life of citizens, build solidarity and strengthen the development of the eu's regions. the erdf regulation provides that 5% of the erdf should be allocated to promoting integrated sustainable urban development actions and that the bodies at urban, subregional and local level responsible for the implementation of sustainable urban strategies should be responsible for actions, at least in relation to the selection of operations. i would therefore like to emphasise once again that strengthening the administrative capacity of local and regional authorities and reducing structural weaknesses are crucial both in the programming and implementation phases of the operational programmes and in order to achieve a higher level of use of the esi funds. i therefore urge the commission to ensure that local and regional authorities, their administrations and bodies are provided with capacity-building support to enable them to play their crucial role in the implementation of cohesion policy, especially when implementation tasks are delegated to lower-level administrations, in particular to city administrations.

in writing. a uk exit from the eu would not only be unprofitable for one half but also a threatening event in the context of the crises that are affecting the community today. i am therefore pleased that a compromise agreement was reached at the european council last week. eu leaders have shown that there is a common understanding of the threats and a willingness to compromise in response. this european unity and ability to talk together is needed today more than ever, because the eu as a global actor has a responsibility not only for the development of its members but also for the development of the world. but we must ensure that this agreement does not become the basis for the development of a two-speed europe. the uk's membership ensures a balanced system of checks and balances within the eu when it comes to the question of which direction, deepening or enlarging, the eu should take, a question which has been the subject of deep debate since the beginning of european integration. london brings the enthusiasts of unconditional integration back to reality by asking fundamental questions. britain also plays a role as a bridge to transatlantic cooperation - particularly important in today's fragile international environment. i would point out that the agreement reached, which is mutually satisfactory in principle, obliges the uk leaders to convince the eurosceptically disposed sections of the public that the alternative to leaving the eu would be a dangerous uncertainty not only for the community but also for britain itself.
madam president, the single market is actually the biggest and most successful achievement that we have in the european union, and we should be proud of it. in the last 50 years it has generated opportunities, created jobs and offered greater choice at lower prices for consumers. but the work is far from finished and a lot of challenges are still ahead. single market governance is a top priority, and the european semester is a wonderful tool for that. i strongly believe that the eu should use the momentum of the collaborative economy. the commission and member states should encourage the development of new business models by ensuring the best possible conditions for them to develop and thrive. the commission and member states should work better to enforce the mutual recognition principle as this is crucial for the better functioning of the single market. furthermore, the single market needs new market surveillance and product safety legislation at european level. i strongly encourage the commission to take the lead there.
the benefits of economic growth and job creation must first be felt by our people. yes, the recovery is on the rise, and we have to admit that: employment is up a little bit, unemployment is down. but, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to draw your attention to a major problem in our european union countries, namely child poverty. as many as 27% of children in the european community live in poverty. i therefore call on the commission and the member states to create a child guarantee, that is to say, a measure with a certain specific budget, under which our children could receive free health care, education, decent housing, adequate nutrition. secondly, i want to draw attention to the poverty of women. however, i would urge the commission and the member states to put forward specific recommendations and measures to reduce the gender pay and pension gap.
ladies and gentlemen, i would like to add a word of praise to mr rodriguez's report. this is the commission's message and i think it is fundamentally wrong to think that member states should be penalized for errors or shortcomings in cohesion management by restricting cohesion support to them or by imposing ex ante conditionality. i do not see a positive link between economic governance and cohesion policy. both issues are very important, but we cannot go down to a strictly instrumental approach, as the commission proposes. these issues must be addressed separately, rather than one condition being the other. i also regret that the rapporteurs have not succeeded in incorporating this provision in their report. in the area of cohesion policy, sanctions on member states not only undermine good governance but also hamper economic growth.
i thank the rapporteur, mr becker, for a good job, because we are indeed aiming to strengthen the eures platform with this regulation and make it a really effective tool for people interested in labour mobility in the european union. and one of the most important improvements is to increase transparency, by making it possible to review as many vacancies as possible in one place at a pan-european level. it is also important to seek to include apprentices and trainees in this network, but of course on the condition that they are covered by normal employment relationships. all jobseekers must therefore be given access to detailed information on the working conditions at the workplace. i am pleased that the negotiations on this regulation have succeeded in strengthening the role of the social partners in the network's activities, so that we have made it easier for both workers and employers to obtain the information they need for employment. it is also essential that the main services of the eures network are free of charge and thus more accessible to the jobseeker.
in writing. today we are talking about a very important topic: work. the conclusions drawn from the high unemployment rates in some european regions suggest that labour mobility in the eu should be strengthened in order to increase the employability of workers and to help employers to fill vacancies better and faster. member states should therefore set up national coordination centres to provide joint support and assistance to all organisations operating in their territory that support cooperation with relevant organisations in other member states, in particular neighbouring ones. such coordination centres should, in particular, be entrusted with the handling of complaints and problems relating to job vacancies and with the verification of compliance aspects relating to voluntary and fair labour mobility within the union. the increasing interdependence of labour markets calls for closer cooperation between employment services, particularly in border regions, in order to ensure the free movement of all workers within the union in accordance with the principles of voluntary and fair labour mobility. this should certainly be done throughout the union and in accordance with the treaties, without any discrimination. a common framework for cooperation between the member states and the commission should be established . this should be based on the pooling of all job offers from across the eu and the possibility for workers and employers to apply for jobs through a job placement agency. it is also necessary to define a common approach to the exchange of information and to the provision of personalised advisory services necessary to facilitate such cooperation.
in writing. the european ombudsman's task is to protect the rights of persons with disabilities and to ensure that the eu administration is aware of its responsibilities in respect of these rights. persons who consider that an eu institution is not complying with the provisions of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities have the right to complain to the ombudsman. in early 2014, the ombudsman's team was joined by a seconded national expert whose task is to help develop a work programme on disability issues and to find ways to better reach citizens and staff of the eu institutions and inform them of their rights and obligations under the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the european parliament supports the ombudsman in that the eu institutions should ensure that disabled people have access to their services and that they can access information and communication. parliament also called on the eu institutions to ensure that working environments are open, inclusive and accessible to people with disabilities, so that they can participate effectively and fully in political and public life. the ombudsman also meets regularly with members of the european parliament and officials of the institutions to discuss ways of improving the quality of administration, to emphasise the proper handling of complaints and to ensure appropriate follow-up to the ombudsman's recommendations and communications. the european parliament calls on the ombudsman to continue to support the european network of ombudsmen in order to better inform eu citizens about the division of competences between the european ombudsman, national and regional ombudsmen and parliament's committee on petitions.
vice-president of the commission.– madam president, i want to thank most sincerely all those who have taken the floor. very clearly this is an issue that is on top of our minds as a concern for many of us, and also very clearly there are certain points on which we have full agreement: firstly, that we ought to concentrate our efforts on making sure that the tobacco directive becomes effective by may 2019, as well as that the who protocol is ratified by at least 40 countries, so it can become effective at the earliest possible time which is 2022, no later. secondly, there is full agreement in this chamber and full agreement from the side of the commission that we ought to fight illegal smuggling of cigarettes. not only does that come from the companies covered by agreements, but especially the so-called ‘cheap whites’ that have taken the space that used to be taken by the companies. where there are clearly also differences in views is around what we do between now and 2019, and what we do between now and 2022. there have been very fair comments made that it has taken the commission time to complete the assessment. just listening to us in this chamber – the divergence of views, the difficulty of the questions that are being asked – this is why it has taken us so much time. we have promised to make sure that we involve all our services, including, in particular, our health service, and we have done it. now we have an assessment that we all have subscribed to, but it has taken time because the questions we are debating are not easy. so what do i take out of this discussion today? i take a recognition that we have to deliver on the issues where we have full agreement, and that we need to focus our efforts where it matters the most. and i also take under advisement the views that have been expressed on what we do between now and then, and i can tell you we will reflect on those very carefully. going back in history, parliament was very supportive of the signing of the agreements – for a reason, because at that time we had nothing. and now parliament is not so supportive – there are divergent views. why? because we have better tools to fight illegal smuggling. but we do not quite have them just yet, and this is what puts us in a debate that we have to integrate in our decision. i was asked a specific question – what information do we use? we use information on seizures from the 28 member states, provided to us on a daily basis. we also use data from euromonitor, and we are currently discussing with our health colleagues the carrying-out of a targeted study on the illicit tobacco market in the eu, with an eye to focusing attention on the ‘cheap whites’ and strengthening our fight against their smuggling. again i want to confirm that, on transparency, we have made the agreements available to parliament, and we will do all we can to promote more transparency in the future. again, thank you for the debate, and of course we will come back to you on this issue whenever you invite us to do so.
in writing. one of the four eu cooperation agreements with tobacco companies, the agreement with philip morris international, will expire in july 2016. under the agreements, tobacco manufacturers agreed to pay the eu and its member states $2.5 billion to settle outstanding cigarette smuggling claims. they also committed themselves to actively combating smuggling and counterfeiting of tobacco products. however, it is clear that there is a serious lack of evidence of the benefits of this partnership for the member states. those agreements do not contribute in any way to the reduction of the consumption of tobacco products. white cigarettes, which have no labels, are also common in europe. this shows that the fight against smuggling is not effective, although the overall volume of cigarette smuggling seized has decreased. this is, by the way, the only significant factor, and the reasons for this can be very diverse, for example, better control of the member states. equally important, despite the dubious benefits of the agreements, there is a risk that the european commission will re-sign agreements with tobacco companies without parliament's opinion. if this were to happen, the commission would once again demonstrate that it does not want to ensure democratic decision-making processes.
the notifier. ladies and gentlemen, the 1965 hague convention establishes a framework for simplifying the exchange of documents between the countries of the european union, simplifying and facilitating judicial cooperation in cross-border and civil and commercial disputes, and thus the convention is proving useful. the convention is used by 25 countries of the european union. following the expression of the wishes of austria and malta to accede to the hague convention, following lengthy discussions in the council and the clarification of the court of human rights, the two member states are given the opportunity to accede to the convention. i therefore urge my colleague to support this recommendation and to allow austria and malta to accede to the hague convention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to allow austria and malta to accede to the hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system whereby documents may be served in another state party to the convention. of the 28 member states, the convention is already applied in 26 of them. the other two member states, austria and malta, have expressed their wish to join. malta has already deposited its instrument of accession to the convention but has prepared a declaration that its accession will not take effect until this decision is adopted. austria is awaiting this decision in order to complete the accession formalities. since the two member states concerned are interested in the application of a single procedure for the service of documents in cross-border relations with third countries, i support the proposal to allow austria and malta to accede to the convention.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this document because it gives parliament its support for the decision authorising austria, in the interests of the european union, to sign and ratify the 1965 hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters and authorising malta to accede to it. the 1965 hague convention establishes a framework under which documents may be served in another state party to the convention. it should be noted that this convention applies only to the cross-border service of documents in or received from third countries. for cross-border service of documents in the european union, regulation (ec) no 1393/2007 on the service in the member states of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters applies. the convention is currently applied in 26 of the 28 member states. the other two member states, austria and malta, have expressed their wish to join. international organisations shall not be admitted to accede to the convention. the eu has acquired exclusive external competence in this area with the adoption of eu legislation on crossborder service of documents. this means that the union must authorise the member states concerned to act on its behalf in order for them to accede to the convention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour on the draft council decision because member states cannot conclude the hague service convention without being authorised to do so. therefore, 24 member states had acceded to the hague service convention before the adoption of eu legislation. the remaining member states which have to be authorised to accede to the convention are austria and malta. these countries should sign it in the interest of the european union because it will make the process of authorisation in regards to the hague service convention much easier.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement between the european community and the republic of san marino on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the european union and san marino signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information with a view to enhancing international cooperation and compliance in the field of taxation on 8 december 2015. the agreement is an important step in the ongoing fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. it provides for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts between the eu and san marino for their residents as from 2017. the aim is to respond to cases where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital consisting of income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. the aim is also to ensure that information is exchanged not only on income such as interest and dividends, but also on account balances and income from the sale of financial assets. the new agreement will enable tax administrations in the member states and san marino to: identify correctly and clearly the taxpayers concerned; administer and enforce their tax laws in cross-border cases; assess the possibility of tax evasion; and avoid unnecessary further investigations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its support for the eu-republic of san marino agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. this agreement is an important step in the ongoing fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, and it builds on the 2004 agreement which ensured that san marino applied measures equivalent to those of the eu savings directive on taxation of income. the new agreement will allow the eu and san marino to exchange information on financial accounts held by their residents automatically from 2017. the aim is to respond to cases where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital consisting of income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. the agreement aims to ensure that san marino applies more stringent measures that are equivalent to the eu legal order, as improved in december 2014.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution on the opening of negotiations on a free trade agreement between the eu and tunisia. the eu and tunisia have a close and longstanding relationship, as the eu is tunisia's largest trading partner and tunisia is the eu's 34th partner. this new partnership will open up opportunities for growth and economic convergence between tunisia and the eu. the partnership should also contribute to the political and democratic stabilisation of tunisia and the recovery of its economy, while also having a positive impact on consumer prices and employment. i support the calls for negotiators to reach an agreement that takes account of the significant economic differences between the two countries, to be flexible in these negotiations, to show a capacity to react quickly and to bear in mind that this agreement should benefit the economy and society of tunisia and the european union. the commission should ensure that these negotiations quickly deliver tangible benefits to the most important sectors of the eu and tunisian economies, as well as to relevant stakeholders, in particular micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. the agreement should also contribute to the development and diversification of tunisia's economy, which is currently focused on agriculture, reduce regional disparities and bring tangible benefits to all tunisians and europeans.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman for 2014. in 2014, the ombudsman opened 325 inquiries based on complaints and 17 inquiries on her own initiative, completed 387 inquiries based on complaints and 13 inquiries on her own initiative. the complaints were mainly lodged by individual citizens, companies, associations and other legal entities. in the cases which the ombudsman closed, he identified 39 instances of maladministration and submitted 12 draft recommendations. a draft recommendation shall be drawn up where the institution complained against is able to remedy the maladministration or where the maladministration is serious or of general scope. the european ombudsman works closely with his colleagues in the member states. this cooperation is carried out by the european network of ombudsmen, which brings together national and regional ombudsmen. in many cases, complaints that fall outside the ombudsman's remit can best be resolved by the members of the network, i.e. the ombudsmen of the member states or regions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the registering of pet animals across the eu member states. not only because illegal trade of animals poses serious risks to public health, or because it is a significant source of revenue for the mafia, but mostly because of the wellbeing of these animals. for this same reason i voted in favour of amendment four. this amendment recognises that poor socialisation and habituation are among the leading factors in the behavioural problems of pets, such as separation issues or fear of everyday objects, and pose a long-term threat to animal welfare. i voted in favour of both parts of recital g as well, since this would be an important step towards compulsory identification and registration of dogs and cats in an appropriate database, which will be linked to an eu database. this recital allows traceability of the animals to help protect their health and welfare, public health and improve consumer protection. i sincerely care for these animals and i believe that this registration will help protect them and their wellbeing.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to strengthen the fight against illegal trade in animals. the illegal trade often results in poor care and a higher risk of disease. as many as 70 percent of the new diseases that have infected humans in recent decades are of animal origin. the proposal aims to encourage eu countries to exchange data on the registration of dogs and cats. many eu countries already have mandatory systems for identifying and registering pet animals, but the information they collect varies. it is therefore essential to harmonise the databases for the registration of dogs and cats in all eu countries and eventually to include other pets. this will reduce the level of document fraud and illegal trade in animals, as well as allow the identification of the sources of animal disease outbreaks and a more effective response to animal abuse.

for the verts/ale group mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank mr marc tarabella (rapporteur) for his excellent work. i was the shadow rapporteur for the greens when i was preparing this report, and i have to say that although our views were not exactly in line with the rapporteur's at the beginning, we did manage to produce a really good document. what good is this document and does it deserve the european parliament's unconditional support? first, it sets out objectives for the development of good eating habits in pupils and guidelines for the good management of the programme. the new regulation has succeeded in extending the list of products for the purpose of developing healthy eating habits in schools. sometimes too much. i still can't figure out how you're going to eat olive oil or what healthy eating habits you're going to form by drinking chocolate milk. but let's leave it to the individual member states. more importantly, we have, perhaps for the first time, succeeded in putting in place a european union law that flavour enhancers such as monosodium glutamate are wrong. we have managed to foresee that european union funds will not be used to finance food products with these unhealthy additives. it is hard to believe, but it does not seem that such a ban has ever existed. we have also managed to improve the overall management of the support programme. the new document clarifies the criteria for allocating funds to the member states. member states will be able to use the support more flexibly. we have also successfully incorporated provisions to promote short supply chains. in addition to the crucial aspect of good governance, it provides for greater involvement of local and regional authorities in the process of programme design and implementation. this is very important because it is the local authorities that are usually better informed than the central authorities about the specific needs of the local population.
in writing.– i believe children will gain a better understanding of healthy nutrition and form healthy eating habits by implementation of this programme. people consume too little fruit and vegetables in the overwhelming majority of the member states and child obesity is a weighty problem. therefore, children need education on nutrition to reverse this trend. moreover, this aid scheme will benefit farmers in the european union. thus, i believe this scheme will benefit many, if not all, parties involved. at the very least, children will enjoy a healthy snack every week.
for the verts/ale group mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to take this opportunity to thank you for your work in this area and to thank the rapporteur for a well-written report. although the draft legislation in question is only a regulatory framework document, it duly reflects the main issues of animal health and disease prevention. we support the aims it sets to protect animals not only from disease but also from stress and pain. we support the system of categorisation of animal diseases and the professional knowledge requirements for animal breeders that it establishes. at the same time, i would urge my colleague to draw attention to the structural circumstances which can make even the best animal welfare efforts more effective. i'm talking about catastrophically low and continuing declines in livestock farmers' incomes, such as the declining incomes of dairy farmers and pig farmers, which are not allowing farmers to invest the necessary funds in the health and nutrition of their cattle. i have information that dairy cows in at least a few member states have been fed with poor quality feed for two years. this means that farmers simply cannot afford the necessary supplements, vitamins and medicines, and this, for economic reasons, creates the conditions for the spread of animal diseases. i would therefore urge my colleague to vote in favour of this report. at the same time, please remember that we cannot achieve animal health in the european union without addressing the economic reasons which prevent farmers from obtaining the necessary animal health products.
i was rapporteur for the 2010 report on the protection of the european union's financial interests, but since then fraud and irregularities have not decreased but increased, costing the european union over eur 3 billion in 2014. however, to date only a small proportion of the irregular payments has been recovered from the member states. as i have said on many occasions, the main problem remains that member states, when they receive large sums of money from the european union, are not obliged to provide detailed and comparable data on their use. it is therefore necessary for the commission to harmonise the principles for reporting fraud cases and to establish a clear reporting framework to enable member states to assess the implementation of the recommendations of olaf investigations and the penalties for non-compliance. this situation cannot be tolerated and the commission must take full responsibility for the recovery of european union funds unlawfully paid.

in writing. ‒ i believe that a common healthcare approach will be much more effective than two separate policies for animal welfare and human health. these two fields are closely interconnected – as can be seen from diseases such as mad cow disease, bird flu and swine fever. moreover, antibiotic resistance is a serious problem at present. resistance to existing antibiotics has increased by 67% per generation, but no new types of antibiotics are being produced. measures, such as this piece of legislation, must be taken to prevent such important medication from losing its effectiveness. additionally, i am pleased with the simplification of eu animal welfare policy introduced by this legislation. furthermore, this legislation will benefit animals: a matter close to my heart. inadequate care will no longer be covered up by the use of copious amounts of antibiotics.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to introduce new animal health rules to strengthen the fight against animal diseases such as avian influenza and african swine fever. the animal health rules combine and update almost 40 existing pieces of legislation in this area and, for the first time in history, establish the interdependence between animal and public health. it introduces mandatory registration of those involved in the trade, a clearer distribution of responsibilities between farmers, traders and veterinarians, and a greater focus on prevention. it also clarifies the role of farmers, traders, veterinarians and animal owners in the fight against the spread of diseases. i agree that the european commission should be given the power to react immediately to outbreaks of animal diseases that may have a significant impact on public health or agricultural production. it is also important to provide for the mandatory registration of persons involved in the trade in animals and to establish national databases on dogs, cats and other pets.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on communicable animal diseases. the communication from the commission to the european parliament and the council 'an action plan to combat antimicrobial resistance threats' highlights the preventive importance of the regulation on infectious animal diseases (animal health act) and the likely reduction of antibiotic use in animal treatment. in addition to the requirements of this regulation, member states are encouraged to commit to collecting relevant, comparable and sufficiently detailed data on the use of antimicrobials in animal treatment and to transmit those data to the commission in order to ensure a more prudent use of antimicrobials in animal treatment and thus contribute to the reduction of the risk of antimicrobial resistance. this regulation lays down rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases which may infect animals or humans, but does not contain any provisions specifically governing animal welfare, although animal health and welfare are linked. the union has a well-developed animal welfare acquis covering a wide range of animal species (broilers, laying hens, pigs and calves) and activities (breeding, slaughter, transport, research, etc.). these animal welfare laws will necessarily continue to apply. the commission is firmly committed to taking full account of animal welfare in accordance with article 13 of the treaty and within the limits set out therein, and to fully implementing and developing legislation in this field.
