in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to harmonise the consumer price indices. this proposal establishes a single legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house price indices (hicps) at union, national and sub-national levels. the hicp is a measure of inflation, used as a valuable input for the inflation-adjusted economic value (e.g. wages, rents, interest rates) and therefore a basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore necessary that those statistics are objective, impartial and comparable for all member states and for all product categories. the current regulation on the hicp was established in 1995, but new developments in consumer price statistics make it necessary to revise the existing rules in order to ensure maximum comparability for the main users of the hicp.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to adopt a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices. the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a single legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house price indices (hicps) at union, national and sub-national levels. hicp a measure of inflation used, inter alia, as a valuable input for the conversion of economic value (e.g. wages, rents, interest rates) to inflation and therefore as a basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore essential that those statistics are objective, impartial and comparable for all member states and for all product categories. the current regulation on the ccctb was drawn up in 1995. new developments in consumer price statistics require a review of the existing standards in order to ensure the greatest possible comparability for the main users of the cpi. the regulation also takes into account the innovation in eu decision-making introduced by the treaty of lisbon, which empowers the commission (eurostat) to adopt implementing measures (implementing acts) or legislative measures (delegated acts) to amend non-essential elements of the regulations. for this reason, the commission proposal should set out a number of actions to be taken by means of delegated acts, for example by establishing a methodology suitable for the establishment of harmonised indices for comparison between countries or by updating the weights of the sub-indices of the hicp.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of angelika mlinar’s report on gender mainstreaming. it is astounding that gender inequality still remains an issue in 2016. gender mainstreaming is a tool to effectively address this problem and empower more women by fairly including them in decision making processes. thus, we need to incorporate gender mainstreaming in the preparation, design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies at the european parliament. analysis shows that our system regarding gender equality is still fragmented and inefficient – i believe that european parliament has the obligation to set a good example in this regard.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal on the integration of the gender dimension into the work of the european parliament. gender mainstreaming means integrating the gender perspective into the formulation, design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, regulatory measures and spending programmes in order to promote equality between women and men and to combat discrimination. in 2009, a network of meps responsible for gender mainstreaming in ep committees and an additional network at staff level were established. the members of this network shall hold regular meetings and exchange information on documents held by the members of the network and share best practices. the european parliament has gradually established a structure for gender mainstreaming. the evaluation of the work of each individual institution is positive, but the overall picture is not uniform. i support the proposals to strengthen the current structure of gender mainstreaming and to make it more effective and efficient, including through the creation of a strong interinstitutional network. it is also important to promote closer cooperation with national parliaments and to exchange views on a regular basis in order to further develop best practices in order to make progress on gender mainstreaming.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines the way in which the gender dimension is integrated into the work of the european parliament, and the documents adopted. gender mainstreaming has been adopted internationally as a strategy for achieving gender equality. in practice, gender mainstreaming means integrating the gender perspective into the design, development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, regulatory measures and spending programmes in order to promote equality between women and men and to combat discrimination. gender mainstreaming has a twofold dimension: it requires both the integration of gender into different policy areas and the resolution of the issue of the representation of women and men in a given policy area. both gender representation and gender-based content should be taken into account at all stages of policy-making. while numbers are important, it is also important to consider how the gender dimension relates to the content of policy instruments in order to better understand how women and men can better benefit from them. a gender-based policy ensures that the needs of all citizens - women and men - are equally met. however, structural gender inequalities remain entrenched in our society. even if women and men are treated equally in law, women still do not have equal access to and control over resources and assets. the current situation therefore shows that gender-based policy content is an essential part of a proper gender equality strategy.
in writing. ‒ i support the promotion of gender mainstreaming in the eu, because achieving gender equality is central to the protection of human rights, the functioning of democracy, respect for the rule of law, and economic growth, social inclusion and sustainability. unfortunately, we have not made as much progress on this front as we should have, and that needs to change. there should be more gender equality regarding decision-making positions and committee influence, and gender equality should be emphasised in all policies that the eu adopts.

in writing. ‒ i support the proposal to integrate the gender dimension into the work of the european parliament. gender mainstreaming has a double benefit: it not only ensures equal opportunities but also provides an example of good practice for other institutions and member states. i would like to emphasise that, although the participation statistics are the same, it would not always be a bad idea to focus on the gender dimension in the content of policy measures, to make the most of the opportunities it provides, while not overstepping the bounds of the equality criteria.

in writing. this proposal for a directive on procedural safeguards for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings is a very important piece of legislation that will regulate the rules across the european union on the rights of children involved in criminal proceedings. despite the abundance of international legal instruments in this area, there is no definition of what constitutes a fair trial for a child and courts must therefore act on the basis of partial and fragmentary law. the european commission estimates that more than one million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu each year - 12% of all those involved in criminal proceedings in the same territory. in addition to the large number of cases, there are also major differences in the treatment of children facing criminal proceedings in the member states. studies at european level show that the rights of children are currently not sufficiently guaranteed at all stages of the criminal proceedings within the union and that the european court of human rights has on many occasions delivered judgments to the detriment of the member states. furthermore, this proposal for a directive is part of the eu's agenda on the rights of the child and aims to promote the rights of the child in the light of other measures, in particular the guidelines of the committee of ministers of the council of europe on child-friendly justice, bearing in mind that such measures do not have the binding force of eu law and therefore the guarantees provided for in them do not apply fully and uniformly in the member states.
in writing. today's debate touches on a very important human rights issue, which is related to the legal protection of children. their problems cannot be left to them alone, institutional solutions must be found at union level to formally harmonise the legal approach in all member states. this is an important topic, as the european commission estimates that more than one million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu each year. the large disparities in the treatment of children facing criminal proceedings in the member states are a cause for concern, demonstrating the inadequacy of the legal protection of minors in the eu. in the case of a crime involving children, children must be placed under legal aid and guardianship immediately after their arrest. all information provided to them should be provided in a manner appropriate to their age and maturity. and, most importantly, a language that they understand, regardless of their nationality or place of residence, without any discrimination on the basis of language. member states must ensure that children are treated with care and diligence in all cases. criminal proceedings involving children should be heard in their absence and, whenever possible, with the knowledge and participation of their parents. it should be borne in mind that the proposed provisions should complement the directive on the rights of the child, as the fair trial of a child has not yet been defined. this is why this problem is of particular importance.

in writing. in considering whether the eu-turkey agreement will really help to turn uncontrolled migration into controlled one, i see too many challenges for now. since the start of the intensive eu-turkey negotiations, one of the main demands on turkey has been to stop the network of illegal migrant movements. but so far, we see no serious action from ankara in this regard: although the flow of migration across the aegean sea was lower at the beginning of the year than at the same time in 2015, a new wave of migrants is forecast as the weather warms up and up to 100,000 new arrivals are expected by the end of march. with the war raging in syria and russia dictating the terms and creating conflict on principle, the flow of refugees into turkey is not diminishing - there are already some 2.7 million refugees and migrants in turkey. perhaps this is what ankara sees as the reason for not closing the road to europe? the lack of a recipe for welcoming those already in europe today raises questions about the commitment to accepting one refugee for every illegal migrant returned to turkey. these are the new hundreds of thousands of asylum seekers. europe promises turkey a lot: visa-free travel, a huge financial injection, the opening of new chapters of negotiations on eu membership, even though the situation of civil rights and freedoms in turkey is deteriorating. but today, i doubt that ankara will pay the appropriate tribute, because so far it looks more like a clever move to use the migration crisis to push the frozen turkish integration with the eu.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to establish an adequately structured catalogue of the rights of children who are suspects or accused in criminal proceedings, providing for a structured set of minimum and interrelated standards adapted to the specific needs of children at all stages of the process. this proposal for a directive aims to protect the rights of the child. according to the european commission, more than one million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu every year - 12% of all those involved in criminal proceedings in the same territory. the current situation in the union is characterised by a lack of adequate protection of children's rights at all stages of criminal proceedings. the right of the child to a fair hearing has not yet been defined, and courts must operate on the basis of partial and fragmentary law. at present, only six member states have prosecutors' offices specialising in children's cases, and nine member states do not even have specialised courts for children's cases. i agree with the suggestions that it is necessary to ensure the mandatory right to consult a lawyer, which is closely linked to the right to free legal aid, the right to individual assessment. mandatory specific training for judges, law enforcement and prison staff working with children must also be ensured.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to adopt a directive of the european parliament and of the council on procedural safeguards for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. the stockholm programme stressed the importance of the rights of individuals in criminal proceedings. the need to ensure, through the application of common minimum standards, the effective exercise by persons under 18 years of age of a sufficiently uniform right to a fair trial at all stages of criminal proceedings is linked to the objective of facilitating the mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions in criminal matters and ensuring the smooth functioning of the european area of justice. the european commission estimates that more than one million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu each year - 12% of all those involved in criminal proceedings in the same territory. in addition, there are significant differences in the treatment of children facing criminal proceedings in the member states. this proposal for a directive is part of the eu's agenda on the rights of the child and aims to promote the rights of the child in the light of other measures, in particular the guidelines of the committee of ministers of the council of europe on child-friendly justice, bearing in mind that such measures do not have the binding force of union law and therefore the guarantees provided for therein do not apply fully and uniformly in the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. there must be set minimum legal procedures on this matter. according to the commission’s estimates, more than 1 million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu each year. eu research shows that, at present, children’s rights are not being sufficiently protected at the various stages in criminal proceedings in the eu.
in writing. ‒ children are a particularly vulnerable part of society. children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings should be provided with the conditions to prevent the repetition of the offence and the possibility of reintegration into society. this decision establishes the minimum procedural rights and protection of such children. the aim is to establish the minimum standards necessary to enhance mutual trust and cooperation in criminal matters between eu member states.
in writing. ‒ according to the european commission, more than one million children are involved in criminal proceedings in the eu every year. there are significant differences in the treatment of children facing criminal proceedings in the member states. it is clear from various sources that children's rights are not sufficiently protected at present, and i therefore support the proposals set out. i also believe that member states should provide specific training for judges, law enforcement and prison staff who work with children.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. all member states are obliged to respect human rights and to ensure their proper implementation. a common eu catalogue of the rights of children who are suspects or accused in criminal proceedings should be applied, adapted to the specific needs of children at all stages of the proceedings and ensuring a fair trial for the child. in particular, suspected or accused children should make full use of their right to understand and follow the proceedings and their right to a fair trial. i think it is appropriate to extend the scope of the directive to include young people who have reached the age of 18 but have not yet reached the age of 21 at the time of the offence committed before that age. it is also essential to ensure that the restriction of a child's liberty is only applied as a measure of last resort. the courts should, as far as possible, endeavour to impose this penalty only where it is unavoidable and provide specific and detailed reasons for that decision. in each case, respect for the human dignity and rights of the child in custody must be ensured, taking due account of the child's personality and the particular circumstances in which he or she committed the offence. particular attention shall be paid to the prevention of child crime and the promotion of social integration.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to adopt a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on veterinary medicinal products. the aim of this draft regulation is to regulate the authorisation, manufacture, marketing, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products throughout their shelf life and the pharmacovigilance process applicable to them. it was concluded that a specific regulatory framework adapted to the specificities of the veterinary sector is necessary. the current legal framework has raised problems such as the shortage of veterinary medicines (especially in small markets), the administrative burden of regulation, the functioning of the internal market and, of course, the phenomenon of antibiotic resistance. the commission would like to establish a list of very important antibiotics for human use only. the european parliament supports this idea, provided that the list is based on sound scientific criteria. the european medicines agency has excellent guidance on this and it should be followed. finally, contrary to what the commission proposes, the online marketing of antibiotics (and of prescription veterinary products in general) should be banned because it poses a serious risk to public health. the commission also proposes to simplify the use of medicines for human use sold without a marketing authorisation for animal treatment. the text leaves the responsibility for such use to veterinarians. parliament does not question the responsibility of veterinarians but calls for this possibility to be better defined, clarifying that the use of medicinal products for human use should be considered only as a last resort when there are no better alternatives.

in writing. ‒ i voted on the ec proposal for a regulation on veterinary medicinal products. the purpose of this legislation is to regulate the authorisation, manufacture, marketing, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products and to simplify the use of medicinal products for human use marketed without a marketing authorisation for the treatment of animals.
in writing. ‒ the eu must have a common legal framework to adequately protect public health, animal health and the environment and ensure food safety. the new legal framework must be proportionate and adapted to the specificities of the veterinary sector. it should be noted that the veterinary and human medicine sectors have very different needs in relation to medicinal products. therefore, a different regulatory mechanism should also apply. in view of the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance, it is necessary to address the public health risk associated with antimicrobial resistance as a matter of urgency. the development of new medicinal products for the treatment and prevention of animal diseases must be encouraged. an effectively functioning common market for veterinary medicinal products in the eu should be established, which would increase the availability of veterinary medicinal products, foster competitiveness and innovation and reduce administrative burden.

in writing. ‒ as a member of the committee on agriculture and rural development, i supported this report because it was long overdue for a change to be made. the european commission's draft regulation on veterinary medicinal products amends the provisions on these products. this document aims to regulate the authorisation, manufacture, marketing, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products throughout their shelf life, as well as the pharmacovigilance process for them. and pharmaceutical safety is paramount, because the final consumer of agricultural products is always a human being. this should be borne in mind whenever the law is amended. there is every indication that the new provisions will improve access to veterinary medicinal products and reduce the administrative burden, in particular as regards pharmacovigilance.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to repeal directive 2001/82/ec on veterinary medicinal products and to amend regulation no 726/2004 laying down community procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use and establishing a european medicines agency, in order to take account of the fact that the centralised authorisation of veterinary medicinal products is different from the authorisation of similar medicinal products for human use.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use. in september 2014, following an assessment of the functioning of the internal market in this sector, the commission published a proposal that the rules applicable to veterinary medicinal products should be merged into a single regulation on veterinary medicinal products, repealing and replacing the provisions of directive 2001/82/ec establishing a community code on veterinary medicinal products and amending the provisions of regulation (ec) no 726/2004 in order to remove any reference to veterinary medicinal products and thus to fully separate the provisions on veterinary medicinal products from those on medicinal products for human use. the european parliament broadly supports this proposal and welcomes the aim of aligning the provisions of the regulation with those of the treaty of lisbon. parliament welcomes the proposal to separate marketing authorisations for veterinary medicinal products from those for human medicinal products in order to take account of the specific needs of the veterinary sector. however, some aspects of this proposal still need to be improved and a cross-reference to the new veterinary medicines regulation and a clear indication of the role of the european medicines agency in the issuing and supervision of veterinary medicines under the centralised procedure are needed.

for the verts/ale group it is no secret that the pigmeat sector is in a deep crisis, as is the dairy sector and others. today, the price of pork is the lowest it has been in a decade. it decreased by an average of 13% per year. of course, the price in the shops is going down much more slowly, if at all. we all know that many pig farms have taken out loans to modernise their production and to meet animal welfare and environmental requirements. the low buying-in prices therefore raise the question: can pig farming survive in europe? what is the reason for this? the reason is twofold. on the one hand, there has been an increase in the world's supply of pigmeat. on the other hand, there is a need for costly animal welfare measures in europe. the unfairness of traders and the outbreak of african swine fever are not the least of these factors. what can we do? let us start with the harmonisation of international competition conditions. why do we force our farmers to adhere to animal welfare standards, but allow the import of meat at a quarter the price from countries like the united states or brazil that have almost no animal welfare standards? we also know that the beef animals are fed gm food. i call on the commission to take measures to restrict meat imports from third countries which apply lower animal welfare standards than the european ones. it would be even better if the commission took real action and proposed the introduction of high global standards of animal welfare at the level of the world trade organisation. secondly, we must take measures to ensure that the value added is distributed fairly, and we must limit the freedom of the traders to manipulate the prices on the shelves. thirdly, i would remind you that farmers are very much looking forward to real export incentives. i am referring in particular to the export guarantee scheme. and last but not least, the african swine fever. this disease, which is present in some member states, including my country lithuania, is damaging the reputation of eu pigmeat and is restricting export opportunities. the lithuanian authorities have succeeded in stopping the spread of this disease, but farmers suffer significant losses due to unfair commercial practices related to it, whereby buyers offer a very low price for healthy pigs raised on farms even in a semi-safe zone iii. (the president agreed to answer the question put by the person who raised the blue card (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure)).
answer to the question posed by the blue card. thank you very much for asking. that's actually a very good question. i said in my speech that european standards are high enough and it should not be the case that imports from other countries are of much lower standards, thus lowering prices and our pigmeat market cannot compete and thus farmers get low purchase prices and some people eat the bad product that is imported.
thank you, chairman. the european commission is not committed to making changes on glyphosate, and the role of the parliament is therefore particularly important. the commission's actions show that it believes that there are no problems with glyphosate, even before the scandals that have arisen in europe over german beer, let alone the scientific studies on the possible harm of glyphosate to the human body. on the other hand, it would of course be premature to ban glyphosate altogether. today, agriculture is already in crisis, with grain prices at historic lows. the ban on glyphosate would put farmers in an enviable position, and the most rational thing to do today would be to extend its use for a couple of years and to tighten the rules on its use, considering that it is not always safe to spray the fields with glyphosate, for example, before harvesting. it is therefore rational to invest time and money in the search for alternatives of similar quality and in the appropriate training of farmers. thank you. thank you.

in writing. mr president, the report touches on the very important issue of migration, which has become a problem for all the member states of the european union. frontex data indicating that 1.83 million people were apprehended in 2015 trying to cross eu borders illegally is alarming and requires action by the european union institutions. therefore, several important issues related to migration need to be addressed. first, let us not forget that the influx of refugees is being exploited by smugglers, by people-smugglers. it is good that the report raises the need to combat this phenomenon at international level in order to dismantle the networks of traffickers and prevent the smuggling of migrants. secondly, the european union must manage the protection of its external borders effectively and implement a transparent and uniform visa policy in all eu countries. cooperation with third countries is also of strategic importance in order to avoid the root causes of migration. and above all, let us remember that when we create a new legal framework for migration, we must first of all remember to ensure the safety of our citizens. all these activities must be supported by a proportionate and appropriate financial contribution allocated to the member states in order to enable them to implement safeguard mechanisms as quickly as possible. in conclusion, i would like to stress that our main task should be to ensure consistency in decision-making, which is lacking today in the field of migration.

in writing. ‒ the i voted on this report, in which the consultative working party unanimously decided that there are no substantive changes to this commission proposal other than those indicated as substantive changes. the consultative working party also found that, as regards the codification of the unchanged provisions of the previous act and the abovementioned substantive amendments, the proposal only seeks to codify the existing act without changing its substance. the commission proposal concerns the recasting, codification and presentation of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007, the so-called market access regulation governing imports of products originating in the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) states. this interim measure provides for the free movement of products originating in acp countries other than the least developed countries and for unrestricted access to the eu market without quotas, while preparing for the conclusion and application of the relevant economic partnership agreements in line with the wto framework as from 1 october 2016. there are currently 27 countries listed in annex i to the marketing authorisation regulation. the aim of codification is to ensure transparency and clarity and to simplify eu legislation, as the original act has been amended many times. the market access regulation has been amended nine times since its adoption in 2007, including the harmonisation of legislation following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon under the trade act omnibus ii and subsequent commission delegated regulations (see annex iii to the commission proposal). codification is therefore necessary to ensure that the regulation is clearer and more understandable.

in writing. – the agreement with greenland is the third most important for the eu in terms of its economic value. the ex-post and ex-ante evaluation of the current protocol, carried out on behalf of the european commission in the first half of 2014 and published in july 2014, delivers some key findings on the effectiveness of the current protocol, even though, as the european commission mentioned, it focused only on the first out of three years of implementation of the current protocol. the main conclusion of the report is that ‘it would be in the interest of both the eu and greenland to renew the protocol, the protocol provides important economic benefits to both parties, and helps ensure coherence with eu fishing activities elsewhere in the region.’ generally speaking, the fpa objectives have been achieved. important exceptions include: agreed quotas for offshore cod that are not consistent with ices advice, though noting that data collected from the fishery will be used to refine management of the stock; limited supply of fish landings to greenland; and the generation of limited employment in greenland.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the fisheries partnership agreement with denmark and greenland. it strengthens cooperation between the eu and two countries as well as promoting a partnership framework in which to develop a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the greenlandic fishing zone.
in writing. i agree to the conclusion of this protocol on a special fisheries partnership agreement with the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland. it should be noted that this agreement is economically beneficial for both parties. it will also strengthen cooperation between the european union and greenland. eu vessels will be granted access to the various fish stocks in greenland's exclusive economic zone and financial support will be provided for greenland's fisheries policy. in addition, a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible use of fisheries resources will be developed in the greenland fishing zone.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation because it deals with the essential issues. one of them is to protect the very sensitive and vulnerable flora and fauna of the arctic. this can be achieved by taking measures for sustainable use and conservation of resources. another important aspect the protocol provides for an annual financial contribution of eur 17 799 978, to be paid for the duration of the protocol, i.e. five years. this will ensure that eu vessels have access to the fish market in the greenland free trade area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal on certain aspects of the eu-macao air services agreement. the proposal replaces some provisions of the existing 15 bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. in 2002, the court of justice of the eu ruled that the traditional clauses in bilateral agreements between member states on the assignment of air services infringed eu law. on the basis of those articles, a third state may refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisation or the authorisation of an air carrier designated by a member state but not owned by the member state or its nationals and not effectively controlled by them.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which deals with the european union-macao agreement on certain aspects of air services. international air links between member states and third countries have traditionally been established by bilateral air services agreements. in 2002, the court of justice of the eu ruled that the traditional clauses in bilateral agreements between member states on the assignment of air services infringed eu law. on the basis of those articles, a third state may refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisation or the authorisation of an air carrier designated by a member state but not owned by the member state or its nationals and not effectively controlled by them. this was seen as discrimination against eu air carriers which are established in one member state but owned and controlled by another member state. this is contrary to article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees that nationals of member states who have exercised the right of establishment may enjoy in the member state in which they are established the same rights as the nationals of that member state. there are also other issues, such as competition, where compliance with eu law should be ensured by amending or supplementing existing bilateral agreements between member states and third countries on air services. the commission has thus agreed to an agreement replacing some of the provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of granting the consent for the agreement. it will allow compliance with eu law in terms of competition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, taking into account the judgment of the european court of justice and the conclusions of the transport council. the commission has agreed an agreement replacing some provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. they include prohibition of anti-competitive activities, equal treatment of carriers and their enforcement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to ensure that the standard rate cannot be lower than 15% from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2018. given that all member states currently apply a vat rate above 15%, the existing minimum standard rate of 15% also provides a degree of flexibility for member states, as it allows for vat reforms aimed at reducing the standard rate by broadening the vat base and limiting the possibility of applying preferential rates.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this communication, which amends the provision of directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax as regards the duration of the obligation to apply a minimum standard rate. the vat directive provides that the standard rate may not be less than 15% from 1 january 2011 to 31 december 2015. the minimum vat rates are based on the fact that the vat rate below the minimum threshold for crossborder and distance trade is still applied in the country of origin rather than in the country of destination. thus, in all member states, the application of the standard minimum tariff as currently in force provides useful safeguards for the proper functioning of the internal market. in this context, pending decisions on the final form of the system, the rapporteur of the european parliament agrees with the commission's proposal to maintain and apply retroactively the principle of a minimum standard rate of vat of 15% and to propose to extend the current rules for three years (until 31 december 2018).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that a minimum standard rate applied in all member states provides a useful safeguard to the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. i agree with the report. it should be noted that vat is one of the most important sources of taxes and revenue. it should be noted that in countries where vat is lower, consumption is higher, which also determines the state of the economy. i think it is appropriate to maintain and apply retroactively the principle of a minimum standard vat rate of 15%. i support the proposal to extend the current rules for a further three years until 31 december 2018. in that case, member states will continue to be able to apply the vat rate they deem appropriate, but it cannot be less than 15%. it should be noted that in many eu countries, the preferential vat is applied specifically to food and other consumer goods that are consumed in the most common way. the main reason why eu countries introduce reduced vat rates on food is to increase the purchasing power of the lowest income earners, because in their consumption basket, food represents the most important part of consumption expenditure.
in writing. - i voted for this report. the vat directive provides that the standard rate may not be less than 15% from 1 january 2011 to 31 december 2015. the commission wanted to extend this obligation until december 2017, while parliament wants to extend it for another year. it should be noted that even at present no eu country applies a vat rate of 15%. the lowest rate is in luxembourg, where it is 17%.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the issues of fisheries in the international agreement on marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction (united nations convention on the law of the sea). the european parliament's position is that maritime activities are changing and multiplying rapidly, and that the pressure to maintain and conserve marine biodiversity is therefore constantly increasing. in this context, parliament welcomes the continued work of the unga and the open-ended ad hoc informal working group. it is difficult to imagine an effective and well-coordinated measure for marine biodiversity that does not include one of the most important activities in the waters - fishing. this should also not lead to the amendment or withdrawal of the un fisheries agreement, which creates a framework that, as in the case of the eu, if properly applied, can improve the situation and produce results. in addition, the new agreement should include accountability measures for all actors involved, as it is difficult to predict real effectiveness and progress without such measures. the efforts to take into account the needs of developing countries, capacity building and information sharing should also be given priority. in this perspective, and with a view to sharing good practice, the eu should continue to play a leading role in the development and implementation of this new instrument.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the proposal for a regulation on zootechnical and genealogical requirements for trade in and imports into the european union of breeding animals and products of their genetic material. the european union (eu) zootechnical legislation aims to promote free trade in and facilitate the import of breeding animals and their genetic material within the european union, while ensuring that breeding programmes and the conservation of all genetic resources in europe are maintained. the production of productive animals, in particular those which have been identified as having valuable genetic characteristics, not only contributes to the economic and social development of the region in which those animals are produced, but is also one of the main factors for food security in the union. the european commission wanted to bring together all the directives relating to zootechnical legislation covering different species into a single legal act this regulation , thus completing the creation of a common market in this field. however, it should be stressed that the european commission's objective is not merely to consolidate and simplify legislation. it is in fact proposing to harmonise the animal breeding system, which will have a major impact on the european animal breeding sector. the rapporteur agrees with this general approach, but some aspects should be clarified or reassessed.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the situation of asylum in europe. the common european asylum system (ceas) comprises common rules governing a common asylum policy, a uniform status for asylum seekers and common asylum procedures across the union. the european parliament stresses that saving lives must be a top priority and that it is therefore of the utmost importance that search and rescue operations are adequately funded at eu and member state level. it also noted that the number of migrants arriving illegally by sea had increased, that the number of deaths at sea was rising dangerously and that better european responses remained necessary. parliament is of course calling for a clear distinction between persons smuggled into the european union and those brought to the eu for the purpose of trafficking in human beings, since the political responses must not only be properly integrated but also properly targeted. it notes that, in general, the criminal entry of migrants involves assisting a person to enter a member state illegally, whereas trafficking in human beings involves the recruitment, transport or reception of a person by violent, fraudulent or deceptive means with the aim of exploiting that person. the european parliament therefore considers that any holistic approach to migration must include measures to combat the activities of criminal networks involved in trafficking and smuggling.

in writing. ‒ i am in favour of solidarity between eu countries, but i cannot support a mandatory quota-based eu asylum policy. it is clear that a coercive element in such a sensitive issue, which concerns a wide range of areas, including those falling within the competence of eu member states, from education to national security, will not be effective. eu member states facing unprecedented migratory pressures need to be helped, but solidarity should not be seen as simply relocating refugees. other measures are equally important and particularly needed, such as improving the management of the southern eu border, assisting in the centres of migration influx, contributing to the capacity of and relevant agreements with the third countries concerned to manage migration flows, establishing refugee centres in the eu's neighbourhood and addressing the direct causes of migration.

in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the annual reports on the application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality for 2012-13. the principles of proportionality and subsidiarity are at the heart of the european union's decision-making process. the exercise of eu competence should be based on the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. the proper application of these principles enhances the protection of rights at both national and transnational levels. in this context, the controls on the application of the principle of subsidiarity should be strengthened, as should the powers of national parliaments in the development of eu legislation. in particular, it is necessary to facilitate greater involvement of the positions, perspectives and other proposals of national parliaments in the political dialogue. in addition, taking into account requests from national parliaments, the deadlines for consulting national parliaments should be extended for the purpose of checks to be agreed between national parliaments and the commission in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. it is worth noting that the annual reports produced by the commission are somewhat sketchy, often lacking in a more detailed examination of how the principles of subsidiarity and, in particular, proportionality are being respected in eu policy-making.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to promote small-scale coastal fishing in areas dependent on fishing. coastal fishing is a very important form of fishing in the eu, providing high employment and being socially and environmentally sustainable. the 2013 cfp regulation emphasises the importance of economic growth in coastal areas. it provides preferential access for small-scale and traditional fishermen in the 12 nautical mile zone, the most sensitive area of eu waters. in order to facilitate the development of innovation, recognised shortcomings such as insufficient investment in science, lack of adequate data on the seas and oceans, insufficient funding, lack of private-public cooperation, etc., need to be addressed. in recent years, more has been invested in marine and ocean monitoring systems, but this is still not enough. the main problem is that the existing data cannot be used. the procedure for requesting and obtaining the appropriate authorisation to use data alone is time-consuming and requires additional resources. the main challenges facing the sector, namely the decline in employment and profitability in the sector and the fight against the displacement of the fisheries sector in developing regions, must therefore be addressed.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to introduce new rules for the application of the external aspects of the cfp, including fisheries agreements. in the 1980s, relatively few countries engaged in long-distance fishing far from their coastal waters (the eu, the soviet union, japan, the usa, and a few others on a smaller scale). now, three decades later, the situation has changed radically and there is intense competition for most species in all ocean regions. i agree that the best strategy to achieve the eu's objective of promoting sustainable fisheries is to use the eu's influence in the international arena to improve fisheries management and transparency standards, to encourage a race for higher rather than lower standards. it is necessary to achieve greater transparency in fishing activities, to apply a regional approach to fisheries management, to make serious political efforts by flag states and coastal states to combat iuu fishing and to improve fish supply in order to feed women in the fisheries sector.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the common agricultural policy (cap), including fisheries agreements. in the 1980s, when the cfp was just beginning, there were relatively few countries that engaged in long-distance fishing far from their coastal waters (the eu, the soviet union, japan, the usa, and a few others on a smaller scale). now, three decades later, the situation has changed radically and there is intense competition for most species in all ocean regions. among the increasingly important players are china, korea and taiwan, all of which have adopted aggressive policies to take advantage of rapidly dwindling resources. to varying degrees, these shipyards tend to operate with less stringent environmental, safety and social standards and benefit from high subsidies and often lower levels of taxation. many of these long-distance fishing countries fail to fulfil their obligations as flag, port and market states or even respect fundamental human rights, all of which give them a competitive economic advantage over eu vessels. it is clear that the best strategy to achieve the eu's objective of promoting sustainable fisheries is to use the eu's influence in the international arena to improve fisheries management and transparency standards, to encourage a race for higher rather than lower standards. the eu is still the world's largest market for fishery products, has one of the largest fleets flying its flag and is often ranked among the top three fishing operators in the world.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the eu’s best strategy for promoting sustainable fisheries is to enhance social and environmental standards, to better control its own external fleet and to use the eu’s leadership on the international scene to improve fisheries management.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. the communication sends an unambiguous message that the eu's objective of promoting sustainable fisheries requires the use of the eu's influence in the international arena to improve fisheries management and transparency standards, to encourage a race for higher, not lower, standards. this is also ensured by encouraging third countries, starting with those with which the eu negotiates sustainable fisheries partnership agreements, to develop a common regulatory framework for eu and non-eu entities in the fisheries, processing and marketing sectors. the report also calls on the commission to play an active role in promoting the idea that third countries publish the terms of agreements they sign with other states or private entities, including the identity, activities and catch data of vessels authorised to fish. this would ensure transparency and increase competition in the environmental aspects of fishing.
on behalf of the alde group.– madam president, all experts agree that, if escalated further, the nagorno-karabakh conflict could certainly become far more lethal and ruthless than it was two decades ago. those who ordered the recent escalations cannot hide from history, an unprecedented arms race by both sides in a conflict that has for a number of years been boosted by one major arms supplier: russia. blood money: billions of dollars is pouring into the russian budget. the vice-prime minister of russia has recently said the following about the russian arms supplies: ‘everything is according to contracts. both countries are strategic partners to us.’ for me, the question is what we, as the eu, should do in order to deal with the so-called ‘frozen conflict’ and the destructive dominance of russia in the region. have we, as the eu, ever asked for our legitimate place at the negotiating table that is supposed to deal with the conflict? indeed, the argument from 1994, when the minsk group was set up and the eu was not considered a global player and mediator, is no longer valid. let us go back to the negotiating table as a global player, let us play a role as a major negotiator and mediator in this conflict, and let us prove that the eastern partnership goals to support peace and stability next door are valid.
the question asked when the blue card is raised. madam president, i would like to ask about the problems encountered in the implementation of the commitments of the member states. lithuanian officials visited refugee camps in greece and italy, but hardly anyone wanted to go to lithuania. they were dominated by germany, the scandinavian countries, but not by the baltic countries at all. do you think that the refugees should be transported by force?
almost a month has passed since the governing council meeting, and the results are too brief to summarise, but sufficient to assess trends. the eu-turkey agreement has returned several hundred irregular migrants and several dozen syrian war refugees who have arrived legally in the eu from turkey. riots on the greek-macedonian border, the czech republic's principled stance against any migrant distribution quotas. the trends are not good, and if we have succeeded in limiting the growth of the problem, the problem itself is not being solved. we need to take much more decisive action. the external borders of the european union must be closed. there must be no illegal movement of migrants across the internal borders of the european union and quotas must be abolished as an unjustified decision. so that the problems of illegal migration in europe do not become a catalyst for economic problems, i would urge that attention be paid, that more attention be paid, to the plan of the president of the european commission, mr juncker, and that the institutions of the european union and the member states take concrete decisions on its implementation much sooner, because another economic crisis is by no means what we need most in this situation. and although the commission's intention to give member states more flexibility on vat rates is not part of this plan, i welcome this proposal, as stimulating consumption can be one of the effective measures against economic slowdown.
in writing. two crises - the refugee crisis and the agricultural crisis - were discussed in the council. i think they both have some connections. first, we must address the living conditions of refugees in temporary camps, which are often inhumane. on the other hand, we have a dairy surplus. europe has been buying butter and milk powder through intervention for some time now, and i think they could reach the camps. this would be a win-win for everyone, first of all, to ensure that the people in the camps have milk products, and secondly, to address the problem of surplus. i welcome the european commission's decision to provide milk to syrian children, but i do not agree with the fact that 30 million from the farmers' fund is being used to implement this programme. this would not be possible for the supply of dairy products to refugees.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution in which the european parliament states that the draft commission implementing regulation on the renewal of the active substance glyphosate does not ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment. glyphosate is a non-selective herbicide that kills all weeds. the concerns about the harmful effects of this substance on human health, including the possibility of cancer, have not been allayed. parliament called on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to withdraw the extension of the approval of glyphosate. instead of renewing the marketing authorisation for glyphosate for an unlimited period of 15 years, the european commission should rely on an independent assessment of the effects of this chemical and make public the data from the european food safety authority used for the assessment of glyphosate. it is necessary to ensure that the classification of glyphosate is revised in the light of scientific evidence of carcinogenicity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the european parliament takes the view that the draft commission implementing regulation on the renewal of the active substance glyphosate does not ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment. the european parliament asks the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft to the committee. parliament also calls on the commission not to extend the approval of glyphosate and to set a deadline for the establishment of a clear list of co-formulants that are not allowed to be used in plant protection products. it also calls on the commission to ensure urgently that the classification of glyphosate is reviewed on the basis of scientific evidence of carcinogenicity and that the potential endocrine disrupting properties are reviewed on the basis of scientific horizontal criteria for endocrine disrupting chemicals. in addition, the commission and efsa, taking into account the overriding public interest in disclosure, should publish without delay all the scientific evidence on which the favourable classification of glyphosate and the proposal for renewal of the approval were based. in addition, the commission should empower its food and veterinary office to test and monitor glyphosate residues in food and drink produced in the eu and in imported production.

in writing. the expiry date of the active substance glyphosate should not be extended. in particular, no scientific evidence has been provided that the substance does not present any unacceptable risk to human health, animal health or the environment. it should be noted that glyphosate is the main active ingredient used in many commercial herbicides. it is therefore essential that proper studies are carried out on its possible adverse effects on plants, animals and humans. it is of particular concern that the increase in glyphosate levels in the food chain and in the organisms themselves, both in animals and in humans, is increasing. in view of this, member states should restrict or prohibit the sale of glyphosate to non-professional users. i think that the commission should withdraw its draft implementing regulation and submit a new draft to the committee.

in writing. ‒ the i voted for this resolution because of the zika outbreak. zika virus is a new mosquito-borne virus whose largest outbreak has been reported in brazil, particularly in the northeast of brazil. according to the evaluation of the european centre for disease prevention and control, as there is no treatment and no vaccine for this disease, protection is currently based on personal protective equipment. it is therefore essential to develop communication plans, adapting them to the most appropriate scale, and to raise awareness among the population and encourage appropriate behaviour to prevent mosquito bites. the commission has decided to allocate eur 10 million for scientific research into the zika virus. i support calls on the commission to ensure that, where eu public funds are used for research, the results of that research are not subject to intellectual property rights and that patients are guaranteed affordable products produced using the results of that research. the commission should propose specific measures for the regions of europe where zika virus is already present, in order to prevent all transmission routes in those regions and to provide support to the infected persons.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution on the zika outbreak. zika virus is transmitted to humans through the bite of infected aedes mosquitoes, and in tropical regions, most commonly through the bite of aedes aegypti mosquitoes, the same species of mosquitoes that spread dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever. according to an assessment by the european centre for disease prevention and control, in the absence of a treatment and vaccine for the disease, and because mosquitoes that spread the virus bite both indoors and outdoors, mainly during the day, the current protection is based on personal protective measures, such as wearing permethrin-treated long sleeves and long trousers (especially at the time when mosquitoes that spread zika virus are most active) and sleeping or resting in mosquito-net rooms or rooms with air-conditioning, or using mosquito nets. parliament called on the commission to draw up an action plan to stop the spread of the virus in europe and to assist member states and third countries in combating the epidemic in the regions where the outbreak is most intense (in particular the caribbean, central america and south america). parliament called on the member states to increase the knowledge of doctors and clinics specialising in the treatment of travellers about the evolution of the zika virus epidemic and the control of transmission of the infection by the authorities in the affected areas, so that they could include zika virus infection in the differential diagnosis of the population and travellers from those areas.

in writing. the rapid development of information technology has led to a much larger footprint in the virtual space than we are likely to think. we voluntarily agree to the transfer of personal data by registering on various portals, uploading photos and location on social networks. it is therefore paradoxical that, as citizens increasingly share their private information publicly, left-wing parties have for years blocked a crucial initiative to collect data on people travelling to the eu in order to ensure the safety of european citizens. it is clear that in the midst of the crises that are gripping europe, it is no longer possible to reconcile the openness and security that have been cultivated for many years. therefore, while privacy is an important value to be protected, it should not become a pretext for inaction in addressing the essential problems arising from a lack of interdisciplinary or cross-border coordination . unfortunately, it took the paris and brussels massacres for some groups in parliament to understand that defending human rights starts with creating a safe environment. if we turn to a society of fear, it will only further strengthen the resolve and confidence of the groups that seek to destroy western civilization in the integrity of their goals. i therefore support the consistent position of the group of the european people's party that the creation of a passenger database will make the fight against terrorism and organised crime in europe more effective.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the recommendation for a council position with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data. since directive 95/46/ec on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, much has changed in the field of data protection, in particular with the improvement of technology, the collection and processing of more personal data, including for law enforcement purposes, the application of a heterogeneous set of data protection rules, and the globalisation of markets and cooperation. moreover, the directive has not been able to achieve adequate harmonisation, as the provisions of this document are implemented differently in the member states. in this context, it has become more difficult for individuals (data subjects) to exercise their right to data protection. finally, this failure hinders the development of the single market between companies (who control or process personal data, data controllers) and individuals facing different data protection requirements. the european parliament welcomes the proposed transfer of the notification requirements to data protection authorities to the practical accountability and corporate data protection officers. the proposed regulation could be simplified by combining the right to information with the documentary requirements, since they are essentially two sides of the same coin. this will reduce the administrative burden for controllers and make it easier for individuals to understand and exercise their rights.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the council position with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, and on the free movement of such data. the purpose of the processing of personal data to serve the human being, i.e. the principles and rules for the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of their personal data should respect the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons, in particular the right to the protection of personal data, regardless of their nationality or place of residence. this should help to complete the creation of an area of freedom, security and justice. it should be noted that rapid technological development and globalisation are creating new challenges for the protection of personal data. the scale of data collection and exchange has increased substantially. technologies allow competent authorities to use personal data on an unprecedented scale in the course of their activities. it is therefore essential to ensure a uniform high level of protection of personal data in order to facilitate the exchange of personal data between the competent authorities of the member states in order to ensure effective judicial cooperation in criminal matters and police cooperation. therefore, an equivalent level of protection of the rights and freedoms of natural persons should be ensured in all member states when personal data are processed by competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the commission proposal on the use of eu passenger name record (pnr) data. it should be noted that the nature of crime and terrorist activities has been changing in recent years. it has become bolder, more complex and increasingly transnational. given the high costs associated with crime, it has been found that a growing number of citizens want stronger action at eu level to combat organised crime and terrorism. pnr data information provided by passengers when booking a ticket and held by the air carrier. these data are primarily used by air carriers for operational purposes (including information provided in 19 fields such as travel date, travel itinerary, ticket details, contact details, travel agent information, means of payment used, seat number and baggage data), although they are valuable to air carriers from both a commercial and statistical point of view. the commission proposal sets out two main objectives: first, to harmonise the provisions on the obligation of air carriers operating flights to or from a third country and to or from the territory of at least one member state to transfer pnr data to law enforcement authorities; and second, to set out the criteria for the use of such information by law enforcement authorities, i.e. for the purposes of preventing, detecting, investigating and prosecuting terrorist offences and serious crime.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the protection of trade secrets against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure. some member states have adopted legislation to protect trade secrets against misappropriation, but some member states have not defined trade secrets and do not have binding legislation on the protection of trade secrets against misappropriation. this situation creates gaps and obstacles to the effective functioning of the internal market. it is also appropriate to determine at union level the cases in which the acquisition, use and disclosure of a trade secret are lawful or unlawful and to limit the period of application of redress procedures in order to achieve the objective of this directive of ensuring the consistent protection of trade secrets in the european union. it is therefore important to establish a uniform definition of a trade secret without limiting the object which must be protected against misappropriation. such definition should be formulated to cover business information, technological information and practical experience, taking into account both the legitimate interest in keeping such information secret and the legitimate expectation that such confidentiality will be preserved.

in writing. ‒ currently, the transport market share held by rail in the eu remains low, and many consumers in a number of eu countries, including lithuania, are not completely satisfied with rail services. i believe that strengthening the european railway agency (by gradually delegating to it some national responsibilities) and making it a one—stop shop would make european railways more competitive and efficient, which in turn would increase consumer satisfaction. having an agency to monitor the performance of the national authorities in charge of rail safety is very important in order to keep standards high and consistent across the eu member states.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal for an eu railway agency. this new set of legislation is designed to create a common european railway area. this is the technical part of the 4th railway code, which regulates the interoperability and safety of the rail system and the activities of the eu railway agency. the new rules simplify and make it cheaper for companies planning to expand their operations in several eu countries to certify locomotives and rolling stock. they will no longer have to apply for these certificates to each eu country individually a single safety certificate will be issued by the european railway agency. this set of documents is of great importance not only for the railway sector but also for the competitiveness of the european union as a whole. the need to strengthen the role of the european railway agency has been discussed for many years. today, that has become a reality. this will not only reduce the administrative burden on carriers in the future, but also ensure a more consistent application of rail legislation across the eu. national authorities will have to recognise the importance of working with and between the european railway agency (era) in order to create an integrated and dynamic cross-border railway system. cooperation is even more necessary for those countries using the 1 520 mm wide crane (the russian crane, which is also used by lithuania), as they will have to conclude a multilateral agreement with the ega, which will define the conditions under which the vehicle's authorisation will also be valid in the other member states concerned.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which examines the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european union agency for railways. the three previous railway files already provided for substantial changes to make european railways more competitive and interoperable, while maintaining a high level of safety. however, barriers to competition, discrimination and a lack of a liberalised, dynamic and business-friendly environment remain in this sector. today there are too many different national legal provisions, and too many unclear procedures and standards. the commission has developed this fourth railway package with the aim of improving the performance of the railway sector and increasing competitiveness, thereby improving the quality and efficiency of rail services. this aims at better compatibility of technical infrastructure, rolling stock, signalling and other railway systems, as well as simplification of procedures for authorising the use of rolling stock on the european rail network. the proposals are closely linked, in particular because the directives set out many of the tasks of the european railway agency.
in writing. ‒ before voting on this much-needed proposal, please note the reasoned opinions of the parliaments of even three member states: lithuania, romania and sweden. they point out that the fact that the european railway agency has acquired the right to certify railway vehicles for both european and national transport activities bypassing national authorities is a breach of the principle of subsidiarity. are we forgetting the principle of mutual recognition and distrust of national institutions? what will be the next step in this direction the establishment of a european agency for the safety of light vehicles? on the other hand, apart from this element which is contrary to the principle of subsidiarity, i am convinced that the egf is a necessary institution. it will make a significant contribution to the creation of a single european railway market.
