in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation, which sets out the position adopted by the council at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union. the european union rail market has undergone major changes over the last decade, which have been gradually implemented under three railway packages to open up national markets and ensure that railways become more competitive and interoperable at eu level, while maintaining a high level of safety. however, despite the major innovations in the eu acquis that have created an internal market for rail transport services the share of rail transport in the context of intra-eu transport remains modest. the overall eu market share for rail transport is currently stuck at 6% and 54% of consumers are dissatisfied with rail services, according to eurobarometer. the commission therefore decided in january 2013 to present the fourth railway package in order to remove the remaining obstacles to the creation of a single european railway market and to improve the quality and efficiency of rail services.
in writing. ‒ the before voting in favour of this much-needed proposal, please note the reasoned opinions of the parliaments of even three member states - lithuania, romania and sweden. they point out that the fact that the european railway agency has acquired the right to certify railway vehicles for both european and national transport activities bypassing national authorities is a breach of the principle of subsidiarity. are we forgetting the principle of mutual recognition and distrust of national institutions? what will be the next step in this direction the establishment of a european agency for the safety of light vehicles? on the other hand, apart from this element which is contrary to the principle of subsidiarity, i am convinced that the fourth railway package is a much-needed document. it will go a long way towards creating a single european railway market. i would also like to draw the attention of my colleagues to the fact that the ega document obliges to take account of the interests of the member states which use the 1520 mm track and which constitute a substantially separate railway area. in this respect, the fourth package lacks only one commitment: to make every effort to speed up the construction of rail baltica and to make european railways finally a single system.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal on eu rail safety. this new set of legislation is designed to create a common european railway area. this is the technical part of the 4th railway code, which regulates the interoperability and safety of the rail system and the activities of the eu railway agency. the new rules simplify and make it cheaper for companies planning to expand their operations in several eu countries to certify locomotives and rolling stock. they will no longer have to apply for these certificates to each eu country individually a single safety certificate will be issued by the european railway agency. this set of documents is of great importance not only for the railway sector but also for the competitiveness of the european union as a whole. the need to strengthen the role of the european railway agency has been discussed for many years. today, that has become a reality. this will not only reduce the administrative burden on carriers in the future, but also ensure a more consistent application of rail legislation across the eu. the european safety certificate will undoubtedly be of benefit to carriers wishing to expand their activities in several eu countries. this will save them not only money but also time. together, we will maintain a high level of security. it is also essential to reach an agreement as soon as possible on facilitating the entry of new entrants and service providers into the internal rail passenger markets, as increased competition would lead to lower prices and higher quality of service.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which examines the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive on railway safety. the establishment of a common railway safety regulatory framework is necessary in order to create a common railway transport market. member states have developed their safety rules, mainly applicable to national lines, on the basis of national technical and operational concepts. at the same time, the different principles, approaches and cultures made it difficult to overcome technical obstacles and to start international transport activities. directive 2004/49/ec on safety on the community's railways was a major step forward in the development of a common regulatory framework for railway safety. in order to ensure that member states do not develop their own safety rules and standards for national lines based on national technical and operational concepts, this directive establishes a framework for harmonising the content of safety rules, the safety certification of railway undertakings, the tasks and functions of safety authorities and the accident investigation procedure. however, safety shall continue to be certified at national level. the establishment and application of the single eu safety certificate has always been a long-term objective. the main objective of the commission proposal for the revision of directive 2004/49/ec was to introduce a single union safety certificate to replace the current two-part system (a and b).
in writing. ‒ the before voting in favour of this much-needed proposal, please note the reasoned opinions of the parliaments of even three member states - lithuania, romania and sweden. they point out that the fact that the european railway agency has acquired the right to certify railway vehicles for both european and national transport activities bypassing national authorities is a breach of the principle of subsidiarity. are we forgetting the principle of mutual recognition and distrust of national institutions? what will be the next step in this direction the establishment of a european agency for the safety of light vehicles? on the other hand, apart from this element which is contrary to the principle of subsidiarity, i am convinced that the harmonization of safety requirements in rail transport is a very welcome development which will lead to the creation of a truly unified european railway system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to increase the credibility of benchmarks. the new rules increase the soundness, transparency and reliability of benchmarks such as libor and euribor. these indices affect the value of financial instruments and contracts in excess of eur 500 billion and can therefore directly determine the stability of eu financial markets. i agree that stricter regulation was necessary after the libor scandal, where traders manipulated benchmarks and interest rates for huge profits. these indicators are used to determine the prices of derivatives and loans worth billions of euros worldwide. it is also important to distinguish between benchmarks of particular importance and to apply stricter transparency requirements to them.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. legislation should take into account the fact that the vast majority of businesses and households, investors and financial institutions use available benchmarks from across the eu and beyond on a daily basis to do business, trade, invest, insure against risks and to grant or receive credit efficiently. it is therefore necessary, in the interests of the stability and efficiency of markets and the economy in general, to ensure that legislative action limits as little as possible the number and variety of benchmarks proposed and used in the eu. indeed, more benchmarks are needed to reduce the importance of certain large benchmarks to the system and to give users more opportunities to exercise effective market discipline and to prevent or deter manipulation of benchmarks. this has three main objectives: firstly, to strengthen the governance of systems and standards, in particular for widely used and systemically important benchmarks, and to reduce the risk of manipulation and abuse. second, to enhance transparency by giving all benchmark users greater access to information to enable them to make informed decisions. third, to support the availability and availability of a wide variety of benchmarks, with a proportionate application of governance requirements. this includes the creation of a level playing field for all administrators, whether established in the european union or in third countries.
in writing. ‒ the i support the draft regulation submitted. the new rules would ensure the soundness, transparency and reliability of indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. it should be noted that these indicators are of crucial importance in the financial sector for the pricing of various products and for the correct allocation of risk and capital. the proposed new measures will prevent index manipulation and help restore confidence in the markets. harmonised international benchmarks will reflect the real economy, increase market transparency and benefit end-users.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because there is a clear regulatory gap where supervisors carry out the supervision of financial instruments but do not supervise the development and management of indices that determine the risk profile, performance and economic value of these instruments. however, the proposed document is weak and its provisions are unlikely to prevent further index manipulation scandals in the future. the document does not mention the transparency of the process or consumer protection, which gives the report an even more incomplete impression.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution on attacks on hospitals and schools in violation of international humanitarian law. the armed conflict has seen attacks on hospitals and schools, on doctors without borders health centres in kunduz, afghanistan, on raza, yemen, and on some towns in syria. the denial of humanitarian aid and access, the execution of civilians and humanitarian workers, the detention of civilians in appalling conditions, and the use of civilians as hostages or forced labour are all on the rise. the increased needs and challenges, the lack of long-term commitments and the increasing costs of humanitarian aid have contributed to the current humanitarian system being close to its limits. i support calls for parties to conflict to respect the basic principles of international humanitarian law during conflicts and not to target civilian infrastructure. it is also essential to increase the security of aid workers by ensuring a more effective response to attacks. the eu and its member states should urge the un and the un security council to ensure the protection of local and international humanitarian workers.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is a report by parliament on attacks on hospitals and schools, in violation of international humanitarian law. the international community has witnessed a worrying trend in recent years worldwide towards attacks on hospitals and schools during armed conflicts, such as the recent attacks on doctors without borders health centres in afghanistan in 2015, the attacks in yemen in 2016 and attacks in some syrian towns during the ongoing conflict. there is an unprecedented increase in the denial of humanitarian assistance and access, executions of civilians and humanitarian workers, and the detention of civilians in appalling conditions, including use of civilians as hostages and forced labour. reaffirming that international humanitarian law is an essential part of modern human history, parliament strongly condemned the failure to respect the norms of international humanitarian law and expressed its shock and deep concern at the deadly attacks on hospitals, schools and other civilian objects, targeting and victimizing patients, students, medical staff and teachers, humanitarian aid workers, children and family members. parliament therefore calls on the member states, the eu institutions and the high representative and vice-president of the commission to recognise the true scale of this emergency and to use all available means to resolve the issue.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. first, it is necessary to prevent attacks on hospitals and schools. these establishments must be adequately protected and must not be the target of armed attacks. in the light of the pattern of deadly attacks on hospitals and schools, it is necessary to draw up a concrete action plan as a matter of urgency and to take all necessary measures to address this issue and ensure that these institutions remain a neutral protected area. it is important to note that attacks on hospitals and schools are to be considered as serious violations of the 1949 geneva conventions and as war crimes under the rome statute of the icc, which would be subject to strict liability. in addition, it is essential to ensure that the provisions of humanitarian law are properly respected in order to protect human life and dignity and to meet the needs of persons in emergency situations of war.
in writing. - i voted for this report. i think it reflects very well the european parliament's position that attacks on hospitals, schools and other civilian objects are intolerable and condemnable. i support the idea that we should impose an eu arms embargo on countries that commit serious violations of international humanitarian law, in particular when the violations involve the deliberate targeting of civilian objects. health is a human right that should be available to all, no matter which side is fighting. i believe that attacks on hospitals are essentially attacks on ourselves.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this proposal on public access to documents in 2014/2015. full transparency is the basis for citizens' trust in the eu institutions. it contributes to the understanding of the rights provided for in the union legal framework and to the understanding and knowledge of the eu decision-making process, and to the proper implementation of administrative and legislative procedures. the right of access to documents is a fundamental right which promotes good administrative practice in relation to access to documents, ensuring democratic control of the activities of the institutions and their compliance with the provisions of the treaties. the eu institutions and bodies have not appointed a transparency officer from within their governance structures to be responsible for compliance and improving practices; i support the calls for the institutions to do so as soon as possible. i agree that in order to ensure a legal, accountable and democratic political system that respects the rule of law, citizens have the right to know and control: the activities of their representatives when they are elected or appointed to public office, the decision-making process and the way public funds are allocated and used, and the results achieved. i therefore agree that it is essential to make public an electronic register containing all the information mentioned above.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it provides an assessment of the way in which the public's right of access to documents was implemented in 2014/2015. parliament noted that full transparency is the basis for citizens' trust in the eu institutions, which helps to understand the rights provided for in the union's legal framework and to understand and inform the eu decision-making process, and contributes to the proper implementation of administrative and legislative procedures. the right of access to documents is a fundamental right protected by the charter of fundamental rights and the treaties, in particular with a view to ensuring that this right can be exercised as easily as possible and to promoting good administrative practices in relation to access to documents, ensuring democratic control of the activities of the institutions and their compliance with the provisions of the treaties. in its report, parliament notes that the three eu institutions have not followed up properly on many of the recommendations made in the 2011-2013 resolution on the public's right of access to documents. parliament particularly regrets that the eu institutions and bodies have not appointed a transparency officer from within their governance structures to be responsible for compliance and improving practices.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal on women domestic workers and carers in the eu. under the ilo convention, a domestic worker is any person who works in one or more households in an employment relationship. supervision services work in public or private institutions providing personal childcare, care for the elderly, sick or disabled. in 2010, more than 52 million people were employed in the household sector, and this figure has yet to be added to the 7.4 million household workers under the age of 15, representing 5.9% of all workers in industrialized countries. the majority of people working in this sector in 2010 were women. unfortunately, undeclared work and exploitation are widespread in these sectors. i therefore agree that it is urgently necessary to recognise the work of domestic workers as genuine work and as having value throughout the eu, since recognition of this occupational sector should reduce undeclared work and promote social integration. i support calls on the commission to present policy instruments in the area of domestic work and care services, which would include initiatives setting out quality guidelines for both sectors.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this report because it is parliament's voice on women domestic workers and carers in the eu. according to the ilo, more than 52 million people were employed in the domestic sector in 2010 and according to the ilo, the majority of people employed in this sector in 2010 were women (83% of the total workforce). however, parliament notes that in both sectors, the prevalence of undeclared work and exploitation, and the work of domestic workers and care providers, is most associated with this risk: job insecurity, geographical mobility, irregular working hours, seasonality, rotation, uncertainty, temporary nature, it is mostly undeclared. according to the ilo, 29.9% of domestic workers are not covered by any national labour legislation, which means that domestic workers and carers are very rarely and unevenly regulated in the member states, are often not considered as typical or ordinary workers and therefore have much more limited labour rights and social protection. parliament therefore called on the member states to develop legal frameworks to define the rights and obligations of the various stakeholders and to allow for legal and organised employment of domestic and care providers, in order to provide legal certainty for both workers in this sector and their potential employers.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. it should be noted that care and household services have a high potential for job creation. they can improve work-life balance, increase productivity and transfer undeclared work to the formal labour market. the transfer of these services from the shadow economy to the formal economy would help to create and develop micro-enterprises and smes. in this context, particular attention should be paid to the ilo convention 189 on decent and appropriate work for domestic workers and its ratification. it is essential to establish legal regulations defining the status of domestic workers in the eu countries. in addition, common rules should be drawn up for the provision of domestic and care services. in view of the benefits of these services, investment in more and better measures to prevent, detect and combat illegal work in the domestic and care services sector should be encouraged.

in writing. – the energy union’s aim is providing mutual benefits: to secure energy for consumers at affordable prices, create competitive market opportunities for suppliers and strengthen eu members’ solidarity. one of the union’s key goals was achieving greater energy diversification by finding alternative sources. nord stream 2 represents neither source nor supply diversification. it duplicates the existing nord stream 1 pipeline and can become a russian political weapon. in order to stay resilient, the eu needs more cooperativeness and interconnection. this killer-project’s aim is opening up old divisions by destroying recently installed interconnectors in central europe and by creating winners that will be directly supplied by nord stream 2 and losers bypassed by it. ukraine’s european future would also be put at risk as nord stream 2 would create the conditions to cut off the gas currently transited through it. developing alternative energy sources infrastructure, boosting eu energy production and building new pipelines and interconnections compose an investment plan towards a common and secure energy future. energy security is a key pillar of the eu’s energy union strategy and i believe nord stream 2 would eliminate any prospect of achieving a competitive and resilient internal eu gas market, free from political manipulation.
in writing. there have been dozens of studies on europe's need to diversify its energy suppliers for its own security. the implementation of the third energy package has fundamentally changed the situation in lithuania. a few years ago we were 100% dependent on gazprom gas, and today we are talking about realistic plans to completely abandon it. the possibility of choosing not to accept the terms of russia's increasingly aggressive foreign policy is an aspiration of the countries of central and eastern europe. the european commission has taken the right steps towards the energy union. however, the nord stream 2 plan is completely contrary to this objective. the eu's largest economy is naturally keen to maximise its efficiency, and it is argued that the agreement will allow this to happen. however, the recent debate in the bundestag on the cost of this 'commercial' project for germany, which will need to adapt its domestic gas networks to the new flow, raises serious doubts. the initial estimate is around eur 500 million. it is clear that the project will be costly and that other countries will pay a huge price for europe's ever-increasing dependence on russian gas. the damage caused by nord stream 2 is therefore not only in terms of geopolitical or energy security, but also in terms of economic viability. moreover, the imminent opening of the possibility to import gas from the usa could fundamentally change the european gas market. trade with this strategic partner, not an aggressive neighbor, should be the direction to take.
for the efdd group mr president, commissioner, youth unemployment is the most painful thorn in the side of europe's future. without work, the union's youth is losing hope for the future. and for years, there have been programs, millions of euros, to try to reduce youth unemployment. if one looks at the statistics for several years, when youth unemployment is by no means decreasing but remains at a stable level, it should be noted that all measures to reduce unemployment are insufficient and more declarative. the financial incentives for employers are too low, the commitment period is too short. the money spent on re-qualification doesn't produce the results we want. i think that we need to have a different approach and that it should not be limited to unemployment. for a young person, a home is as important as a job. let's build it and let the young people have it on a preferential basis. housing and work for young families with children should be the main priority of every european union country and every municipality. another incentive for young people let's create legislation to allow young people to take up family businesses on preferential terms throughout the european union. thus, lower taxation of labour, preferential taxes and tax rates for employers and for young people themselves under the age of 30 could at least partially address the problem of youth unemployment.
in writing. in the last few years, there has been a lot of discussion in the eu and in the member states on how to combat youth unemployment, or at least how to reduce its negative consequences. youth unemployment itself is a strange enough phenomenon in a developed, safe and educated europe the data show that young people have never lived better than now in history, if we consider the availability of nutrition, education, the level of protection of human rights and freedoms, the ability to travel for academic and professional purposes not only in the european union but also around the world, not to mention the opportunities offered by the internet. so does the commission not think that we have so far involved young people too little or not enough in the eu debate on the problems facing young people today, and in particular the problem of unemployment? do i think that the eu has not paid enough attention to promoting youth entrepreneurship, and in particular to promoting innovative entrepreneurship, which is what our younger generation is best equipped to do? does the commission not think that it would be worthwhile for the eu to launch a large-scale initiative to actively involve young people (both young entrepreneurs and those who want to become entrepreneurs) in order to jointly seek concrete means to empower the young generation and unlock their potential to create jobs not only for themselves but also for others? could such an initiative be one of the initiatives supported by the european fund for strategic investments, as a real investment in the future?

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation because the european union (eu) has signed a number of fisheries partnership agreements and protocols with third countries in recent years. under fisheries partnership agreements, the eu provides financial and technical assistance in exchange for fishing opportunities for various fish stocks in the exclusive economic zone of the partner country. since 2014, following the reform of the common fisheries policy, these agreements have been referred to as sustainable fisheries partnership agreements. this sustainable fisheries partnership agreement is the first to be concluded between the european union and the republic of liberia, which has 570 km of atlantic coastline. the liberian exclusive economic zone, covering 246 152 km2, is home to bottom and pelagic fish stocks, including tuna and related species. the eu and liberia cooperate through multilateral agreements. in addition, the liberian food and agriculture policy and strategy 2008 adopted relevant provisions based on international best practice as set out in the non-binding 1995 food and agriculture organisation (fao) code for responsible fisheries (ccrf). the liberian authorities are working closely with the eu to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the conclusion of a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with liberia would therefore help the eu to achieve its objectives in combating iuu fishing and to promote the common fisheries policy objective of sustainable management of fisheries and aquaculture activities.

in writing. the communication on the directive on parental leave raises issues of major importance for modern european society. europe is without doubt the most ageing continent. the birth rate and replacement rate for generations in the european union are incredibly low. there are a number of reasons for this situation, but the main one is the deviation from traditional european family values. no institutional solution will remedy this situation unless we try to restore the importance and special values of the family, with a place for mother, father and children. in recent decades, we have seen a dangerous and socially damaging trend towards the devaluation of the family in the public sphere and even an attempt to change the definition of the family. the countries that have chosen this wrong path face the greatest demographic challenges. to change that, we must remember the reasons why it happened. the first step is to restore the right order in the sphere of values, and then to concentrate on the means of resolving the most serious social crisis europe is experiencing. one such measure is the issue of parental leave. this leave must be supportive and not a threat to the functioning of the family and the decision to have children. it is therefore best to leave matters relating to parental leave to the member states which know best the needs of their citizens.

member of the commission. – mr president, on behalf of commissioner arias cañete, let me first thank honourable members for their questions on the commission’s action on nuclear installations in belarus. allow me to update you on how we are working towards ensuring the facility will be operated only with the highest level of safety standards. nuclear safety remains a key priority for the commission as confirmed by the energy union framework strategy. while fostering cooperation, transparency and trust, we are using all the instruments at our disposal to ensure the highest possible safety standards in the eu and internationally. this is absolutely non-negotiable. on eu-belarus nuclear safety cooperation: that is exactly the approach we have always taken with belarus – nuclear safety and radiological protection have always been the key focus of our exchanges. since 2011, the european union has been providing the belarusian nuclear regulatory authority with technical assistance under the eu’s instrument for nuclear safety cooperation by transferring eu best practices on the regulatory process, including formulation of licensing conditions and inspection practices, from site selection to commissioning and operation. since april 2015, one eu expert has been based in minsk, where we have been strengthening the regulator during the construction of the nuclear plant project from an early stage. the ultimate aim is to share eu expertise and build national capacity to ensure compliance with the best international practices and standards. through this technical assistance the competent regulatory authority of belarus has improved its human and technical capacity. however, the commission considers that the independence of the belarusian regulator has to be further strengthened and a close monitoring of development is therefore needed. on nuclear safety stress tests: as i said before, openness and transparency is essential when it comes to nuclear safety. by working together with our neighbours in an open way we can benefit from the exchange of information and expertise while building trust. in that spirit, the commission welcomes belarus’s extensive use of iaea expert peer review services to help ensure safety. before i address where we are with the ostrovets nuclear safety stress test, i would like to clarify two things which are essential in understanding the overall process. firstly, nuclear safety stress tests, both in the eu and in third countries, are carried out on a voluntary basis. legally speaking, the european union cannot oblige any member state, nor third countries, which choose nuclear energy, to undertake such stress tests. nevertheless, there is a political commitment to perform stress tests within the eu and an encouragement to extend them outside, as the march 2011 european council called not only for comprehensive and transparent risk and safety assessments of all eu nuclear power plants, but also for carrying out similar stress tests in the neighbouring countries and worldwide. since then, the commission has been promoting the undertaking of stress tests in neighbouring countries. it is encouraging that ukraine has already voluntarily participated in such an exercise and armenia is currently in the process of doing so, supported financially by the european union. secondly, a stress test is a national competence. it is performed by the operator and supervised by the national nuclear regulatory authority. it is only after the national stress test assessment is finalised and the outcome of the assessment is reported on, that the commission can and in fact does organise peer reviews by eu national nuclear safety authorities. in june 2011, based on a commission initiative, several neighbouring countries, including belarus, confirmed their willingness to undertake nuclear stress tests by signing the declaration on conducting nuclear safety stress tests. since then, we have been urging belarus to perform a nuclear safety stress test. the commission expects, in the light of the council conclusions in february 2016, that eu-belarus cooperation will evolve positively also in this regard. what are the next steps? the commission was informed by belarus that it has now put in place a legal instrument regulating the implementation of nuclear safety stress tests in line with european specifications. belarus has also indicated that upon conclusion of the ostrovets stress test process, the national assessment report will be presented to the commission in the course of 2016 and 2017. on our side, the necessary preparations for the peer review have already been done, and it is now in the work programme of the european nuclear safety regulators group. together with the commission, this group of experts will organise the peer review as soon as we receive the national assessment report. while this is already a positive development, the commission would like to speed up the process’s implementation in belarus and to receive the stress test report as soon as possible. therefore, our services are planning a technical mission to belarus in the coming months to discuss progress. to conclude, let me assure you that the commission remains fully committed to raising nuclear safety with the belarusian authorities at all political levels. we will continue to promote the highest level of standards on nuclear safety in belarus, together with all of our international partners. let me also assure you that we are in close contact with the neighbouring member states, in particular lithuania, to follow the developments with the ostrovets nuclear power plant. i will ensure that the european parliament is kept fully up to date with all the developments as and when they happen.

in writing. – unfair trading practices (utps) can affect small food producers and retailers in business relationships where one party is in a stronger position than the other. utps are often regarded as practices that deviate from good commercial conduct or are contrary to good faith and fair dealing imposed from one trading partner to another. these practices can have a negative effect on the eu economy as a whole, resulting in smes losing their ability to invest and innovate and a failure to seek expansion in the single market. the issue has come to our attention in recent years with many member states installing self-regulatory frameworks and providing examples of best practices. however, the problem of utps is growing and becoming more widespread, and voluntary procedures will not be enough to solve the issue. consistent action from the eu is needed to eliminate utps in the food supply chain and to protect small producers. this can be done through defining what utps consist of and the penalty for their use, as well as encouraging member states to exchange best practices. the problem of unfair trading internally in the eu must be dealt with to protect fair competition and prevent worsening effects on the eu economy.
in writing. i strongly support this future council directive and the improvements that parliament has made to it. this directive lays down rules to combat tax avoidance practices. one study estimated that the global economy loses $100 billion to $240 billion annually because of aggressive tax optimization by multinational corporations. this amount represents 4/10% of the worldwide income tax revenue. such huge revenue losses are particularly damaging to countries, as they reduce their ability to invest in promoting employment, fighting poverty and developing effective universal health care systems. the further development of economic and monetary union requires the harmonisation of tax systems in the european union, inter alia, to limit tax avoidance by multinational companies. a fair and efficient corporate tax system must become a cornerstone of the single market. because if the member states agree on taxation issues, we will have an efficient and reliable single market. we need to take a balanced approach to the implementation of tax systems. i also support the main objective of parliament's proposals - that companies pay taxes where they make their profits - and i therefore urge the commission to amend its proposal accordingly.
in writing. mr president, the report on combating tax avoidance raises a number of important issues to which i would like to draw attention. the union's policy priorities in relation to international taxation should focus on a framework that ensures that tax is paid where profits are generated, i.e. where residence or business is located. this approach will make it possible to protect national tax systems more effectively. this is all the more important given that, according to oecd research and data, unfair and aggressive tax planning by multinational companies contributes to a loss of between usd 100 and 240 billion from national budgets each year. such actions lead directly to a loss of revenue for the states, reduce employment in the states and lead to problems in the pension systems. for this reason, the emphasis in the communication on the fight against tax fraud is a step in the right direction, condemning the threat to the cohesion of the internal market. in addition, we should follow the rules of social justice when it comes to legal developments in this area. therefore, the transfer of profits to tax havens and the avoidance of taxation in the country of origin of profits should be opposed, and taxation by multinational companies in particular should be fair. however, the introduction of a single european taxpayer identification number should not be necessary as it has little to do with the fight against financial fraud and would only unnecessarily restrict the sovereignty of the member states in this area.
in writing. ‒ illicit trade in tobacco products is criminal activity that poses a serious threat to public health and huge losses of revenue to the eu in unpaid taxes. the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products (fctc protocol) was adopted by the fctc in 2012 and constitutes the only multilateral regulatory initiative in combatting illicit tobacco trading and needs to be ratified by 40 parties for it to enter into force. the protocol contains a set of rules and policies in the field of fighting illicit trade in tobacco and aims to make the supply chain, products, and equipment of tobacco secure in the global system. the ratification of the fctc protocol will benefit public health and improve the fight against the illegal trade of tobacco products. i voted in favour of the resolution to give the european parliament’s consent to the conclusion of the protocol and forward its position to the council, commission, and member states to ensure the quick ratification so the protocol can enter into force and implementation.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its support for the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol to the who framework convention on tobacco control on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products. the who framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) is the first global health agreement. it was developed in response to the global tobacco epidemic and aims to address certain causes of this phenomenon, including illicit trade in tobacco products. the convention entered into force in 2005 and currently has 180 parties. the protocol on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products was adopted by the conference of the parties in seoul in 2012. this protocol is currently the only multilateral regulatory initiative in this area. the eu signed the iccpr protocol in 2013. the protocol requires the ratification of 40 countries for its entry into force and the immediate ratification by the european union (and its member states) would make a significant contribution to the speedy entry into force and implementation of the iccpr protocol.

in writing. ‒ the the objective of the protocol is to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. the protocol defines illicit trade in tobacco products as any practice or activity prohibited by law in connection with the manufacture, transport, receipt, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products. to address this problem, the protocol applies to the tobacco supply chain, using a variety of governmental instruments. it requires the establishment of a universal marking and tracing system within five years of the entry into force of the protocol. the aim is also to establish a global information-sharing contact point within the secretariat of the who framework convention on tobacco control. it will lead the development of national and regional labelling and tracing systems. the protocol also contains additional provisions to combat the illicit supply chain of tobacco products. they cover licensing, record keeping requirements, as well as online sales, duty-free trade and international transit regulation.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is the report in which parliament has spoken on peace support operations and on the eu's relations with the united nations and the african union. peacekeeping operations are a crisis response with a un mandate, usually in support of internationally recognised organisations, and aim to prevent armed conflict, restore, maintain or strengthen peace, ensure the implementation of peace treaties and respond to complex emergencies and challenges posed by failing or weak states. stability in the neighbouring countries of africa and europe would have a very positive impact on all our countries. however, africa is increasingly fragile states and unmanaged areas, and many people are affected by poverty, lawlessness, corruption and violence, while permeable borders on the continent create favourable conditions for violence, reduced security and opportunities for criminal activity. in its report, parliament stresses the need to coordinate external action, using diplomatic, security and development tools, to restore confidence and address the challenges of war, internal conflicts, insecurity, vulnerability and transition. it also considers that the deployment of several un mandated missions, involving different actors and regional organisations in the same area of operations, is becoming an increasingly common phenomenon in the field of modern peacekeeping operations. considers it therefore essential to manage these complex partnerships without duplication of activities or missions in order to successfully conduct operations, and therefore calls for the evaluation and rationalisation of existing structures.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal for an eu-palau agreement on the short-stay visa waiver. relations between the european union and the republic of palau are governed by the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states (acp) and the european community and its member states, known as the cotonou agreement. the proposed agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and palau to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa-free regime applies to all categories of persons (civilians, diplomats, officials and/or officials and holders of special passports) travelling abroad for any purpose other than gainful employment.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its consent to the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of palau on the short-stay visa waiver. relations between the european union and the republic of palau are governed by the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states (acp) and the european community and its member states, known as the cotonou agreement. the signed agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and palau to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa-free regime applies to all categories of persons (civilians, diplomats, officials and/or officials and holders of special passports) travelling abroad for any purpose other than gainful employment. this agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is the result of the development of relations between the european union and the republic of palau, further confirming the important political importance of the cotonou agreement, and is a complementary instrument to strengthen economic and cultural links and to promote political dialogue on a wide range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms.

in writing. ‒ the information technology agreement (ita) today counts 82 wto member states as participants. each participant must eliminate and require customs duties at zero for all information technology products (it) covered. the duty free treatment of it products has been crucial in the development and expansion of trade in the it sector. in july of 2015, an agreement was reached to expand the product coverage of the agreement between 27 members. by 2019 almost all of the imports of the relevant it products will be duty free. the expansion of the ita is important for trade, and this is the first major tariff cutting deal since the inception of the wto. i voted for this resolution because of the huge potential to create jobs and increase the gdp of the eu. it is important for the eu to not just give its consent to the agreement, but to ensure that more members join the agreement to create a beneficial situation for all.
in writing. ‒ the first agreement on trade in information technology products (itp) was concluded in 1996. it requires each participant to undertake to eliminate customs duties and apply a zero duty rate to all information technology products covered by this agreement, subject to the principle of most-favoured-nation status. in may 2012, six countries (the eu, the usa, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica) entered into negotiations with a view to extending the list of products covered by this agreement. the products covered by this agreement include next generation semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical devices including magnetic resonance imaging devices, printed circuit board machinery, telecommunications satellites and touch screens. this agreement will reduce prices for consumers as well as prices for producers who rely on imported components. the extension of the ita is a historic agreement the first significant agreement on tariff reductions since the establishment of the wto, with a high potential for job creation and gdp growth, and i therefore support the conclusion of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its support for the conclusion of the agreement as an extension of the declaration on trade in information technology products (itp) on behalf of the european union. the its requires each participant to undertake to eliminate customs duties and apply a zero duty rate to all information technology (it) products covered by this agreement, subject to the principle of most-favoured-nation status. the its covers approximately 200 tariff lines, including computers, telephones, as well as raw materials, components and equipment for the production of it goods. the unlimited regime for its participants has played a very important role in the extraordinary growth and expansion of trade in the it sector over almost 20 years of its application. trade in this sector has increased fourfold. however, technological progress has changed the it sector beyond recognition during this period and the scope of the its has remained the same. the products covered by this agreement include next generation semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical devices including magnetic resonance imaging devices, printed circuit board machinery, telecommunications satellites and touch screens.

in writing. ‒ trade in information technology products is probably one of the fastest growing areas of international trade. although the first agreement on trade in information technology products was concluded in 1996, its success is illustrated by the fact that the number of participants has increased from 29 signatories wto countries to the current 82. the its requires each participant to commit to eliminate customs duties and apply a zero duty rate to all it products covered by this agreement, subject to the principle of most-favoured-nation status. the its covers approximately 200 tariff lines, including computers, telephones, as well as raw materials, components and equipment for the production of it goods. the unlimited regime for its participants has played a very important role in the dramatic growth and quadrupling of trade in the it sector over almost 20 years of its application. the eu exports eur 189 billion worth of products falling under the expanded its and this is expected to increase significantly with the reduction of tariffs. this agreement will reduce prices for consumers as well as prices for producers who rely on imported components.

in writing. ‒ the anti-tax avoidance directive aims to transpose into eu law measures that limit the erosion of the tax base and the shifting of profits. its basic principle is that taxes must be paid in the country where the profits are earned. the directive also proposes to clearly define terms such as 'permanent residence', 'tax havens' and 'minimum economic activity', which have so far been interpreted in a rather different way, which hinders the effective fight against tax evasion. one of the ep's recommendations is to curb intra-group borrowing, one of the most common ways of showing low profits and thus avoiding taxation. the aim is also to limit the amount of interest payable that could be allowed to be deducted, as this would help to increase the proportion of taxes payable.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it sets out parliament's position on the council directive laying down rules for combating tax evasion practices which have a direct impact on the functioning of the internal market. according to one oecd study, the global economy loses $100 billion to $240 billion annually as a result of aggressive tax optimization by multinational corporations. this amount represents 4/10% of the worldwide income tax revenue. such revenue losses are particularly damaging to states, as they reduce their ability to invest in promoting employment, fighting poverty and developing effective universal health care systems. the creation of economic and monetary union requires harmonisation of the eu tax system. a fair and efficient corporate tax system must become a cornerstone of the single market. in order to create a reliable single market, member states must agree on taxation. a coherent approach to the implementation of tax systems is essential to ensure the proper functioning of the single market and the successful completion of the capital markets union. parliament welcomes the commission proposal and considers it a step forward in the fight against tax evasion by multinational companies. however, it considers that the adoption of the proposed amendments would make the proposal clearer and more effective. the main objective of these proposals is to ensure that companies pay taxes where they make profits.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. fair and effective corporate taxation must become the cornerstone of the single market. the goal is to fight against fraud from a competitive and productive approach and to protect medium and small businesses from being damaged by these practices. this is the only possible approach if we want to deliver competitiveness and a fairer tax system.
in writing. ‒ today, too often, multinational companies take action to shift their profits to tax havens without paying any corporation tax. i therefore support the amendments to the directive which seek to limit the possibilities for multinational companies to avoid taxation.
in writing. ‒ globalisation not only ensures the free movement of labour, capital, services and goods, but also facilitates the movement of businesses. unfortunately, as the experience of recent years has shown, companies have been very successful in exploiting tax regulatory disparities simply to hide their profits and avoid paying taxes where they produce or provide services. and these taxes finance all the public services, from public safety to ensure that these companies can operate, to training and education to provide companies with skilled workers, to health care to ensure that workers are not only skilled but also healthy. the question we are discussing today is therefore of vital importance to the existence of our present society. will we be able to ensure that companies, especially the big ones, play fair? will we continue to see some companies parasitize at the expense of states, and some states, including some eu member states, help to do so to their own advantage?

in writing. ‒ active substances which are deemed to have endocrine disruptors can pose a significant threat to the welfare of people that are exposed to them. the general court of the european union declared on 16 december 2015 that the commission breached eu law by failing to act to adopt delegated acts to specify scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties. the failure of the commission to not comply with its obligation and a violation of its institutional obligations must be noted. i voted in favour of this resolution as the commission must propose scientific criteria for determining endocrine-disrupting properties before the summer. the commission must comply with its obligations and this resolution and its forwarding to the president of the council and commission will help reach that goal.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is delaying the publication of criteria to determine whether a chemical is endocrine disrupting. the commission committed to do so by the end of 2013. as early as 2013, the european parliament called on the commission to take measures to reduce the exposure of humans to endocrine disrupting substances. these substances are likely to cause premature puberty, cancer and metabolic disorders. in december last year, the european court of justice recognised that the european commission had not established scientific criteria for the identification of endocrine disrupting substances in a timely manner. they were prepared back in 2013 but not published because it was decided to carry out an impact assessment, although this was not required by eu law. the commission should immediately implement its commitment and publish these criteria by the end of june this year.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is parliament's position on endocrine disrupting chemicals and the situation following the judgment of the general court of the european union of 16 december 2015. under eu law, active substances that are considered by scientific criteria to have endocrine disrupting properties that may cause adverse effects in humans are not approved. the commission has not yet adopted delegated acts setting out scientific criteria and their adoption is currently more than two and a half years behind schedule. in its judgment of 16 december 2015 in case t-521/14, the general court of the european union found that the commission had infringed eu law by failing to adopt delegated acts establishing scientific criteria for the definition of endocrine disrupting properties. in its resolution, parliament condemned the commission not only for failing to fulfil its duty to adopt delegated acts but also for failing to fulfil its institutional obligations under the treaties themselves, and recalled the commission's political commitment to present a proposal by the summer on scientific criteria for the definition of endocrine-disrupting properties.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. the general court ruled that the specification of scientific criteria can only be carried out in an objective manner on the basis of scientific data related to the endocrine system, independently of any other consideration, in particular economic ones, and that the commission is not entitled to change the regulatory balance laid down in a basic act via the application of powers delegated to it pursuant to article 290 tfeu.
in writing. ‒ the eu is in a dangerous situation as regards the control of dangerous substances. the court of justice of the eu last year found that the commission had breached eu law by failing to publish scientific criteria to be used to determine the endocrine-disrupting properties of the endocrine system when the current interim criteria do not provide an adequate level of protection. unfortunately, the commission did not act and decided in 2013 to carry out a social and economic impact assessment of the possible scientific criteria. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measure is imputable to the state. this decision seems even more strange in the sense that no one has asked the commission to carry out such an investigation, i.e. we can conclude that the commission has decided on its own initiative to violate eu law and has suspended the preparation of all legislation relevant to the health of europeans. we note that the commission, as guardian of the treaties, has itself infringed the eu treaties. it seems strange that the commissioner responsible for this issue, mr andriukaitis, has told parliament that the commission will still carry out an impact assessment and will not adopt the necessary legislation. we must condemn this behaviour of the commission, demand the immediate implementation of eu law adoption of delegated acts under regulation 528/2012 and the fulfilment of its institutional obligations under article 266 of the eu treaty, and recall that the explanations provided by president juncker or commissioner andriukaitis appear regrettable and cast doubt on their ability to perform their duties.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at simplifying the recognition of birth or marriage certificates. the new rules will simplify the presentation of certain public documents, such as birth or marriage certificates, to authorities in other eu countries. for example, they will no longer need to be legalised or translated into another language. the regulation provides that a multilingual standard form may be attached to certain civil status documents or certificates of authenticity. it will allow those wishing to present these documents to the authorities of other eu countries to avoid the obligation to present them together with a translation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it sets out parliament's position on the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the promotion of the free movement of citizens by simplifying the presentation of certain public documents in the european union. the purpose of this act is to promote the free movement of citizens and businesses by simplifying the recognition of certain public documents in the european union. the legislation does not regulate the recognition of the content of public documents, as it aims to preserve the independence of the member states in the field of family law. mobility of union citizens is a reality: some 12 million citizens study, work or live in a member state other than that of their nationality. while union citizens and businesses currently enjoy the right of free movement or the freedoms of the internal market, they may face administrative difficulties when they have to submit public documents to the authorities of another member state, for example when they arrive in another member state. following interinstitutional negotiations, the legislature and the commission reached a compromise text. this regulation thus applies to the civil status documents and to certain other documents frequently requested by citizens and relating, for example, to residence, nationality and conviction. the regulation provides that these authentic instruments do not require legalisation and apostille - the two administrative formalities normally required for authentic instruments issued by another member state.
in writing. ‒ i voted against. parliament would have liked to include within the scope of the regulation diplomas and education certificates, certificates of disability and certain documents relevant to businesses. furthermore, multilingual standard forms cannot circulate autonomously but must be annexed to the appropriate national documents, which constitutes an avoidable complication.
in writing. ‒ the legislation under consideration will simplify the recognition of certain public documents in the european union. some 12 million union citizens study, work or live in a member state other than that of their nationality. it is therefore clear that they may face a number of bureaucratic obstacles, in particular in relation to the recognition of documents issued in another country. it is important to note that the legislation does not regulate the recognition of the content of public documents. this preserves the independence of the member states in the area of family law. more importantly, public documents will not require the two administrative formalities of legalisation and apostille that are applied to documents issued by another member state. these simplifications for citizens are counterbalanced by the possibility for the administrative body receiving the document to request, by electronic means, the authenticity of the document directly from the issuing body. it is also welcome that the regulation establishes multilingual standard forms for many of the necessary public documents. they will be issued by the national authorities. this will greatly simplify procedures for eu citizens when they arrive in another member state. unfortunately, the outcome of the negotiations with the council has disappointed parliament on some issues. for some reason, the council did not agree to include diplomas and certificates of completion of training courses, certificates of disability and certain documents of importance to businesses in the scope of the regulation. it also did not allow multilingual standard forms to be submitted separately, they had to be attached to the corresponding national documents, a difficulty that could have been avoided. but that does not change the fact that much progress has been made.
in writing. ‒ this regulation is the fourth one, concerning the reform of the court of justice. the first regulation introduced various amendments concerning the composition and the rules of procedure of the court of justice and the general court, while the second regulation introduced a provision on temporary judges of the civil service tribunal. the third part of the reform was the subject of the main dispute, since it concerned the increase in the number of judges of the general court. the number of judges was increased on condition that the civil service tribunal was abolished and that civil service disputes were returned to the general court. this regulation is therefore drawn up in the light of the third regulation on the reform of the court of justice. the tribunal of the seven judges should be abolished in the second stage of the increase in the number of judges at the general court from 40 to 47. the court's proposal is therefore logical and in line with what the legislature has asked to be taken into account. so i'm in favor of the deal.

in writing. ‒ tuna is a vital part of the fish supply. unfortunately, many fishing countries have the capacity to destroy most of the world's tuna stocks without regulating fishing. to that end, we are today adopting a multiannual recovery plan for tuna. in evaluating the document, i can point to three shortcomings. the first plan is pretty irresponsible. it pays very little attention to the restoration of fish stocks, the essential condition of which is to fish far less than the adult fish. the second weakness of the plan is its social irresponsibility: the poorer eu member states are treated in the same way as the richer ones, despite the fact that not even the expansion of fisheries, but their recovery after irresponsible actions to reduce eu fishing capacity, could become one of the engines of regional growth and even regional expansion. and the third weakness is that the plan does not pay enough attention to working with non-eu countries, especially those known for their failure to comply with international agreements. still, a bad plan is better than no plan at all. i therefore vote against, while at the same time calling on the commission to take account of the comments made in the future.
in writing. in implementing this plan, member states should pay particular attention to non-industrial fishing activities and non-industrial sustainable gear types such as traditional traps (e.g. almadraba, tonnare), which have a very positive contribution to the recovery of tuna stocks due to their high selectivity and low environmental impact in marine ecosystems, and also have scientific value.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it aims to establish a mixed management plan for cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, which is the main fishing area for these three species. in recent years, 94% of the fish caught in the baltic sea were cod, herring and sprat. the baltic sea is essentially a closed sea where these three species are widespread and constantly interacting. it is therefore important to establish rules that take into account the interaction between those species, the impact of cod on stocks of haddock and sprat, and the impact of the latter on stocks of cod. given the significant impact of biological interactions and environmental conditions on the resources in the baltic sea, it is desirable that the scale and patterns of exploitation of these resources be adapted to reflect the revised scientific data on such interactions and changes in environmental conditions. in addition, such a method would be in line with the principle of ecosystem-based fisheries management. in order to achieve such adaptive management, the first step would be for the commission to propose that all the relevant resources be included in a single management plan.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. multiannual plans for fisheries management are an essential tool to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks and marine ecosystems. european parliament supported a proposal for multiannual plan for stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea and for the fisheries exploiting them. this baltic multiannual and multispecies plan is the first proposed plan to build on the principles of the 2013 reform of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ the i support this multiannual baltic cod, sprat and herring management plan. the plan will ensure that fishing in the baltic sea is sustainable and more predictable, and that the balance between the use of resources and the stability of fishing opportunities is maintained. it is also the first plan to actually cover different fish stocks, ensuring that their management is based on the latest scientific information. the additional sustainable fisheries buffers provided for will help to respond appropriately to the changing situation of the stocks. it should be noted that the measures provided for in this long-term plan will help to preserve the small-scale fisheries sector and ensure a reliable income from fishing. the rules will be clearer and simpler for fishermen. a clear, predictable and long-term conservation-oriented management of fish stocks will be established.
in writing. ‒ fishing in the eu's main inland seas the baltic sea is a highly sensitive issue. it is sensitive not only to us, the representatives of the baltic sea countries, but also to the entire baltic ecosystem. the countries around the sea have the capacity to destroy all fish stocks in this sea if fishing is not regulated. to this end, we are today adopting a multiannual plan for the management and fishing of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea. in evaluating the document, i can point to three shortcomings. the first plan is pretty irresponsible. it pays very little attention to the restoration of fish stocks, the essential condition of which is to catch fewer fish than they are grown. the second weakness of the plan is its social irresponsibility: the poorer eu member states are treated in the same way as the richer ones, despite the fact that not even the expansion of fisheries, but their recovery after irresponsible actions to reduce eu fishing capacity, could become one of the engines of regional growth and balanced regional expansion. and the third weakness is that the plan does not pay enough attention to working with non-eu baltic sea countries, which are notorious for their failure to comply with international agreements. still, a bad plan is better than no plan at all. i therefore vote against, while at the same time calling on the commission to take account of the comments made in the future.
in writing. the objective of this plan should be to restore, achieve and maintain populations of the species concerned above levels which can ensure sustainable fishing of the stocks concerned, while minimising the impact on other species.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it concerns the proposal for a council regulation on the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of matrimonial property regime. this regulation will be a very useful tool for international couples living in the european union. it governs the jurisdiction, the law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of matrimonial property regime. however, matters relating to the capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of the marriage, maintenance obligations and the succession of the deceased spouse are not covered by the scope of the regulation. the independence of the member states in the field of family law is thus preserved. furthermore, the regulation does not affect the substantive law of the member states as regards the matrimonial property regime.
