mr president, the commission recognises the link between trade, human rights and social and environmental standards. trade and foreign investments are indeed important tools in achieving economic growth, sustainable development and protection of human rights, which we expect from the commission and the council with regard to the implementation of the new trade strategy. at the multilateral level, the commission should take a leading role in the reform of wto governance. in particular, the wto should reform its trade policy review mechanisms in order to include social, environmental and human rights dimensions. it is important that the commission and the council both promote regular in-depth monitoring of the implementation of the human rights clauses in trade and association agreements. our parliament should also be more actively involved and consulted in this respect. clearly our trade policy should be a way to encourage eu partner countries to adopt higher social and environmental standards. on the other hand, eu companies abroad should comply with all their obligations, particularly with international standards in the areas of human rights, labour and the environment.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i was really surprised by the european council's approach, its approach to brexit. the question that is central to europe today is not just about listening to information. does this mean that the decision of citizens of one community member to leave that community does not raise any questions and discussions for the leaders of other countries? dear ones, brexit did not start yesterday, it started when we lightly cut europe's christian roots in the european union's constitution, which has not yet come into force. and when european politicians in 2005 did not hear the voice of either the french or the dutch citizens, they rejected that constitution. it was replaced by the lisbon treaty with bureaucratic red tape. and then later on, the greek financial crisis, the migrant tsunami, and so on, but nothing was really done to make the british voice heard, to change the european union, to make it more democratic, to make all states equal, to make all voices heard, to make collective decisions remembered, to have nation states, because otherwise it would be bad. honey, the british didn't give up anything. they gave the european union a last chance to change its policy. from globalisation and federalisation to a europe of states and peoples free from globalisation and federalisation. who are we today if we are left behind by a country that lives by the oldest rules of western politics and the highest standards? to answer the fundamental question: what will the future of europe be: a union of equal states or a dictatorship in brussels? it is necessary to convene a convention of all european states, which will outline the new guidelines of the european constitution and will be a new real impetus for the unity of peoples on the road to a prosperous europe.
the question asked when the blue card is raised. i'd like to ask you a question. i have spent seven years in this parliament observing the behaviour of the eurosceptics, and today i also have to say that they are very strangely disillusioned and confused. how do you think they really didn't understand and expect, or they just pretended that there are certain rules in the world that nobody just barges into their own market because it's extra jobs and stuff. and now they want to be friends with that bad europe, to communicate with it and sell their goods. how did you do that? what do you think, or did they really not understand?
today, the brexit camp is talking about the pressure being put on them, about the will of the british people being ignored. there is no such thing and there cannot be in this parliament. obviously the other british political leaders are under such pressure from their own citizens, i stress from the british citizens, that no leader dares to take responsibility for the outcome of the referendum and start brexit negotiations. there was no majority left in the british parliament to legitimize the referendum result and give the government a mandate to ask the european union to trigger article 50 of the treaty. i'm sure that with the british decision, we won't be divided into national cages. the challenge of patriotism is nationalism, the internal collapse of the european union, and it is nationalism that europe has already learned its lesson from. the best solution and our best response is a strong and united european union.
in writing. – brexit has created a political earthquake that has spread across europe. europe today needs to be reformed, with a new vision to be presented to its worried citizens, yet there is not enough recognition of this in the council. european citizens are not against the european union, they are tired and dissatisfied with the lack of action of the current european union. the european union currently gets caught up too much in the little things, whereas it needs to focus more on the big issues such as the migration crisis and terrorism. we must respect the decision of the british people and move forward and let britain figure out how to pull itself out of this crisis. the new british government must immediately activate article 50 and make clear the direction they plan to take. the remaining 27 eu countries need to look forward and move towards a stronger and more interconnected union that can offer more to its citizens.
in writing. the uk referendum has shocked europe. but if properly handled, such shock can have long-term benefits. european unity will not depend on loud theses about the need for further integration or on naive proposals to move towards a federal europe. we must respect the decision taken by the british, but we cannot in any way encourage their disengagement from europe as quickly as possible, as some senior officials have done carelessly. because we're cutting the branch we're sitting on. the latest meeting between the european commission and the european council decided to strengthen eu-nato cooperation in both continental security and missions outside europe. this is a serious positive step, as despite all the crises affecting europe, geopolitical and security issues remain paramount. first, we must understand that without the active participation of the united kingdom, this objective cannot be achieved. so, especially in the face of political chaos in london, we need to not blame the fence, but to reach out and find the best way for both sides to coexist after brexit. second, eu-nato cooperation must not become an increase in eu capabilities in the field of security. nato must remain the main security umbrella in europe, because only then will we be able to maintain the necessary close transatlantic link. the eu can and must play a greater role in expeditionary peacekeeping missions outside the continent.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu-peru agreement on the short-stay visa waiver which was signed on 14 march 2016 in brussels. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for the citizens of the eu and for the citizens of peru when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (ordinary, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders) travelling for all kinds of purposes, except for the purpose of carrying out a paid activity. the agreement has also many other important aspects. this implementation of this agreement will bring closer the people of the eu and peru, it will boost tourism and increase trade and investment relations. the eu is already one of the main trade partners and foreign investors for peru. moreover, the agreement contains a joint declaration on cooperation on illegal immigration and will help peru to become an important partner for the eu in the fight against organised crime, including human and drug trafficking. respect for human rights and the values of democracy are indeed an essential element of eu-peru relations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a visa-free regime agreement between the eu and the republic of peru. this agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is the result of the development of relations between the european union and the republic of peru and is a complementary instrument aimed at strengthening economic and cultural links and promoting political dialogue on a wide range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. this agreement will help to strengthen regional cohesion, as peru is one of the few latin american countries whose citizens still have to apply for a visa, and will be a rather important factor in bringing european peoples and peruvians closer together.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, in which the european parliament gives its consent to the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver. this agreement is the result of the development of relations between the eu and the republic of peru and is a complementary instrument aimed at strengthening economic and cultural links and promoting political dialogue on a wide range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. this agreement will help to strengthen regional cohesion, as peru is one of the few latin american countries whose citizens still have to apply for a visa, and will be a rather important factor in bringing european peoples and peruvians closer together. as regards the political and institutional situation, the republic of peru is a country with a relatively stable democracy, as is the european union, which defends the principles and values of democracy, good governance, respect for human rights and the rule of law, and which remains a key partner of latin america in this field. human rights and democracy are key elements in the relations between the european union and this andean country. strengthening democracy and human rights remains one of peru's priorities, and the visa liberalisation agreement will help to continue a balanced, sustained and comprehensive political dialogue on human rights and specific issues such as the situation of women.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. the new visa regime provides for visa-free travel for eu citizens when travelling to the territory of peru and for citizens of peru when travelling to the eu, for a period of stay of 90 days in any 180-day period.
in writing. i give my consent to the conclusion of this agreement. in particular, this agreement will provide an opportunity to develop relations between the european union and the republic of peru and to strengthen economic and cultural links, as well as to foster political dialogue on a wide range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. it is worth noting that peru is one of the few countries in latin america whose citizens are still subject to a visa regime, so this agreement will also be one of the factors that will help strengthen the cohesion of the region in order to facilitate the integration of individuals. the visa waiver agreement will promote tourism and contribute to strengthening trade and investment links. it is worth noting that the agreement includes a joint declaration on cooperation in the field of illegal migration.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation because back in october 2014 the european commission adopted a report which examined in detail peru's compliance with the criteria for granting visa-free travel to this country. in may 2015, in the light of the positive outcome of the evaluation, the council decided to authorise the commission to open negotiations for the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the eu and peru. the agreement was signed in march 2016 and has been provisionally applied until now, pending its approval by the european parliament. the visa-free regime allows travellers to stay in the territory of a contracting party for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. the agreement will strengthen economic and cultural links between the eu and peru, promote political dialogue, tourism and contribute to strengthening trade and investment links.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment of the resolution of the european parliament and of the council on the visa waiver for peruvian citizens. the eu-peru agreement on the abolition of short-stay visas will have a positive impact on relations and strengthen political dialogue, especially in the important area of respect for human rights on the south american continent. the agreement will also promote tourism, which will have a positive impact on trade and bilateral investment. this is a very important aspect, since peru has one of the highest rates of economic growth in latin america. the eu is also peru's third largest trading partner, its main export market and its largest investor. the visa-free regime therefore brings great benefits to the european community.
in writing. ‒ the multiple-mode ignition engines (mems) are a diverse range of combustion engines installed in a wide range of machinery, from small hand-held devices, construction machinery and generating sets to cranes, locomotives and inland waterway vessels. these engines are increasing air pollution. the emission limit values for these engines are currently set in directive 97/68/ec, but they need to be amended. this proposal aims to protect human health and the environment and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market for engines installed in non-road mobile machinery. it also seeks to take into account aspects of competitiveness and compliance. in line with eu air quality policy, the aim is to gradually reduce emissions from new engines placed on the market, while replacing older, more polluting engines over time.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the emission limit values for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery. the main objective of this report, as proposed by the commission, is to ensure the right balance between health and environmental issues and the competitiveness of the eu's manufacturing industry, jobs and practical experience. the health and safety of our citizens, especially those who work with the machinery covered by this proposal on a daily basis and are particularly affected by emissions, are the key issues of this proposal. in view of the competition aspects, the rapporteur considers that smes which create a large number of jobs may be vulnerable and should therefore be granted certain advantages. another important objective could be to ensure certainty of long-term planning and a stable regulatory environment for industry. in this respect, this new legislative instrument in the form of a regulation is clearly superior to a directive, which requires time to be transposed into national law, and therefore risks being interpreted differently.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the regulation is very ambitious in terms of environmental protection and public health protection because non-road mobile machinery engines account for about 15% of all nox and 5% of particulate emissions in the eu.
in writing. i support the draft regulation submitted. it is essential to ensure the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital within the internal market. it is therefore essential that the eu applies transparent, simple and consistent rules that provide legal certainty and clarity, to the benefit of both businesses and consumers. in order to achieve sustainable reductions in engine emissions, direct cooperation between manufacturers and related companies and reliable research institutions needs to be continuously strengthened. such cooperation is important for the development of new products and technologies with a positive impact on air quality. it should be noted that in order to reduce the risk of market distortion and consequently the negative effects on health, it is necessary to harmonise the emission limit values for certain categories of engines. in addition, manufacturers must be able to fulfil their warranty obligations properly and to ensure that there is a sufficient number of such engines on the market.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, even though it is not as ambitious as we would like. it should be noted that these engines contribute significantly to air pollution and are responsible for approximately 15% of nitrogen oxide and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the european union. however, this report is a step forward in the fight against air pollution. i am glad that this report shows that air pollution is being looked at in a broader way. efforts are currently being made to reduce pollution in all sectors, including the non-road internal combustion engines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the social inclusion and integration of refugees into the eu labour market. the humanitarian crisis represented by the arrival of refugees constitutes one of the main challenges the european union has to face today. in 2015, a new european agenda on migration was adopted with the aim of addressing the difficult management of an unprecedented influx of people. in this regard, cooperation with third countries, humanitarian aid and development aid are some of the main tools available in addressing the root causes of migration (e.g. conflicts and poverty). this crisis has been made more complex by the high number of children, including unaccompanied children, who are involved. moreover, the crisis is occurring at a time of severe economic conditions in many eu countries, including high unemployment rates. the aim of the report is to outline the issues connected to the refugee crisis and to provide some proposals, recommendations and suggestions for achieving the objective of social inclusion and integration of refugees into the labour market of the eu.
in writing. ‒ with the great numbers of refugees arriving in europe, there is a tremendous need for an appropriate framework for their inclusion in the labour market. we should spare no effort to ensure their social, cultural and economic integration: those migrants who were forced to leave their homes usually suffer from physical and psychological trauma and must be helped. a sense of humanity is crucial and an appreciation of the hardships that migrants have to go through. secondly, with due regard to high rates of unemployment, refugees should be allowed to contribute to the process of reviving the labour market, and here they can be of great help. if refugees are properly trained and educated, demand and supply on europe’s labour market will be met. it is clear that the refugee inclusion process is vital for both migrants and their host countries, and therefore their integration must be properly effected and immediate.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal on the social inclusion and integration of refugees into the labour market. i agree that the refugee crisis is first and foremost a humanitarian crisis of global proportions, but it is also a political crisis, and so policymakers need to take urgent decisive action and long-term measures that respond to the needs of society and the labour market. first, it is necessary to address the root causes of migration: conflict and poverty, through eu external policy instruments such as cooperation with third countries, humanitarian aid and development assistance. it is important to establish a common asylum system without delay in order to improve recognition procedures while ensuring the highest level of protection for refugees and eu citizens. i agree that allowing refugees to work would not only help restore their dignity, but would also be cost-effective - they would be self-sufficient, pay taxes and reduce the cost of refugee maintenance. i also support calls for language and vocational guidance courses for refugees. it is necessary to assess in advance, in a fair, transparent and free manner, the formal and informal skills of refugees and asylum seekers and to recognise and validate their qualifications.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament examines the situation of refugees and their integration into the labour market. managing the refugee crisis is one of the most important challenges facing the european union and its society today. this is not only a humanitarian crisis, but also a political crisis on a global scale. the new european agenda on migration was adopted to overcome the challenges of managing the flow of people arriving - this requires additional strengthening of border management, search and rescue operations, and the renewal of the common european asylum system. efforts are also needed to create the necessary conditions for the integration of asylum seekers and refugees into society. a holistic approach to migration requires that the eu's external policies address the root causes of migration and that internal policies are open and consistent. another set of factors that complicate the social inclusion and labour market integration of refugees is related to the current macroeconomic situation in the european union. record levels of unemployment, poverty, fragmentation of the labour market and slow economic recovery suggest that these can become barriers to the integration and inclusion of refugees. a healthy labour market in the country of arrival is one of the key factors for successful and long-term integration of refugees, according to the data. in addition, reducing social or other support measures would have negative social and political consequences.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the swift integration of refugees through their participation in the labour market and social inclusion will bring benefits for the refugees (economic independence and a sense of belonging and usefulness) and for society as a whole.
in writing. i do not support the motion for a resolution on the social inclusion and integration of refugees into the labour market. it is worth noting that today, even without these things, almost 25% of europeans are at risk of poverty and social exclusion. about 10 percent of them suffer from severe material deprivation. nothing has been done to change the situation, and the question is what benefits the community countries should give to migrants in terms of employment. we should not create labour markets specifically for refugees. each newcomer must submit to the law and order of the particular country. member states shall not be obliged to facilitate the admission of refugee students to educational establishments at all levels or to organise additional classes in the language of the country of origin. it should be noted that a common compulsory asylum system will not solve the existing problems. we must abandon any policy of quotas. it was, is and will be the obvious catalyst for migration to europe. because that's how you send the signal that you're welcome here, you're taken care of.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which discusses the need to do more to integrate refugees into the labour market. the communication also sets out specific measures to be taken: the establishment of a language training system, better access to training, the speedier development of integration plans, etc. one of the most important tasks is the need to establish robust and transparent procedures for the recognition of qualifications acquired abroad, outside the european union. this would allow refugees to better exploit their existing skills in jobs where they already have some professional knowledge. at the same time, the report makes clear that refugees must not be discriminated against or exploited by employers, nor must they be treated worse than local residents. the report also mentions the need for specific efforts to integrate girls and women, in particular through access to formal and non-formal education and home. this would speed up the integration.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate responsibilities. the report welcomes the commission decision to carry out ex ante and ex post sustainability impact assessments (sias) and declares that the human rights impact assessments (hrias) and the sustainability impact assessment should become binding. the report underlines the importance of human rights conditionality in trade agreements and of respect for, and implementation of, the human rights clauses. the commission and the council should promote regular in-depth monitoring of the implementation of the human rights clauses in trade and association agreements, which are also to include chapters on trade and sustainable development. parliament should also be involved at every stage and actively consulted during the drafting, negotiating and implementation of such agreements. the report underlines the importance of corporate social responsibility (csr) provisions. in this regard, the commission should be able to carry out investigations into alleged breaches of csr commitments. the eu should also actively engage with the un on an international treaty to hold transnational companies accountable for human rights abuses and the violation of the environmental standards.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the fight against trafficking in human beings. the trafficking of human beings is a modern kind of slavery and a serious crime which constitutes one of the worst forms of human rights violations. trafficking in human beings represents a highly lucrative business, therefore it is important to fight against the corruption which facilitates it. the eu and its member states shall increase cooperation with third countries and improve the exchange of information with the aim of investigating and combating transnational trafficking. at eu level, the report recognises and supports the work of the eu anti-trafficking coordinator, established to improve coordination and coherence among the eu institutions, agencies and member states and third countries and international bodies, and urges the coordinator to further develop concrete joint action and measures by all these protagonists.
in writing. ‒ cooperation and coordination between member states is crucial in the fight against human trafficking, and this report is an important step in that direction. the report urges the eu and the member states to deal intensively with the crime of human trafficking. this growing illicit industry of human suffering affects all societies in a profound and enduring manner. the trafficking of human beings is a transnational issue of global nature that is a modern form of slavery. to combat this, we need measures that fight the issue at the root causes and global trends. the eu and member states should take necessary efforts to combat forced labour in eu industries abroad, particularly in third countries. international cooperation is crucial in the case of trafficking in human beings, where there is currently an insufficient level of cooperation. the eu anti-trafficking coordinator needs further coordination, joint action, and coherence among the eu institutions, agencies, member states, third countries, and international actors. this report is a great step in the fight against all forms of human trafficking, however, the eu should develop a new post-2016 anti-trafficking strategy with a stronger and more targeted external dimension.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this motion on the fight against human trafficking. trafficking in human beings is one of the most serious human rights violations, as it involves the commoditisation of human beings, is a fundamental and persistent violation of the dignity and rights of victims, and affects entire families and communities. the ilo estimates that illicit annual profits from forced labour, including money laundering, amount to approximately usd 150 billion, with 90% of victims estimated to be exploited in the private sector and two thirds of profits derived from commercial sexual exploitation. i support calls on the commission to assess the use of the internet for trafficking in human beings, in particular sexual exploitation via the internet. it is important that europol step up the fight against trafficking in human beings online. i support calls on the commission and the member states to also extend the definition of trafficking in human beings to include references to new forms of trafficking in human beings by strengthening legal instruments to combat trafficking in human beings. it is also important to review the mandate of the future european public prosecutor's office so that it is empowered to fight against trafficking in human beings once it is established.

first vice-president of the commission. – mr president, i have come here today to listen to parliament’s views on the commission work programme for next year. now, we are just before the time when parliament needs to vote, so that is why the chamber is filling up, and it is quite a sight to see all of you here. i mention this because, all too often in the last couple of months, something seems to have been forgotten, and that is that 751 europeans have been elected to directly represent citizens from 28 different nations in all their diversity, with all their differences and their different outlooks and lives: you all come together here in this chamber to look for majorities to take decisions. that is the essence of representative democracy: that you decide by majority, just as the british people have decided by majority to leave the european union. that decision needs to be respected. but, likewise, those who only shouted during the years they were here in this parliament should have had more respect for the majority in this parliament, whose decisions are just as legitimised by the voters who went to vote for them. and please, i call on all of you, now that i have the opportunity to speak to so many of you, do not let your democratic mandate be ridiculed or diminished. stand up for it. you are the representatives of more than 500 million people. be proud of it, stand up for it and do not let those people tell you do not represent the people. (heckling)is that all you have offer? destroy for the sake of destruction rather than build something for your citizens? (loud applause)if there is one man in our european institutions who has listened very carefully to the majority in this parliament, who has tuned and changed his propositions and his priorities on the basis of a majority in this parliament, it is jean-claude juncker, and he deserves the respect of this parliament and others for this attitude, which is entirely and fundamentally democratic at european level. i repeat: our people, the people you represent, are worried about the future, are concerned about those who represent them, are anxious. if it were only the european institutions they were challenging, that would be wonderful. we could get rid of the institutions and everything would be okay. (interjection from the floor: ‘hear hear!’) but look at what has happened, ‘hear hear!’ look at what is happening now in the uk. look at what is happening to the pound and your economy. are you happy with that? i would not be happy with that, looking back on it. (loud applause)what we have seen is that political choices have real consequences for real people. these are not games we are playing. as politicians you have responsibility. face up to them. do not run away when you are scared of the consequences of your actions. (loud applause)and that, ladies and gentlemen, is what distinguishes jean-claude juncker fundamentally from people like farage and others. when things get tough, he starts working. he puts his back into it. he does not run away. that is the difference between him and you, sir. so yes, we will focus and reorient our work programme on the basis of what a majority in this parliament tells us to do, not on account of those who, because they are too weak to find majorities in a democratic way, always referred to a mythical ‘people’. let democracy work. get the votes. and shouting at me will not make your position stronger. let me end on this, ladies and gentlemen: never be intimidated by big mouths. never be intimidated by insults. listen carefully to the real concerns of our voters. they are not happy with us. we need to change our ways. we need to do better, but walking away is not the answer. providing concrete solutions for concrete problems is the answer, and the commission is your partner to make this happen this year and next year. in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report concerning the measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security across the union. today we have endorsed legislation that will impose security and reporting obligations on service operators in industries such as banking, energy, transport and health and on digital operators like search engines and online marketplaces. the commission proposal introduces obligations for network and information security (nis), in order to create a level playing field and close existing legislative loopholes among eu member states. digital services providers (dsps), as in cloud computing providers, search engines and online market places, will be subject to simplified procedures concerning security requirements. in case of non-compliance by operators or dsps penalties will have to be foreseen in national law. with respect to member states’ obligations, a cooperation group for strategic coordination and a csirt (computer security incident response teams) network for operational cooperation will be established. these rules should help to prevent cyber-attacks on europe’s most important interconnected infrastructures.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this bill to increase cyber resilience. new eu rules require companies in energy, transport, banking, healthcare or other critical sectors to strengthen the resilience of their information systems to cyberattacks. each eu country will have to develop a cybersecurity strategy and appoint an authority responsible for the security of information systems. the eu's network and information security directive aims to increase cooperation between eu countries in the field of cybersecurity and reduce the existing fragmentation. the rules set out the sectors in which companies providing essential services, such as those responsible for electricity or gas supply, air traffic control or financial services, will have to ensure the security of their information systems and report cyber-attacks to the authorities responsible.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which deals with the commission's proposal for a directive on measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems throughout the european union. the objective of the proposed directive is to ensure a high overall level of network and information security (nis). this means enhancing the security of the internet and of the private networks and information systems that support the functioning of our societies and economies. this will be achieved by requiring member states to increase their preparedness and enhance cooperation with each other, and by requiring operators of critical infrastructure such as energy and transport, and key information society services (e.g. trading platforms, social networks, etc.), as well as public administrations to take appropriate action to manage security risks and to inform the national competent authorities of serious incidents. this commission proposal is presented in conjunction with the joint communication from the commission and the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on a european cybersecurity strategy. the aim of the strategy is to ensure a safe and secure digital environment, while upholding and protecting fundamental rights and other core eu values. this proposal is a key part of the strategy. the future strategy will focus on raising awareness, developing cybersecurity products and services, and promoting investment in research and technological development. these actions will be complemented by other actions to promote the fight against cybercrime and to shape the eu's international cybersecurity policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. the aim of the proposed directive is to ensure a high common level of network and information security (nis). this means improving the security of the internet and the private networks and information systems underpinning the functioning of our societies and economies. this will be achieved by requiring the member states to increase their preparedness and improve their cooperation with each other, and by requiring operators of critical infrastructures, such as energy, transport, and key providers of information society services (e-commerce platforms, social networks, etc.), as well as public administrations to adopt appropriate steps to manage security risks and report serious incidents to the national competent authorities.
in writing. i support the report presented, as it is necessary to increase the security of the internet and of the private networks and information systems that support the functioning of our society and economy. it should be noted that information systems may be affected by security incidents such as human error, natural phenomena, technical failures or malicious attacks. these incidents are becoming larger, more frequent and more complex. in addition to being a means of communication without borders, digital information systems are interconnected in all member states and play a crucial role in facilitating the movement of goods, services and persons between countries. a major disruption of these systems in one member state can have repercussions in other member states and across the eu. the resilience and stability of network and information systems are therefore crucial for the implementation of the digital single market and the smooth functioning of the internal market. at present, there is insufficient protection against cis incidents and risks at eu level. existing measures are simply not sufficient to ensure a high overall level of protection in all member states. this may lead to barriers to the internal market, which may result in compliance costs for undertakings operating in more than one member state. effective management of the security of network and information systems requires a global approach at union level, including common minimum requirements for capacity building and planning, information exchange and coordination of actions, and common minimum security requirements for all relevant market participants and public administrations.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation. it is mainly related to the intensification of cyber-attacks. as far back as 2012, a eurobarometer survey revealed that 38% of eu internet users are concerned about the security of online payment systems. in addition, the european commission's public consultation showed that 57% of respondents had experienced attacks on information systems during the year that had seriously affected their business. admittedly, solutions to counter this type of attack are still being sought. this document is just one of the attempts to take the first steps towards a common level of security for eu networks and information systems. despite the importance of this directive, experts acknowledge that the provisions contained in it are unlikely to reduce the number of cyber-attacks or to contribute to genuine security.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at more explicit labelling of energy efficiency. the new rules propose to abandon the misleading a+, a++ or a+++ labelling within five years and replace it with a scale from a to g. most appliances currently meet the highest energy efficiency class a and manufacturers tend to break it down into smaller categories and add advantages such as a+, a++ or a+++ in order to achieve product excellence. this may mislead consumers who expect to buy the most economical device when buying a product in category a. i agree that the product label should be clear and legible, indicating the energy efficiency class and the kilowatt consumption of the appliance. this would allow consumers to make an informed decision before purchasing the desired appliance and contribute to energy savings.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which sets out the european parliament's amendments to the energy efficiency labelling rules, with the aim of abandoning the misleading a+, a++ or a+++ labelling within five years and replacing it with the ag scale. in its report, the parliament notes that most appliances currently meet the highest energy efficiency class a and that, in order to achieve product exclusivity, manufacturers tend to break it down into smaller categories and add bonuses such as a+, a++ or a+++. this may mislead consumers who expect to buy the most economical device when buying a product in category a. the european parliament proposes to return to the ag energy efficiency scale within five years and to reflect this on product labels. they should also indicate the energy consumption of the product in kilowatt hours. in addition, consumers must have the right to return the product to the trader and receive a refund if it is found that the product does not meet the requirements, meps believe. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the revision aims to ensure that consumers make better-informed purchase decisions of energy-efficient products, and thereby reduce energy consumption and associated energy bills (as well as other major environmental impacts of products). the proposed regulation would restore the a-g scale for energy labelling, create a mechanism for rescaling products that can accommodate further improvements in energy efficiency, establish a product database on energy efficiency, and introduce a safeguard procedure to improve national market surveillance.
in writing. i agree with the report. energy labelling is environmentally beneficial because it allows consumers to compare products in terms of their energy efficiency and to make cost-effective and environmentally sound choices. it is therefore essential that a clearer and simpler product information management and labelling system is applied in the eu to ensure consistency and continuity. it is also essential that consumers are provided with more information when choosing a product, which will help them save energy and money. it should be noted that the eu will not be able to function properly as a single market without the common digital database of new energy-saving products that the us, australia and other countries have developed over the past few years. this would allow citizens to play a key role in the eu's transition to a new energy system, as well as facilitate access to information, enhance the ability to monitor market developments in real time and increase the effectiveness of safeguards. by acting as a platform to which 100% of the information relevant to consumers is transferred, updated and freely accessible, the product database will contribute significantly to consumer confidence.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report concerning the european border and coast guard. the schengen area as an area of 26 countries without internal border control in which persons may move freely is rightly considered by many as among the biggest and most visible achievements of european integration. however, this area is challenged by the reintroduction of border controls as a reaction to the secondary movements of irregular migrants. last december, the european commission presented its proposal on the european border and coast guard (ebcg). this proposal has many innovative elements such as the establishment of a vulnerability assessment, the deployment of liaison officers to member states, and the setting up of a rapid reaction pool of 1500 border guards. the creation of the european border and coast guard can ensure a european integrated border management at the external borders of the eu by managing efficiently the crossing of the external borders, by contributing to addressing serious crimes with a cross-border dimension and by ensuring a high level of internal security within the union, while safeguarding the free movement of persons therein.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a european border and coast guard (ebcg) addresses the need for proper control of the schengen external border in order to ensure the high level of security, at the same time protecting the free movement of people within the eu. this concept of the ebcg is a step in the right direction in improving the current border guard frontex and introducing a system of an integrated border management. the proposal foresees a much stronger role of the agency in the field of return, the strengthening of its capacity (staff, budget, equipment), increased cooperation with third countries, and the establishment of a european cooperation on coast guard functions. i voted for this report as it will enhance the solidarity between the member states, reinforce integration regarding border management and contribute to preventing crisis situations at the external border. without internal borders, the external borders of the schengen area should be a shared responsibility among all member states. this proposal should fix the previous weaknesses of the external border and allow a return to the schengen area without internal border controls.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to establish a european border and coast guard agency. it will be composed of representatives of frontex and national border protection authorities, who can provide emergency border assistance, for example, if a country is experiencing high migratory pressure or is threatened by the schengen area. the new agency will be supported by a pool of national border experts, which can be activated at the request of an eu country or by a decision of the eu council. the implementation plan for this decision shall be approved by the eu state concerned and by the agency itself before the agency's teams are deployed. if an eu country facing migratory pressure does not agree to the eu council's decision to send the teams of the said services to its territory and this threatens the schengen area, other eu countries will be able to resume border checks with that country.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament sets out its position on the commission's proposal for a regulation establishing a european border and coast guard agency. in recent years, the european union has been under enormous pressure at its external borders, as the massive mixed migration flows across the eu's external borders, followed by intensive secondary movements, have shown that the existing structures at eu and member state level are not adequate to deal with the challenges posed by such large influxes. it is therefore necessary to ensure european integrated border management at the external borders of the eu in order to manage migration effectively and to ensure a high level of security in the eu while maintaining the free movement of persons within it. in addition, this regulation extends the competences of frontex, the external border protection agency of the eu member states, and renames frontex as the european border and coast guard agency. the main tasks of the european border and coast guard agency are to develop an operational and technical strategy for the implementation of integrated border management at eu level, to monitor the effectiveness of border control at the external borders of the member states, to carry out vulnerability assessments and to ensure that national authorities address any deficiencies in external border management, and so on.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the eu needs a real common border and coast guard system for our common european borders, otherwise schengen will remain under pressure. the refugee crisis needs common european solutions and common border management is a key element to put a stop to the chaos at our borders. although this proposal is only a first step towards fully fledged european border management, it is a step in the right direction.
in writing. given the current situation, it is essential to improve the cooperation and coordination of activities between the relevant eu agencies in order to increase the synergy of their respective services, in order to provide national authorities with coastal functions with more efficient and cost-effective multi-purpose services. however, the new regulation must not in any way infringe the sovereignty of the member states. the activities of the agency shall be duly aligned with the national interests of the member states before any action is taken. no decisions may be taken unilaterally without the consent of the member state concerned. it is essential to ensure that the agency's operational plan is not implemented without the approval of the state concerned. it should also be empowered to issue instructions to the teams in all cases.
in writing. ‒ i voted on this report, in which the european parliament sets out its position on the establishment of a european border and coast guard agency. i think it is clear that europe's borders must be protected. the influx of migrants has revealed europe's vulnerability and the inability of member states to respond effectively and quickly to such challenges. on the other hand, the final test has become much weaker following the negotiations with the council. more importantly, this document states that member states will in principle not be able to refuse the agency's services even if they so wish, as otherwise it may be threatened with the return of border checks, even if the country is part of the schengen area. the agency is also authorised to operate in third countries, but it is not specified how legal problems related to such activities will be avoided.
in writing. while the newly defined areas of competence represent a major step forward, they should be seen as the first steps towards a fully independent, integrated, eu-led, eu-wide border and coast guard force, funded by the eu budget and with operational autonomy. when this regulation is finally adopted, member states and all eu institutions should give a clear political commitment to do so.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the proposal concerning the european maritime safety agency. the purpose of this proposal reinforcing european co-operation on coastguard functions is to improve cooperation and coordination between the relevant eu agencies in order to enhance synergies between their respective services, thus allowing them to provide more efficient and cost-effective multipurpose services to national authorities carrying out coastguard functions. the main tasks of the european maritime safety agency will be the following: to provide valuable information in order to improve surveillance of the external borders of the european union; to collect all relevant maritime data on human activity at sea in one place, offering a “one-stop shop” solution which feeds other authorities at national and eu level with this data; as well as to increase the collective skills and capacity for coastguard functions and to assist them to collaborate and act jointly.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines the commission's proposal for a regulation to establish a european maritime safety agency. there are currently over 300 civil and military authorities in the member states, which carry out coast guard functions in the fields of safety of navigation, security, search and rescue, border control, fisheries control, customs control, general law enforcement and environmental protection. in carrying out these functions, national authorities are assisted by a number of eu agencies, in particular the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union (frontex), the european maritime safety agency and the european fisheries control agency. the objective of this initiative is to improve cooperation at european level in the performance of coast guard functions: to this end, it is envisaged to develop cross-sectoral cooperation between the european border and coast guard agency, the european maritime safety agency (emsa) and the european fisheries control agency (efca) in order to improve the synergies between the activities of these agencies in order to provide national authorities with a more efficient and cost-effective multi-purpose service for their coastal functions. the objective of this legislative act, which strengthens cooperation at european level in the exercise of coastal protection functions, is to improve the cooperation and coordination of activities between the relevant eu agencies in order to increase the synergy of their respective services, in order to provide national authorities with coastal functions with more efficient and cost-effective multi-purpose services.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the european parliament expresses its concern at japan's decision to resume whaling for the 2015/16 season. the european parliament supports a global moratorium on commercial whaling and a ban on international commercial trade in whale products, urges an end to unjustified whaling for scientific purposes and supports the establishment of whale sanctuaries in large ocean and marine areas where whaling would be banned indefinitely. parliament regretted that japan had clearly ignored the ruling of the international court of justice in its decision to resume whaling and considered that the hunt violated the standards of the international whaling commission and international law and was detrimental to the protection of biodiversity and marine ecosystems. real research doesn't need to involve large-scale whale killing. parliament therefore called on japan to immediately cease whaling activities and called on the commission, the european external action service (eeas) and the council to urge japan to take international commitments on the protection of marine mammals. regrets that japan has not yet reconsidered its decision despite the diplomatic demarche and widespread international protests, and calls on the eu and its member states to do everything possible to resolve the issue through political dialogue and the international whaling commission;

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report concerning the implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the eu acceded to the un convention in december 2010. with its ratification, the eu is now subject to scrutiny by the committee on the rights of persons with disabilities. the crpd covers a large range of rights, spanning all areas of life, some of which fall outside of the competence of the eu. therefore, member states are required to equally implement the convention at all levels, including regional and national. there is no hierarchy of human rights, and disability-based discrimination must be tackled; this is especially important for women and children with disabilities, older persons and individuals who have complex support needs, including those with intellectual and psycho-social disabilities.
‒ the eu acceded to the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities in 2010. this convention is the first (and so far only) international human rights treaty that the eu has ratified as a single entity. the eu, like the other parties to the convention, was required to submit a preliminary report on the implementation of the convention upon accession. the purpose of this report is to examine first the issues raised in the concluding observations of the report. the eu institutions themselves are given the greatest attention, as they are to be the model for how the convention should be implemented. recalls that the full inclusion of persons with disabilities is not only a right and an entitlement of the persons concerned, but also a benefit for society as a whole, as it can benefit from the values and different capacities that these persons provide; the inclusion of people with disabilities in society, regardless of the social, economic, political or cultural status of the country, is not only a developmental issue but also a human rights issue. i support calls on parliament, the council and the commission to fully implement the recommendations of the un committee on the rights of persons with disabilities and to ensure that these conventions are respected in all future legislation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it supports the implementation of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the european union acceded to the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities in december 2010 and was the first regional integration organisation to sign the convention. the eu was required to submit an initial report after accession, as were the other parties to the convention, and subsequent periodic reports every four years. the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is different from other human rights treaties in that it involves people with disabilities and their representative organisations from the very beginning of its drafting. to this end, the european parliament's joint working group on the advocacy of the rights of persons with disabilities, in cooperation with the european disability forum, held a joint working group meeting to hear the views of the european disability forum and its member organisations. their written and oral contributions are included in the working document and the draft report. the convention covers a wide range of rights, such as social inclusion, economic rights, the guarantee of freedom of movement for eu citizens and other rights relating to all areas of life, some of which fall outside the eu's remit. it is therefore necessary that member states also implement this crucial convention at all levels, including regional and national.

commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it must be admitted that member states want to enjoy the privileges of free movement of goods when exporting their own products, but when it comes to granting the same rights to goods from other countries, goodwill often evaporates. there is a constant effort to create additional rules, requirements, that would restrict the entry of products from other countries into that country's market. so basically, we want to play an unequal game. a good example is the way in which the united kingdom adopted the colours of the traffic lights for food labelling a few years ago. at first sight, the system seemed useful in that it informed consumers about the fat, sugar and salt content of products. however, synthetic materials were ignored. therefore, products with a higher fat content made from natural products would be assessed less favourably than those made from lighter but synthetic materials. the question therefore arises whether the intention was really to protect the health of consumers or to remove certain products from the market. the system was also intended to reduce sales of products from other countries, since consumers often preferred an even less well-reviewed brand to one they were familiar with, rather than one they were unfamiliar with. i am in favour of various labelling initiatives which help to attract consumers, but the development of these systems must also take account of the specificities of food packaging in other countries. i believe that the european commission should be more active in this area and ensure that all parties are informed in advance of any changes to the labelling of a country and are able to make their own proposals.

in writing. the creation of an eu single energy market is one of the eu's top priorities, not only in the field of energy itself, but also in general in terms of increasing the eu's competitiveness, resilience to various crises and in the implementation of the eu's 2030 climate change and energy targets. a well-designed and properly implemented european energy market has the potential to significantly enhance europe's energy security and independence, in particular from the monopolistic external suppliers on which the union is still dependent. the creation of a genuine energy market requires the urgent need to dismantle the remaining eu energy islands and integrate them into the european energy networks in the fields of gas and electricity. the development of a new electricity market model requires a greater health of electricity and gas systems, which in the future will allow the eu and individual member states to become more resilient and to respond more quickly and effectively to supply disruptions.

the rapporteur. thank you, madam president. first of all, i would like to thank co-rapporteur tatjana ždanka and all the shadow rapporteurs for our joint work, because in fact our report is a contribution of the european parliament, a response to the action plan on work-life balance solutions, especially for families with children, published by the commission in summer 2015, and a contribution to the public consultation and the consultation with the social partners launched by the commission. the question is indeed very important and we expect to receive legislative proposals from the commission, because this is a very topical issue in the member states as well, since it affects every one of our citizens. in june this year, the council adopted conclusions on gender equality, stressing the need to adopt and strengthen legal instruments that would provide a real framework and equal opportunities for women and men to reconcile work, private and family life. it is good that we all want and strive for a common goal in this area. in the report, we therefore call on the commission to present as soon as possible an ambitious new proposal for a maternity leave directive, as well as a carers' leave directive, which would enable family members to look after dependent family members, disabled or elderly family members and provide them with a certain level of social protection. we also call on the commission to come forward with a proposal for a paternity leave directive providing for at least two weeks of fully paid parental leave and finally to review the childcare leave directive and extend the minimum paid leave from four to six months, as women must in fact participate in the labour market, as the integration of women into the labour market is a key instrument in the fight against poverty and social exclusion. but if we are to encourage women to work and to stay in the labour market as long as possible, we must also provide them with the best possible conditions for reconciling work and private life. it is also important to emphasise that better coordination, coherence and access to the different types of leave in the member states would certainly increase employment. we must also take into account that europe is ageing rapidly, and that better work-life balance would enable parents to devote more time to their families, while also boosting fertility. it is often the case that if families, especially women, cannot balance work and childcare, they are not willing to have more children or choose not to have any at all. it is therefore not surprising that the european union is experiencing a declining birth rate. it is therefore essential to create a family-friendly environment at the workplace and for employers to guarantee flexible working relationships and additional social guarantees for families raising children. we must ensure gender equality and a fair distribution of family responsibilities. unfortunately, it is still the prevailing view that the problem of work-life balance is more often highlighted as a women's problem, as they bear the greatest burden of family care. we also strongly urge the commission to introduce, during the semester, certain target indicators for the care of elderly and other dependent persons, similar to the barcelona objectives, and to this end we call on eurostat and eurofound to collect relevant data and carry out research in this area. so there is no one-size-fits-all solution to work-life balance and it is up to each person to find the right thank you. thank you. colleagues, we can rejoice that the g20 meeting took place in china. unfortunately, it has not been marked by any major agreements or decisions. the real beneficiary of this outcome is its host, china, which has used the g20 format as yet another opportunity to promote beijing's economic model of the world, its 'one belt, one road' strategy, its strategy of de-atlanticisation. at that time, canada applied to join the aiib, the asian infrastructure investment bank, and now, of the major nations, only the united states and japan are not members of this chinese-led credit institution. the european union, beset by many problems, is not giving sufficient attention to the obor strategy and its possible consequences. finally, i should like to welcome the fact that the final communication also devotes considerable attention to the problem of antimicrobial resistance, with the aim of involving the world health organisation, the fao, the food and agriculture organisation of the united nations, the oecd and, in general, raising the issue to the level of the united nations.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy and research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation (ris3). research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation are an ex-ante conditionality for the allocation of the european structural and investment (esi) funds. smart specialisation combines and brings together different policies, including those for entrepreneurship, education and innovation, in order for regions to identify and select priority areas for their development and related investments by focusing on their strengths and comparative advantages and contributes to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. the s3 platform, located at the jrc in seville, plays a key role in advising regions and setting benchmarks on their innovation strategies, helping lagging regions and enhancing multi-level governance and synergies between regions, by providing information, methodologies, expertise and advice to national and regional policymakers. the report stresses that there is a still limited role for civil society, which must be more actively involved, a lack of interregional cooperation and of synergies across esi funds and other eu funds. ris3 strategies have to be well implemented and improved in order to tackle the innovation gap and boost jobs in europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the cohesion policy and the research and innovation strategies for the smart specialisation initiative (ris3). ris3 strategies are an important tool to address the innovation gap in europe and to boost job creation and economic growth. i agree that the authorities should pay particular attention to monitoring and reviewing strategies in order to achieve high results and to increase interregional cooperation as much as possible in the development of large-scale projects that create added value for the economy.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this report because it is the parliament's position on cohesion policy and research and innovation strategies for the smart specialisation initiative. the strengthening of research, technological development and innovation is one of the investment priorities under the european regional development fund 2014-2020. however, support for innovation varies widely across the eu, particularly in terms of the use of knowledge and technology to foster innovation. for the first time in this programming period, member states are obliged to develop national and regional smart specialisation strategies involving national and regional managing authorities and higher education institutions, industry and social partners in the entrepreneurship process. in this report, parliament therefore underlines that the aim of these strategies is to ensure knowledge-based sustainable growth, sustainable development and high-quality jobs in all regions, not only in developed areas but also in transition regions, as well as in less developed and rural regions and islands. parliament also calls for full compliance with the new ex ante provisions on the conditions for the allocation of esi funds to ensure that the smart specialisation strategy works.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. ris3 strategies are a valuable tool to tackle the innovation gap, and boost jobs and growth in europe. simplification, as well as coordination of the existing programmes, is also essential in contributing to a good implementation of those strategies in the years to come.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which discusses the benefits of cohesion policy and research and innovation strategies and the key challenges in developing them. it should be noted that these strategies are important because they can help to address the innovation gap in europe and boost job creation and economic growth. however, not everything has been done in the area of cohesion policy. increased interregional cooperation is necessary, especially when large projects with economic added value are being implemented. equally important, the document suggests that better coordination at all levels of governance can be achieved by promoting a top-down vision of regional strategies. i think that's the kind of approach that can lead to much better results.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on european territorial cooperation (etc). etc so far has made a significant contribution to strengthening the eu’s objective of territorial cohesion through integrating diverse sectorial policies on a territorial scale. however, the etc budget of eur 10.1 billion represents only 2.8% of the total cohesion policy budget; therefore, an increased budget for etc in the next programming period will boost the added value of cohesion policy. the report also calls for greater respect for article 174 tfeu on territorial cohesion (rural areas, islands, cross-border and mountains regions, outermost regions). the report underlines the lack of reliable data on cross-border cooperation and thus calls on the commission, eurostat and other managing authorities to cooperate with the aim to set up common criteria and a common database. the etc programmes have proved to be effective; however, their potential should be further developed in areas beyond regional policy such as the single market, the digital agenda, employment, mobility, energy, research, education, culture, health and the environment. the report calls on the commission and the member states to consider preserving etc as an important instrument.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to further promote european territorial cooperation (etc) activities, which has become one of the two equivalent objectives of cohesion policy for 2014-2020. the eit is an effective tool for developing potential in areas such as the single market, the digital agenda, employment, mobility, energy, research, education, health and environmental protection, and it is therefore necessary to maintain the eit as an important tool beyond 2020 and to substantially increase its budget.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is the parliament's position on european territorial cooperation, best practice and innovative measures. the overall objective of european territorial cooperation is to reduce the impact of national borders in order to reduce regional disparities, remove remaining barriers to investment and cooperation across borders, strengthen cohesion and promote sustainable economic, social, cultural and territorial development throughout the union. unfortunately, today, not enough citizens of the european union are still taking full advantage of the opportunities offered by the eu's internal market and free movement. the european parliament therefore stressed that, for the period 2014-2020, approximately 41% of the european regional development fund will be invested in measures to improve the environment, 27% in the promotion of smart growth, including research and innovation, 13% in promoting inclusive growth through employment, education and training activities, and 33 programmes will generally aim to improve connectivity between different countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. european territorial cooperation represents high value for money and has future potential beyond regional policy. it makes a significant contribution to boosting integrated and sustainable territorial development, including implementation and dissemination of integrated approaches, development of governance approaches, harmonisation of planning instruments, administrative procedures and legal provisions across borders.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which discusses best practices and instruments for european territorial cooperation. the impact of european territorial cooperation has a high economic value. at the same time, it is a potential for future projects. the communication therefore calls on the european commission and the member states to work towards preserving the era as an important, positive instrument in the process of european integration and in cohesion policy beyond 2020. however, the management and implementation of eib programmes and projects must become less bureaucratic in the future. at the same time, the private sector contribution to the implementation of the etf is still lacking. it is therefore necessary to develop financial instruments that allow for the involvement of private stakeholders and encourage public-private partnerships.
