in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report concerning statistics on natural gas and electricity prices. since the 1970s the commission has been collecting data on natural gas and electricity prices. in 1990 the council adopted the directive to define the procedure to improve the transparency of gas and electricity prices charged to industrial end-users. according to this directive, for household and final non-household consumers, the collection of data has been done by national authorities on a voluntary basis. i support the proposal to transform the voluntary basis into a mandatory one as serious problems in the data collection occurred as has been reported by several member states.
in writing. ‒ i did not vote for the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is the parliament's position on the future eu regulation on european gas and electricity price statistics. since the 1980s, the european commission has been collecting data on natural gas and electricity prices. in 1990, the council adopted a directive defining a procedure to increase the transparency of gas and electricity prices for industrial end-users but not for household end-users. the collection and publication of data is the responsibility of eurostat. in 2007, the methodology was improved to take account of liberalised energy markets. at the same time, data on natural gas and electricity prices to final household customers were collected on a voluntary basis and the response rate was 100%. the aim of the regulation is to make the voluntary approach mandatory in order to avoid problems in collecting data, as reported by some member states. this step is necessary to avoid a significant deterioration in the quality of the electricity and natural gas price data surveys and to continue to aim for high market share and high quality of the price data.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the price collection is supposed to not lead to an additional burden for the reporting authorities and the price data will continue to be collected by the competent national authorities. this report aims to clarify the goals, facilitate certain provisions for the reporting authorities and the companies which have to provide the data, as well as to avoid misunderstandings which – in the worst case – would lead to incomparable data sets.
in writing. it is desirable that the collection of price data does not become an additional burden for reporting authorities and that price data continue to be collected by the competent national authorities. the report aims to clarify the objectives, to facilitate some provisions applicable to reporting authorities and companies that are required to provide data and to avoid misunderstandings that could, in the worst case, lead to inconsistencies in the data sets.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on a new energy market design. the report aims to strengthen the internal market for energy and to allow electricity to move freely to where it is most needed, to reap maximum benefits from cross-border competition and provide the right signals and incentives to drive the right investments. the electricity market should enhance regional cooperation on all dimensions of energy supply and demand, and should focus on improved, more decentralised and more flexible markets, in order to ensure a well-regulated, market-based system, which is capable of delivering on all of the eu’s established energy and climate goals for 2030. the report also considers that all member states have to implement fully the third energy package and to be more proactively involved in designing a flexible and decentralised internal market on electricity. furthermore, renewables need to be fully integrated into the electricity system by ensuring that markets are fit for renewables, promoting their participation in electricity markets on an equal footing with conventional generation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the development of a new energy market model. on 15 july 2015, the communication on the single european market was published and a public consultation on the structure of the new electricity market model was launched. in the energy sector, europe faces challenges including: increased dependence on oil and gas imports in recent years, lack of diversification, high energy prices influenced by high tariffs, overall increasing global energy demand, threats to the security of producing and transit countries, the fight against climate change, slow progress in energy efficiency, increased share of energy from renewable sources, integration and interconnection of energy markets and market distortions due to different support schemes. i therefore support the need for better integration and coordination of the energy market, which will make it easier to achieve the common european objectives of ensuring a secure, cost-effective and environmentally friendly energy supply.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is the report in which parliament spoke about the future model of the european electricity market. the european energy policy is to ensure the functioning of the energy market and the security of energy supply, to promote savings through more efficient use of energy, to develop renewable forms of energy and to connect energy networks. however, several member states are projecting a shortage of generation capacity, which could lead to a power outage in the near future, unless the necessary back-up mechanisms are put in place. closer cooperation at regional level is therefore essential and should contribute to enhancing market integration at european level. the commission should also be able to provide the necessary information to the member states to enable them to assess the impact of the measures taken on the energy market. however, parliament called for the regulatory framework of european markets to be adjusted to increase the share of renewable energy and close the existing cross-border regulatory gaps.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. improved integration and coordination of energy markets means that there are many opportunities to achieve the common european goal of a secure, affordable, environmentally-sound energy supply. predictable energy prices and security of supply are indispensable in particular for maintaining domestic standards of living and ensuring job security at energy-intensive companies.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the new energy union strategy is even more beneficial for energy consumers, offering them more opportunities to participate in energy markets and ensuring better consumer protection.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the eu strategy on heating and cooling. in the eu, almost 50% of the eu’s final energy demand is used for heating and cooling, of which 80% is used in buildings. the share of primary energy from fossil fuels in heating and cooling remains very high at 75% and presents a major barrier to decarbonisation, thereby accelerating climate change and causing significant harm to the environment. the heating and cooling sector should reflect the 2015 paris agreement on climate change (cop21) and be compatible with the eu’s energy and climate goal of 100% cent renewables by 2050 the latest. this issue affects in particular some eu member states (mediterranean countries) more than others. in order to tackle this issue, the energy efficiency of buildings must be improved and the use of renewables (including solar energy) must be increased. reversible heat pumps may play an important role since they are energy efficient and the re-use of waste heat and cold generated by industry should be encouraged.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu's heating and cooling strategy. the eu heating and cooling strategy is an integral part of the energy union strategy and the heating and cooling sector is therefore crucial to the achievement of the eu's energy and climate targets for 2020, 2030 and 2050, as well as to the objectives of increasing the security of energy supply. in addition, the new member states that joined the eu after 2004 have the greatest potential for efficiency gains in the area of thermal renovation of buildings. i therefore support the need to increase funding for work on the thermal regeneration of entire settlements. this should be considered as a priority, in particular because the owners of the buildings concerned cannot cover the costs and the state support is not sufficient.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this report because it was the one in which parliament spoke on the strategy for heating and cooling buildings. heating and cooling accounts for almost 50% of the eu's final energy demand, 80% of which is used in buildings, and each additional percentage of energy saved would reduce gas imports by 2.6%. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of energy from renewable sources, such as solar panels, solar water heating and solar thermal systems. the report also highlights that the share of renewable energy sources has been slow to increase, but that there is still a huge potential at all levels and that it should be exploited in the member states. parliament welcomed the commission communication on the eu heating and cooling strategy, which represents an important step towards a holistic approach to the restructuring of the heating and cooling sector in the european union and sets out priority areas for action.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. there needs to be a substantial increase in the funding for work on the thermal renovation of entire housing estates, especially those built using large-panel system building methods. at least 25% of the european energy efficiency and renewable energy fund needs to be set aside for this purpose. this objective must be given high priority, particularly since on the whole the owners of the buildings concerned are unable to meet the costs involved and support from the state is insufficient.
in writing. ‒ the i support the report by the ep, which proposes a substantial increase in funding for the thermal renovation of entire settlements, especially those built using large-scale structures. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. this objective must be considered as a major priority, as the owners of such buildings cannot cover the associated costs and the state support is insufficient. i also support the report's suggestion that the obsolete boiler plants in the settlements should be replaced as soon as possible by small but highly efficient cogeneration plants.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. it contains some very good ideas, such as emphasising the need for energy efficiency, encouraging the renovation of buildings, calling for specific solutions to the problems of rural buildings, which are often older, less energy efficient, less healthy and less thermal comfortable. however, it was decided to exclude important green proposals from the report, which is very vague about the development and integration of renewable energy sources into the common system. the commission also rejected proposals for stricter regulation of waste energy conversion, more efficient energy production and decentralised energy production.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on enhancing the competitiveness of smes. under the theme ‘competitiveness of smes’ the esi funds have allocated more than eur 63 billion (plus eur 31 billion of national co-financing for a total amount of eur 94 billion) in the 2014-2020 programme. in the eu there are 23 million smes, which account for around 99% of all businesses, make a fundamental contribution to economic growth, social cohesion, innovation and high-quality job creation, providing over 100 million jobs. however, only a small percentage of the eu’s smes are currently able to identify and exploit the opportunities offered by international trade, trade agreements and the global value chains, and only 13% of them have been active at international level outside the eu over the past three years. while voting in favour of this report i also call for a less regulated access to funding. i also invite the commission and the member states to ensure enhanced coordination and consistency among all eu investment policies targeted at smes and member states to exchange data and best practices. i also encourage the european commission to make serious efforts and to encourage the long-awaited internationalisation of smes.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the communication on the implementation of the thematic objective of improving the competitiveness of smes referred to in article 9 (3) of the general regulation. the economic and financial crisis has increased poverty and social exclusion, as well as long-term unemployment, youth unemployment and social inequality in many member states, and therefore smes have a vital role to play in promoting european recovery. each european structural and investment (esi) fund supports 11 thematic objectives each. by focusing support on themes, the operational programmes were better tailored to a specific number of strategic objectives, in particular those relating to the potential of smes, including micro-enterprises, to boost growth and create high-quality jobs. however, while smes are crucial to the success of cohesion policy, they face a number of problems - legal, institutional and technical. i therefore agree that the obstacles to smes that arise must be removed and that the support provided by the esi funds must be further strengthened.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is the parliament's view on the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the european union. there are 23 million smes in the eu today, representing about 99% of all businesses. they contribute substantially to economic growth, social cohesion, innovation and high-quality job creation: smes provide over 100 million jobs, or 2 out of 3 private sector jobs, and have an employment growth rate twice that of larger companies. and yet smes that could qualify for assistance from the esi funds are particularly adversely affected by the complex and volatile rules and the associated bureaucratic burden, and in particular by the fact that the administrative costs are completely disproportionate in terms of the funding allocated, the time taken to process applications for funding and the need for advance payments. in this report, parliament therefore calls on the commission and the member states to take account of the added value of smes' projects in terms of development and innovation in traditional sectors, since this would not only create jobs but also preserve the specific character of local and regional businesses, while respecting the principles of sustainability.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. improving resource efficiency in smes offers enormous potential for the reduction of production costs and for productivity gains. a better use of resources is calculated to represent an overall savings potential of eur 630 billion per year for european industry. smes need a favourable business environment in which green ideas can be easily developed, financed and brought to the market.
in writing. i call on the commission and the member states to urgently find a long-term solution to the accumulated regional policy arrears and to properly apply the late payments directive (2011/7/eu) in order to ensure that smes, as project partners, do not lose interest in participating in support programmes and projects during the current programming period due to late payments; i also note that a more consistent compliance with this directive, which, inter alia, requires public authorities to make payments for their purchased goods and services within 30 days, would contribute to the stabilisation and growth of smes.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on the eu trust fund for africa. launched at the valletta summit on migration on 12 november 2015, the eutf aims to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration by promoting resilience, economic opportunities, equal opportunities, security and development. it has been conceived in order to assist 23 countries across three african regions (the horn of africa; the sahel and lake chad basin; and north africa) that contain some of the most fragile african countries, which are affected by migration as countries of origin, transit or destination. the european union contribution amounts to eur 1.8 billion. the report considers that the eutf should contribute to the strengthening and improvement of local public services (e.g. social services, health, education, nutrition, culture) and that civil society and ngos should be actively involved. i would like to underline that the rules and criteria that govern development aid for projects financed by the eutf must be set according to the respect and promotion of human rights. it is crucially important that the commission monitors how the eutf funds are employed and allocated. parliament’s scrutiny powers over the fund are to be increased.

in writing. ‒ i have expressed my support to the report concerning labour market conditions favourable for work-life balance. in 2015 the european commission launched a public consultation titled ‘a new start to address the challenges of work-life balance faced by working families’. despite the recognition, as a fundamental right, of the reconciliation of professional, private and family life in the last decades, the eu legal and policy framework needs to be updated. i support the objective of the commission which is to increase the participation of women in the labour market in order to allow for parents with children and/or other dependent relatives to better balance family and work life, to allow for greater sharing of care responsibilities between women and men, and to strengthen gender equality in the labour market. i would like to take this opportunity to call on the commission and the member states to take necessary measures in order to promote equality between women and men at work and to ensure equal earnings and equal career opportunities. in the near future the commission should present a proposal for a revised maternity leave directive, bring forward a paternity leave directive and a carers’ leave directive as well as present an implementation report of the parental leave directive.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the creation of favourable conditions for work-life balance in the labour market. the need to modernise the work-life balance system at eu level is evident. society is undergoing demographic change, unemployment is still a major problem and childbearing continues to have an extremely negative impact on women's employment. i therefore agree that it is necessary to promote employment, to provide children with quality pre-school education and care and to provide all opportunities for leisure activities. in addition, an appropriate work-life policy will help to ensure the safety and quality of life of dependent persons who are elderly, disabled or suffering from chronic illnesses.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this report because, first of all, we must also take account of the fact that europe is rapidly ageing. a better work-life balance would enable parents to devote more time to their families and would encourage fertility. it is often the case that when families, and especially when women, cannot balance work and childcare, they are either unwilling to have more children or choose not to have any at all. it is no wonder, then, that many developed countries are now experiencing a declining birth rate. it is therefore essential to create a family-friendly environment at the workplace and for employers to guarantee flexible working relationships and additional social guarantees for families raising children. the commission will also be supporting the development of the european union's new strategy for the prevention of and fight against drug trafficking, which will be based on the european strategy for the prevention of drug abuse and trafficking in persons. it is also important to encourage fathers (and men) to take paternity and parental leave, as this will help to achieve gender equality in the labour market and encourage women to be more active in the workforce. thus, there is no one-size-fits-all solution to reconciling work, personal and family life, and the right balance needs to be found for each person to meet professional, personal and family needs.

thank you, madam chairman. mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i have to say that i am very pleased with the commission's decision. i agree with many of the points made in this report. but i would point out that we should not overdo it, especially with transport companies. the exploitation of workers is a recurring phenomenon. it is clear that preventing such abuses is very difficult, especially since workers who are driven by crisis, poverty or other reasons often agree to all the conditions of their employer. these people rarely report violations to the authorities, for fear of losing their jobs. complicating matters further is the fact that some companies are registered in one country but actually operate in another. we must protect workers, but we cannot create a system that prevents business from competing. for example, we cannot force a lithuanian transport company to pay a truck driver a huge german salary just because he loads and unloads goods in this country, even though that driver is already earning a salary higher than the average lithuanian salary. thank you!
in writing. the annual speech by european commission president jean-claude juncker raised the question of whether we would hear proposals to tackle europe's problems, or whether the speech would be a 'day-to-day' one. the final result is somewhere in the middle. i think too much attention is being paid to current eu affairs: tax policy, the development of the telecommunications market, talk of the importance of investment or reducing unemployment. the president of the commission has certainly sought to set the tone for his work, but it is worth looking at the future from the other side. wouldn't the state cut all other jobs if it lost a fifth of the land that generates its economy? perhaps the comparison is too graphic, but this is the state of affairs we are talking about after brexit. this is not only an economic challenge, but also a political one, as more countries, or a significant number of their citizens, are eager to follow in the footsteps of the united kingdom. in his messages, mr juncker seems to have sought a balance between nation states and supranational institutions: he said that the path to eu integration was not aimed at the united states of europe, he stressed the importance of voluntary solidarity in the refugee crisis, but also spoke of the need for greater integration in areas that until now have remained largely within the competence of national states. i was surprised by the call not to criticise the commission's work and not to seek its role in the challenges that arise. i believe that it is raising questions and answering them, rather than fearing responsibility, that can help solve europe's problems.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the protocol amending the eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons. following the rejection of accession to the eea agreement in 1992, the eu and switzerland signed a number of bilateral agreements. the agreement on the free movement of persons gave citizens of the contracting parties the right to enter, live and work in each other’s territories by reciprocally abolishing most of the restrictions. this agreement is the only one that did not automatically extend to new eu members, and a protocol thus needs to be signed whenever new countries become part of the eu. protocol iii was initiated after the accession of croatia in july 2013. the swiss referendum of 9 february 2014 “against mass immigration” sparked a reaction by the eu, with the suspension of bilateral negotiations on several subjects. on 4 march 2016 protocol iii was signed. under the protocol, for a period of seven years from its entry into force, switzerland may limit the access of croatian citizens to the labour market. during the last two years of this transition period, the restrictions must be accepted by the switzerland-eu joint committee. i fully welcome this decision of the european parliament.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation on the protocol to the eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons. following the accession of croatia to the eu in 2013, the preparation of protocol 1 on the free movement of persons was started. however, the protocol was suspended after an anti-immigration referendum in switzerland in 2014. however, in 2016, the eu and switzerland signed protocol 3 extending the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. i support protocol 3 because i believe it will bring economic, political and cultural benefits to both sides.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its consent to the conclusion of the protocol to the agreement between the eu and the swiss confederation on the free movement of persons, on the granting of the status of contracting party to the eu accession of the republic of croatia. the eu and its 28 member states are switzerland's most important partners, due to their geographical and cultural proximity and, in particular, their political and economic importance. the eu has concluded a wide range of agreements with switzerland, which has closer ties to it than any other country outside the european economic area (eea). switzerland is the eu's fourth largest trading partner (after the united states, china and russia), and the eu is switzerland's largest trading partner. over a million eu citizens live in switzerland, and another 230 000 cross the border every day to go to work. there are about 430 000 swiss citizens living in the eu. the accession of romania, bulgaria and croatia has further expanded the single market (now comprising almost 505 million people) and made it an even more important partner for switzerland.
in writing. ‒ the i support the protocol to the eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons, which should have been legally adjusted following croatia's accession to the eu. the aim of this agreement was to establish rules in the eu and switzerland equivalent to those laid down in community law, allowing entry, residence, work, self-employment, study, entitlement to social protection and access to the same living, employment and working conditions as nationals of that state. furthermore, the aim of the agreement was also to facilitate the provision of services in the territory of the parties to the agreement. the agreement contained certain transitional provisions, gradually allowing all eu and swiss residents to enjoy the right of free movement.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the economic partnership agreement (epa) between the eu and the sadc epa states. on 11 june 2016, the eu and six members – botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, south africa and swaziland – of the southern african development community (sadc) signed the economic partnership agreement (epa). angola is the only country that is not part of the epa, but as provided for in a clause of the agreement, may join in the future. the objectives of the agreement are: a) eradication of poverty through a trade partnership; b) promotion of regional integration; c) gradual integration of the sadc epa states into the world economy; d) to improve the sadc epa states’ capacity in trade policy; e) to support conditions for increasing investments and f) strengthening existing relations between the parties on the basis of solidarity and mutual interest. it is important to stress that on market access, the epa will give the sadc countries duty-free access to the eu market. although south africa will not receive duty free access, an improved offer will be proposed. overall, i welcome the epa which will liberalise 86% of trade with the eu in 20 years.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the resolution on the agreement on the implementation of the work in fishing convention. workers in the fisheries sector require special protection, considering the special characteristics of work on board of fishing vessels: the high rate of fatal and non-fatal accidents, as well as the risk and incidence of occupational diseases in a hazardous working environment and the unclear distinction between work hours, rest and leisure. to date, only eight countries have ratified the ilo work in fishing convention. since the agreement applies to all fishers employed on board of a fishing vessel, which is registered in, or flying the flag of, an eu member state and which is engaged in commercial fishing operations, i support this resolution of the european parliament which recommends the immediate adoption of the council directive implementing the work in fishing convention of the international labour organisation (ilo).
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the agreement on the implementation of the convention on employment in the fisheries sector. given the specificities of work on board fishing vessels, the high number of fatal and non-fatal accidents and the risk and frequency of occupational diseases, the hazardous working conditions compared to the rest of the sector, the unclear definition of working hours, rest and leisure, the impact on health and safety of fatigue partly caused by lack of rest, the prevalence of informal and non-standard working relationships and pay arrangements, it is necessary to ensure agreement between the social partners. i therefore agree that these provisions on wages, social protection and social insurance need to be improved in order to ensure a fair income for workers and their families, including in the event of injury, accident or death.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it was the report by parliament on the implementation of the agreement on the convention on work in the fisheries sector. in view of the specific nature of work on fishing vessels, the high number of fatal and non-fatal accidents and the risk and frequency of occupational diseases, the hazardous working conditions compared to other sectors, the unclear definition of working, resting and leisure hours, the health and safety effects of fatigue caused in part by lack of rest, the existence of informal and non-standard employment relationships and pay arrangements, including crew-sharing systems, the ilo adopted in 2007 a convention on labour in the fisheries sector. however, so far only 8 countries have ratified the ilo convention on work in the fishing sector (no. 188), of which only two eu countries - france and estonia - have done so. the european parliament believes that the eu and its member states should play a leading role in promoting fair wages and working conditions in the fisheries sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. workers in the fisheries sector require special protection, considering, among other things: the special characteristics of work on board fishing vessels; the high rate of fatal and non-fatal accidents, as well as the risk and incidence of occupational diseases, in comparison with other sectors, in a hazardous working environment; also, the unclear distinction between work hours, rest and leisure, and the impact on health and safety of fatigue resulting, in part, from insufficient rest required to implement specific rules on work in the fisheries.
in writing. ‒ i support the ep resolution calling on the member states to implement the convention on employment in the fisheries sector. this convention is important in ensuring acceptable standards of working conditions for fishermen. i believe that fisheries workers need special protection, given the specific nature of work on board fishing vessels, the high number of fatalities and other accidents, the risk of occupational diseases compared to other sectors, and the lack of a clear definition of working hours, rest and leisure, taking into account the effects of fatigue, the prevalence of informal and non-standard employment relationships and pay arrangements.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on social dumping in the eu. the european union was planned by its architects as a democratic space endowed with a strong economy and a high level of social protection. however, the harmonisation of social rights was often neglected and this resulted in situations of unfair economic and social competition, which also represent an obstacle to maintaining a high level of social standards in the member states. the eu authorities have become aware of this issue and the president of the european commission, jean-claude juncker, made a solemn commitment to fight against ‘social dumping’. in his 2015 state of the union address, he also stated he wishes to avoid ‘abuses and risks of social dumping’. therefore, i welcome this report which proposes to strengthen controls and inspections, at both national and european level, in application of existing legislation. it is important to modernise the registration of employment benefits and develop a single digital document guaranteeing social rights for every european worker, as well as to adopt measures in order to ensure social convergence in the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on social dumping in the european union. the growing pattern of abuse and social dumping in europe weakens the support for the internal market and the competitiveness of businesses, especially smes, undermines european workers' rights and undermines confidence in european integration, and therefore requires social convergence in the sectors of agriculture, construction, catering and food, transport, care and household services. i therefore support further action which is necessary to ensure social convergence in the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it was the first time parliament had spoken out against social dumping in the eu. the report states that a competitive advantage for firms in our common european union market, if it is obtained at the cost of unfair practices or the exploitation of workers, should be absolutely intolerable. such practices generate poverty and exclusion in some member states, conflict within the european union and divide the eu. unfair practices and exploitation of workers must be tackled by various means: by strengthening labour inspections, including in cross-border cases, by combating the shadow economy, illegal work, false economy, tax avoidance and all the other things that undermine mutual trust between eu member states and threaten our common market and the free movement of workers.
in writing. i call on the commission to coordinate and strengthen cooperation between national authorities on road transport legislation, including through the exchange of information and other actions to support the implementation of legislation and to ensure a level playing field for operators. i welcome the launch of the european platform against undeclared work and the objectives it has set for strengthening cooperation in the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a commission delegated regulation of 30 june 2016 supplementing key information documents for retail packaged investment products and insurance-based investment products (mipps and dips) with regulatory technical standards on the presentation, content, review and refinement of key information documents and the conditions for the submission of such documents. it is essential that information provided to consumers on investment products is comparable in order to create a level playing field in the market, irrespective of the financial intermediary that issues or distributes them. similarly, the exclusion of credit risk from the calculation of the risk breakdown by category of insurance products would be misleading to investors. i agree with parliament's objection to the commission's delegated regulation and call on the commission to submit a new delegated act to address the concerns raised.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it raises parliament's objections to the commission's delegated act on packages of retail investment products and the key information document for insurance-based investment products. the parliament considers that it is essential that information on investment products be comparable for consumers in order to create a level playing field in the market, irrespective of the financial intermediary issuing or distributing them. however, excluding credit risk from the calculation of the risk breakdown of insurance products by category would be misleading to investors. the delegated act adopted by the commission has shortcomings in forecasting future performance scenarios and therefore does not comply with the requirement to provide accurate, fair, clear and non-misleading information laid down in regulation (eu) no 1286/2014, in particular because even adverse scenarios for some mipps and imps, as well as information on products that consistently lose money when invested within the shortest recommended timeframe, do not indicate that investors could lose money.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the ep's report, as it is essential that information provided to consumers about investment products is comparable in order to create a level playing field in the market, regardless of which financial intermediary issues or distributes them.
thank you, mr president, and thank you to the rapporteurs laura aguirre for their work. commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we really must finally face up to the reality of how our people, our citizens of the european union, live. and look, the number of people at risk of poverty and exclusion, instead of going down by 20 million as we had ambitiously committed, has gone up by several million. in some countries, employment levels have not yet returned to pre-crisis levels. in some member states, the proportion of young people who are not in education or training exceeds 20%, and the proportion of those who are out of school is 23%. i'm not talking about children living in poverty anymore. and in this context it is indeed very difficult to understand why the council ignores the proposals of the european parliament on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. you think you can do it alone, but you can't. life and results are really bad, which is a different story. i therefore strongly urge that we all work together - the council, the commission and the european parliament - because only in this way can we achieve concrete results in improving the lives of our people and creating quality jobs. thank you!
in writing. more than 120 million europeans are currently facing poverty due to factors such as long-term unemployment, low wages and weakening social protection systems, particularly in the countries most affected by the crisis. it is not normal for people to earn more than they need to support their families. economic growth has not reduced poverty and social exclusion by itself, poverty increases with age and minimum income protects the most vulnerable. minimum income schemes are an important and effective way of overcoming poverty, supporting social integration and access to the labour market and enabling people to live in decent conditions. i would also point out that even minimum income schemes during austerity should be seen not as a cost-increasing factor but as a key crisis-management tool, as early poverty-reduction investments have the greatest benefit in reducing long-term societal costs. in order to fulfil the commitment of the europe 2020 strategy to end the threat of poverty or exclusion for at least 20 million people in the european union, the commission must therefore take concrete action and propose solutions that ensure a europe-wide minimum income in the fight against poverty. i would just like to remind you once again that commission president juncker, in his inaugural address, mentioned the need to ensure a 'decent income' for all europeans, but the eu strategy remains unclear. so how does the commission define 'fair income' and what are its characteristics?
on behalf of the s&d group thank you, chairman. first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur, renate weber, for her excellent report and for our cooperation. in fact, this directive affects each and every one of us in the european union, each and every one of our citizens in the european union - young or old, disabled or not, male or female. it is particularly important to recognise that demographic changes in europe, as well as the increase in the retirement age, are making age discrimination in employment more relevant. therefore, if we are already taking decisions in the member states to increase the retirement age, we must ensure that our seniors have every possible opportunity to remain in the labour market as full-fledged employees. i also want to urge the member states to ensure that older workers are protected against unfair dismissal in the case of retirement age, because the rights of older workers are often violated in the member states. another point i would like to make is that we are still failing to protect the most vulnerable members of society, the disabled, from discrimination. some member states are in fact in breach of this directive by failing to adapt jobs to disabled people, by failing to provide adequate living and quality working conditions, by failing to ensure equal opportunities in education and vocational training. we must therefore again call on the member states to make use of the structural funds to adapt workplaces and provide the necessary support for disabled people at work. we also have to deal with the problem of harassment at work, which can arise for a variety of reasons - both because of gender and because of age, because of religious beliefs, which offends against human dignity, which is degrading, and finally because it is really difficult for the employee to work in such a work environment. i therefore believe that it is very important to spread information and to carry out information campaigns to inform people about their rights and opportunities at work and in the labour market, and about the responsibilities of employers towards their employees. many of our citizens do not even know what rights are covered by this directive. thank you!
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on women's rights and gender equality. the european globalisation adjustment fund has indeed helped people across europe who have lost their jobs, and its support has been very significant, especially during the economic and financial crisis, when different industrial sectors in most member states were experiencing severe difficulties and people were losing their jobs en masse. in my home country of lithuania, for example, four sectors benefited from the fund's support: construction, textiles, electronics and furniture. and that meant a lot to our small labor market and to its recovery. as rapporteur for the committee on women's rights and gender equality, i would like to point out in this report that only one third of the beneficiaries of the fund during the period under review were women. of course, this is probably due to the fact that globalisation and the financial and economic crisis have hit those sectors where men are the most employed, but i would ask the commission to continue to monitor that women are not disadvantaged in the allocation of the fund's support, so that the harmonised package of individual services for women who have lost their jobs is really tailored to their real needs. it also calls on the member states to collect data by gender to better assess the rates of women's return to the labour market and to monitor the sectors in which they return. it is particularly important to know whether women are in secure quality employment and whether their entrepreneurship is equally encouraged.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the postal services directive. the revision of postal services in 2008 achieved key objectives in terms of the liberalisation of european postal services. however, postal services have undergone dramatic changes due to the growth of e-commerce. postal services are a vital part of communication in the eu internal market, and this sector remains a fundamental contributor to social, economic and territorial cohesion and to the development of the digital single market. sectors such as e—commerce, publishing, mail order, insurance, banking and advertising depend heavily on the postal infrastructure. one of the commission’s core tasks is to promote and safeguard effective competition in the postal services sector. promoting more competition in this sector is also important in reaching the europe 2020 goals for sustainable growth in a resource-efficient and more competitive economy.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the application of the postal services directive. the 2008 postal review has achieved the main objectives of the liberalisation of european postal services. however, since the full opening of the postal services market in 2008, the postal services sector has undergone a major transformation. on the one hand, there was a decrease in paper notifications in many member states, i.e. the number of letters in 2012-2013 decreased by an average of 4.85% in all 28 eu member states. on the other hand, new technologies have made it easier to shop online, which has led to an increase in the number of parcels and parcels carried by postal service providers. as a result, more than half of the total revenue of the postal sector now comes from parcel and express transportation. over the past five years, the business-to-consumer segment of the parcel and parcel delivery markets has grown rapidly as a result of the expansion of e-commerce, and competition in these markets, while fully open across the eu, has developed slowly. i therefore agree that the commission's main tasks remain to promote and protect effective competition in the postal services sector.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is the parliament's assessment of the application of the postal services directive. the 2008 postal review has achieved the main objectives of the liberalisation of european postal services. however, since the full opening of the postal services market in 2008, the postal services sector has undergone major changes. on the one hand, paper-based notifications have decreased in many member states. in 2012-13, the number of letters across the eu fell by 4.85% on average in the 28 eu member states. on the other hand, new technologies are making it easier to shop online, which is increasing the number of parcels and parcels carried by postal service providers. as a result, more than half of the total revenue of the postal sector now comes from parcel and express transportation. over the past five years, the business-to-consumer segment of the parcel and parcel delivery markets has grown rapidly as a result of the expansion of e-commerce, and competition in these markets, while fully open across the eu, has developed slowly.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the ep's report on the application of the postal services directive. one of the main objectives of the directive is to promote and protect effective competition in the postal services sector. accessibility and reliability of postal and parcel delivery remain essential for the common market. postal services cover a wide range of services, from the dispatch of letters and parcels to the provision of value-added services. other sectors such as e-commerce, publishing, mail order, insurance, banking and advertising are highly dependent on postal infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of smes’ funding in a capital markets union. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are a substantial part of the eu economy. access to finance for smes has, therefore, been a long-standing theme on the policy agenda. bank lending constitutes still the most important source of funding for the large majority of smes. therefore, it is important to diversify the funding options for smes to allow for a wide range of choices. i welcome the proposals made in the capital market unions (cmu) action plan for connecting smes more effectively with a wide range of funding options and i support the initiative of the commission to examine and assess barriers and obstacles for smes in tapping capital markets.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on access to finance for smes and increasing the diversity of sme funding in the capital markets union. during the crisis, access to finance for smes was more limited than for larger companies. this was driven by the high reliance of smes on bank lending and the decline in bank lending caused by the crisis. the diversification of sme financing opportunities has therefore become one of the priorities of the cmu initiative. i am in favour of making it easier for smes to access a range of financing options. however, there are still many barriers to smes accessing market-based and other more innovative financing instruments. i therefore support the commission's initiative to examine and assess the obstacles to smes' access to capital markets. the analysis would remove various restrictive obstacles in a timely and appropriate manner.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it was the parliament's view on access to finance for smes and on increasing the diversity of sme finance in the capital markets union. micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps play an important role in the european economy in terms of jobs and growth. in the eu's non-financial business sector, smes employed 67% of all employees, created 71.4% of new jobs and added 58% of value in 2014. currently, there is no clear common definition of smes in union law, except for the categories 'small enterprises' and 'medium enterprises' defined under the accounting directive. smes in europe are very diverse, with a large number of micro-enterprises, often operating in traditional sectors, as well as a growing number of new start-ups and fast-growing innovative companies. these business models encounter different problems and therefore have different financial needs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and mid-caps form a substantial part of the eu economy. access to finance for smes has therefore been a long-standing theme on the policy agenda. therefore, i welcome the recognition of the importance of bank funding for smes in the commission’s capital market unions (cmu) initiative. nevertheless, it is important to diversify the funding options for smes to allow for a wide range of choices.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on harnessing job creation potential for smes. unemployment and migration flows are the biggest challenges facing europe at the moment. therefore, for eu member states it is crucial to strengthen the conditions for new job creation. the european economic structure is mainly based on smes, which are a heterogeneous group and there is a diversity of small business models. the report underlines that for achieving a sound environment for business development and boosting its job creation potential, national and european policies must as a priority address the issues of skills, regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens. it highlights the necessity of ensuring a level playing field for the smes regarding their competitive position compared with large corporations. in this regard, there is a need for specific measures for smes in order to curb their market diseconomies, enabling their internationalisation and boosting their job creation potential.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on how best to exploit the job creation potential of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the unemployment rate across the eu remains the highest in its history. in 2015, there were 23 million unemployed in the eu, including 4.5 million men and women under 25 who were not working or studying. the arrival of hundreds of thousands of new migrants is another huge social challenge, as more and more jobs are needed to properly integrate people settling in europe. i believe that smes should be given the highest priority in the european union and that all necessary steps should be taken to enhance the job creation potential of this sector. i therefore agree that it is necessary to ensure a level playing field for smes in relation to their competitive position vis-à-vis large enterprises.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this report because it is a report in which parliament has spoken about better job creation opportunities for smes. smes create more jobs than other private sector enterprises, employing around two thirds of all people in the eu private sector, thus making a significant contribution to the eu's social and economic growth and development. support to smes helps to combat unemployment and youth unemployment in europe, which are at 8,9% and 19,4% respectively, which is particularly important given the unemployment rate around 23 million people in 2015 which remains at historic highs to date. in the parliament's view, in order to improve the conditions for the creation of quality jobs in the sme sector, member states and the commission need to address the following problems, which are not equally prevalent in different member states and regions: skills shortages, mis-assessment of future skills needs, skills mismatches, brain drain, unnecessary regulatory burden and regulatory uncertainty in all areas, insufficient dialogue between labour market stakeholders, limited access to finance and public procurement, low innovation capacity and access to new technologies, insufficient support for smes in the implementation of public investment policies, the shadow economy and even fraud, as well as the highly advantageous position of multinational corporations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. unemployment and migration flows are the biggest challenges facing europe at the moment, with multiple implications for the future. high unemployment threatens demographic perspectives, as many young people without work delay starting a family. as a longer term consequence, this situation puts pressure on social security systems and pension schemes, threatening also the future of the current generation. the report emphasises the importance of a stable regulatory environment, improved regulation quality and enforcement, as the right way to lower smes burdens, including labour costs. this is an essential prerequisite for the permanence of jobs and for the smes’ potential to create high quality jobs.
in writing. ‒ the i support the report drawn up by the ep to encourage better use of job creation opportunities in small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the communication identifies a number of existing problems facing smes and identifies the most important priority measures to address these problems. for example, the report emphasises the importance of stable and improved regulatory quality and enforcement as one of the ways to reduce labour costs. the communication also welcomes in particular the further development of vocational training to promote work-based learning and apprenticeships. the communication stresses, inter alia, the need to ensure a level playing field for smes in relation to their competitive position vis-à-vis large enterprises.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on the application of the employment equality directive. the employment equality directive, whose ultimate objective is the creation of a level playing field as regards equality in employment and occupation, was adopted 15 years ago. the report underlines that some eu member states go beyond the requirements of the employment equality directive, not limiting the protection against discrimination based on religion and belief, disability, age and sexual orientation to employment, occupation and vocational training. however, challenges to the implementation of the employment equality directive still exist, since some groups and minorities in the eu have reported experiencing discrimination. this situation has a negative impact on social cohesion, as well as on respect for fundamental rights. i welcome the report as it stresses the importance of raising awareness among public opinion and the need to increase dialogue among governments, civil society and the social partners across all grounds.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the application of the directive on equal opportunities in employment. according to the european commission, the number of people of working age (15-64 years) in the eu has started to decline, and the proportion of the population aged 65 and over is projected to increase from 87 million to 152 million between 2010 and 2060. in view of this future need, i agree that there is a need to ensure more active participation in the labour market, long-term income and better work-life balance, including family care. the role of the organisation of long-term care services in society and in the labour market must be of great importance.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because this equal opportunities directive in the field of employment affects the daily lives of everyone - young people, disabled people, the elderly. it is particularly important to recognise that demographic changes in europe, as well as the increase in the retirement age, are making age discrimination in employment more relevant. therefore, if we are already extending the retirement age, we must ensure that our seniors have every possible opportunity to remain in the labour market as full-fledged employees. i would also like to urge member states to ensure that older workers are protected against unfair dismissal in the case of retirement age, as older workers' rights are more vulnerable. secondly, we are still unfortunately failing to protect the most vulnerable members of society - people with disabilities - from discrimination. some member states are in breach of this directive by failing to adapt jobs to disabled people, by failing to provide adequate living and quality working conditions, by failing to ensure equal opportunities in education and vocational training. we must therefore encourage member states to make use of the structural funds and adapt jobs and provide the necessary support for disabled people in the workplace. we cannot be indifferent to the most vulnerable groups in our society and to these problems, and i would therefore urge the commission and the member states to ensure better implementation of this directive on equal opportunities for all in the member states, as this directive should become a tool of everyday life for the member states, protecting and improving the lives of all people.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on the activities, impact and added value of the european global adjustment fund (egf). initially the egf was established by regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 to allow solidarity with workers who lost their jobs in large-scale redundancies because of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, where these redundancies have a significant adverse impact on the regional or local economy. the report underlines that the egf has undergone numerous reforms since 2006. i welcome the fact that the egf’s scope has been broadened in order to include self-employed persons and persons not in education, employment or training (neets) and that the period of intervention has been extended up to 24 months, thus allowing many beneficiaries to access more extended training or educational programmes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons with restricted liberty and legal aid in the european arrest warrant procedure. the commission proposal is a welcome step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. however, the commission proposal does not enhance legal certainty, nor does it make clear to suspects or accused persons the extent to which they will be able to exercise their right to legal aid effectively and the quality of legal aid. i therefore agree that the scope of the directive should cover the right to temporary and ordinary legal aid in all cases.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the question of provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and with the question of legal aid measures in the context of the european arrest warrant procedure. the right to legal aid is a difficult issue and this may explain why it took the commission a relatively long time to present the current measure. however, this should not prevent the new european parliament from starting to consider the proposal for a directive on a priority basis. different interpretations of the right to a fair trial, including the right to legal aid, recognised, inter alia, in article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and in article 6 of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, create obstacles to the exercise of fair and effective judicial cooperation in criminal matters. it is therefore necessary to adopt the remaining measures of the action plan as soon as possible, in particular the draft legal aid directive. the commission proposal is a welcome step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. however, this proposal limits the right to provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings when deprived of liberty and the right to provisional legal aid and legal aid for requested persons subject to the european arrest warrant procedure. additional aspects of the right to legal aid are dealt with in a separate commission recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. this proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council aims to set common minimum standards on the right to provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings when they are deprived of liberty and for provisional legal aid and legal aid for persons subject to proceedings. this proposal seeks to improve the rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. having common minimum standards governing these rights should boost mutual trust between judicial authorities and thus facilitate the application of the principle of mutual recognition. a certain degree of compatibility between the legislation of member states is crucial to improve judicial cooperation in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i support the european commission's proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and on legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. i believe that the same rules for legal aid for suspects or accused persons with restricted liberty and for legal aid in the european arrest warrant procedure should apply throughout the eu. these rules will strengthen the rights of suspects and accused persons and establish common minimum standards of due process. it should be noted that persons requested to be extradited in accordance with the european arrest warrant do not always have access to legal aid in the member states. moreover, despite the rights of suspects or accused persons, judicial cooperation is disproportionately affected. it is therefore essential to remove existing obstacles and to strengthen mutual trust between judicial authorities and to facilitate the application of the principle of mutual recognition. it should be noted that judicial cooperation must be based on mutual trust and confidence in different judicial systems.

in writing. ‒ the european union can be hailed as one of the leading champions in the fight against the practice of torture and execution, which is why it should demonstrate that quality throughout one of its biggest activities – trade. this report urges to close all the loopholes that are present in the current trade strategy that allows for pharmaceuticals to travel in and out of the eu, and that are then misused for the purpose of torture or execution (such as lethal injection). it enforces both annex ii and iii and establishes an urgency procedure or a ‘fast track,’ for future pharmaceuticals to be added to the lists of banned substances without a consequential delay. this report stresses the fact that in the case of other pharmaceuticals and medicines which are not on the list of possible torture and execution substances, their trade cannot and will not be hindered. this report is a milestone in europe’s fight against the death penalty and the use of torture throughout the world. it provides a solid basis for member states to work off and add on to, allowing the eu to uphold its values not only domestically but also internationally.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the eu's main instrument in the fight against torture and the death penalty is the 2005 rules on the control of trade in instruments of torture. they prohibit the export of goods (such as electric chairs, guillotines or automatic drug injection systems) and control the trade of goods that can be used for these purposes (such as tools or materials for riot control). in 2010, the european parliament called on the european commission to update the above rules, as certain legal loopholes allowed to avoid trade or advertising restrictions. in this context, and in the light of the european parliament's calls, i agree that it is necessary to ensure an appropriate combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external policy measures to prevent the production, trade and use of goods for torture and to prohibit and effectively control goods that may be used for life-threatening and inhumane purposes.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. eu-wide export controls are an instrument of external trade policy serving a variety of wider policy objectives. the torture regulation is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights by controlling goods and activities that are or could be misused for the purposes of capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the torture regulation contributes to the eu's long-term policy to abolish the death penalty and prevent torture worldwide. the regulation contributes to these objectives by combining prohibitions with the requirements for the issuing of marketing authorisations for specified commodities. it covers the prohibition of the sale of goods intended solely for torture and execution and the provision of related technical assistance and a system for the authorisation of goods for various uses which could be improperly used for torture and execution by lethal injection. it is therefore essential to ensure an appropriate combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external policy measures to prevent the production, trade and use of goods for torture and to prohibit and effectively control goods that may be used for life-threatening and inhuman purposes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. it is important to ensure the right mix of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of torture goods as well as effectively control items with potential lethal and inhumane uses. it is essential to ensure coherence of the eu’s export controls including military, dual use, firearms and torture goods lists, without subjecting items to duplicate controls.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report. i think that it is necessary to set very strict requirements for trade in goods which could be used for capital punishment or torture. in particular, due respect for human life and fundamental human rights must be ensured and public interests and moral standards protected. it is necessary to prohibit the export and import of such equipment. it is welcome that the rules have been supplemented by provisions which will, at the same time or in certain cases, strictly control not only the export of the goods in question but also their transit through the eu or their advertising. the implementation of the measures envisaged will ensure that economic operators do not benefit from trade in goods which are used in practice only for capital punishment or for torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

madam president, i would like to object, based on rule 192 of the rules of procedure. in respect of minutes for 3 october, i did not agree to be replaced by catherine bearder in the committee on internal market and consumer protection.
mr president, just a few remarks. the first concerns migrants. today it is clear that the people of the european countries do not accept the policy of quotas. and hungary, regardless of how we interpret the referendum result, will not accept migrants, as will some other countries in the european union. will the european parliament and the council have the courage to admit that the quota policy has been a complete failure? will it be strong enough to recognise that the only effective means of tackling migration and the problems it brings is through control of external and internal borders? secondly, the treaty between the united states and the european union. neither the name of the president nor the timing of the election campaign can be an excuse to turn a blind eye to a treaty that will open the door to the people of europe to export unsafe food, chemicals and other products to their countries. calls for speeding up negotiations, where the parties' ambitions are so far diametrically opposed and no compromise is being reached by either side, are another example of the irresponsible policies we have in common today. and the third is about the future. dialogue, and dialogue alone, is a prerequisite for the continued existence of the european union. i am not just talking about the contract. dialogue, not confrontation, is necessary after the hungarian and british referendums. that dialogue is no less needed now that america and russia have broken off talks on a possible peace process in syria. the european union should be the initiator of the dialogue in this respect, trying to bring the two sides to the negotiating table in a trilateral or a quadrilateral way. (the president agreed to answer the question after the blue card had been raised) (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure)
answer to the question posed by the blue card. thank you for asking. the free movement of people is certainly one of the four fundamental freedoms of europe, and i think it's a positive concept, but i see no limit and no end to the possibility of accepting these tens or even more millions of people from other countries, where we are doing nothing to cause armed conflict and people have to flee their own country.
syria must be on the agenda of the next eu council meeting. we are watching as the syrian government, backed by the russian air force, is conducting an intensive campaign, methodically killing civilians in and around aleppo. the international community, including the european union, cannot even deliver humanitarian aid. what the russian-backed syrian government is doing in aleppo is a vicious campaign that must be stopped, and we await the decision of the council of the european union on this matter. given the way russia is allowing itself to behave not only in syria, but also in ukraine, georgia, there is only one way - sanctions on russia must remain. russia has not implemented the minsk agreements and, until they are implemented, any proposals to consider lifting sanctions against russia are unacceptable and, most importantly, useless to the european union. on foreign trade issues, the ceta, the free trade agreement with canada, must be given the green light immediately, everything must be done to ensure that the agreement is not only signed but also enters into force immediately.
in writing. the forthcoming european council at the end of october will focus on the russian question. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the compatibility of the aid with the internal market. in september, parliamentary elections were held, which finally eliminated the non-systemic opposition from the russian political system. in early 2014, he was appointed as a member of the security council of the russian federation. at the end of the month, the dutch chief investigator's report on the mh17 tragedy confirmed that the passenger plane over eastern ukraine was shot down by a buk zenit missile system brought from russia and later returned to russia. while the specific identities of the officials who committed and ordered the crime are not yet being revealed, questions about russia's responsibility for this tragedy should no longer arise. on october 4, it was announced that the country would begin a three-day general military exercise that would mobilize 40 million people, or one third of the population. this is obviously a propaganda figure, but the number of such unannounced exercises in russia is increasing. this should be sufficient to assess the current political situation in russia and the success of any attempts to normalise relations with it by returning to the usual formats.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the proposal for a council decision authorising the republic of austria and romania to accept, in the interest of the european union, the accession of peru to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. i welcome the accession of peru to the convention as eu-wide protection should be ensured for the children in question. the convention introduces a system of cooperation between the contracting states aimed at settling cases of international child abduction. the convention also initiates a system which ensures the immediate return of children who have been abducted. following the accession of peru to the convention, a council decision is therefore necessary to authorise the two member states which have not yet accepted the accession of peru – austria and romania – to accept that accession. this will allow the convention to enter into force between peru and the entire european union and it has a particular significance because of many eu citizens that are of peruvian origin. children with links to the peruvian community will thus be safeguarded against abduction.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the proposal authorising the republic of austria and romania, in the interests of the european union, to accept the accession of peru to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important document providing a framework for cooperation between the contracting parties in dealing with cases of international child abduction. in many cases, child abduction problems arise when a couple separates. in addition, the courts of both countries often recognise their jurisdiction and each country grants custody to a parent who is a national of their respective country. in the light of these examples, i support the accession of peru to the hague convention to determine the competent courts and to apply the laws of the state of the child's habitual residence. it would also ensure that the child abducted is returned without delay.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which discusses the european union's interest in supporting peru's accession to the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important document. it has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention provides for a system of cooperation between the contracting parties to deal with cases of international child abduction. in many cases, these problems arise when couples separate. if the mother and father are from different countries, there is a desire to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between these countries in order to secure custody of the child. the media are full of reports of international child abductions, either by separation or by adoption. in these cases, the main problem is the national bias of the legal systems of individual countries. often, the courts of both countries recognise their jurisdiction and each country grants custody to the parent who is a national of their respective country. following the accession of peru to the convention, a council decision is necessary in order to authorise the two member states which have not yet acceded to peru's accession (austria and romania) to accede to that country. this will allow the convention to enter into force between peru and the whole of the european union. the accession of peru to the convention is welcomed. the rapporteur fully supports this accession, especially since a large number of eu citizens are of peruvian origin. so children with connections to the peruvian community will be protected from abduction.
