in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which discusses the european union's interest in supporting the accession of the republic of korea to the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important document. it has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention provides for a system of cooperation between the contracting parties to deal with cases of international child abduction. in many cases, these problems arise when couples separate. if the mother and father are from different countries, there is a desire to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between these countries in order to secure custody of the child. the media are full of reports of international child abductions, either by separation or by adoption. in these cases, the main problem is the national bias of the legal systems of individual countries. often, the courts of both countries recognise their jurisdiction and each country grants custody to the parent who is a national of their respective country. following the accession of south korea to the convention, a council decision is necessary to empower member states (with the exception of denmark, which is not subject to the union's civil justice policy, and the czech republic, ireland and lithuania, which have already agreed to the accession of south korea) to agree to the accession of south korea. this will allow the convention to enter into force between south korea and the whole of the european union. the accession of south korea to the convention is to be welcomed.
in writing. ‒ the accession of south korea to the convention is welcomed. the commission, together with civil justice experts from the member states, has assessed the functioning of the justice system in south korea and its commitment to implement the convention and considers it desirable that the convention enter into force between the european union and south korea. i agree with the provisions of this report because i believe that the hague convention system will be more effective and the handling of international child abduction cases will be easier if more countries accede to the convention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which authorises certain member states, in the interests of the european union, to accede to the accession of the republic of korea to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. following the accession of south korea to the convention, this decision is necessary in order to empower member states to accede to the accession of south korea. this will allow the convention to enter into force between south korea and the whole of the european union.

in writing. ‒ i have voted against the motion for a resolution on global goals and eu commitments on nutrition and food security in the world. while i appreciate the effort to call on the member states to step up with their commitments for global food security, the final document had serious weaknesses, deploring that the eu biofuels policy is encouraging speculation on arable land and urging the eu to remove public incentives for the production of crop-based biofuels. additionally, despite the fact that this resolution stressed the need for eu trade and development policy to respect the political and economic policy space of developing countries in order for them to establish the necessary policies to promote sustainable development and dignity for their people, including food sovereignty, it failed to respect the right of local food producers to have control over their land, seeds and water, meaning that privatisation of natural resources was not excluded, due to an unsuccessful amending attempt, from the final text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal on the follow-up to the global goals and on the eu's commitments on nutrition and food security in the world. there are currently 159 million children in the world with developmental disabilities (due to age and low height) and 50 million children suffering from malnutrition (due to height and low weight, often associated with extreme hunger). poor nutrition weakens physical and cognitive abilities and creates a cycle of poverty. the commission's action plan on nutrition has committed to reducing the number of children with developmental disabilities by 7 million by 2025, but investment in nutrition remains insufficient. i therefore agree that the commission must honour its commitment to invest eur 3.5 billion to reduce the number of children with developmental disabilities by at least 7 million by 2025.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the european parliament stresses the need to tackle the systemic problems that lead to malnutrition in all its forms. reinvestment in local food production, with a particular focus on small-scale food producers and agro-ecological practices, is a key condition for the successful implementation of nutrition strategies. it is also essential to establish social protection schemes to ensure that all people have access to nutritious food at all times. parliament also stressed that priority should be given to local food production in tackling food shortages and stressed the importance of supporting small farmers and farmers as food producers. it is therefore important to encourage the eu, in the context of its global nutrition strategy, to help developing countries and small farmers to develop and exploit local markets, local value chains and food processing opportunities, while implementing trade policy measures to support these actions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the eu's commitments on nutrition and food security in the world. i believe that everyone should have access to nutritious food, and that is why it is important to consistently help developing countries and their small farmers to develop local markets, local value chains and food processing opportunities. this would reduce poverty and disease caused by malnutrition in developing countries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the way forward towards the global goals and on the eu's commitments on nutrition and food security in the world. worldwide, 795 million people do not have enough food to lead a healthy and active life. yet, at the same time, one third of all food produced worldwide - about 1.3 billion tons - is wasted. in the european union alone, 88 million tonnes of food is wasted. so the first step to tackling food insecurity is to adapt all food systems so that food is not wasted. secondly, it is necessary to encourage food production where it is scarce, rather than spending millions on exporting it, thus increasing the climate change problem. therefore, the funds allocated to food security must be used to train local people in the implementation of new technologies. on the other hand, it is necessary to ensure that food is safe and healthy. feeding the hungry is important, but food cannot be poisoned.

mr president, as a member of the european parliament delegation, i have been observing the plebiscite in columbia. let me share with you my observations and a few conclusions. last sunday we witnessed colombian democracy in action. we should fully respect the will of the colombian people expressed during the plebiscite. the result of the plebiscite does not question in any way the will of the colombian people to have peace and reconciliation in that country, which has been facing armed conflict, killings, kidnappings, displacements and all kinds of violence for 52 years. the perception in europe that the ‘no’ camp voted in favour of war is totally wrong. the colombian nation wants peace and voted for peace. the peace process in colombia is irreversible. bilateral ceasefire commitments made by the colombian government and farc have been kept. the european union will continue its support for the peace process in colombia. president santos and his government deserve our support in their efforts to reach a de facto peace in colombia without prejudging the content of the peace agreement, providing that the colombian people endorse and approve it through the plebiscite. the result of the plebiscite clearly indicates that the final peace agreement has to be renegotiated and at least two issues are to be addressed, namely participation of farc in the political process and impunity for farc. the current peace agreement guarantees ten seats for farc in the colombian congress and five seats in the senate, without the need to be elected, plus justice reviews for farc members. now it is evident that a new phase of dialogue must be opened that should be inclusive and transparent. my last remark has regard to the delisting of farc from the eu list of terrorist organisations. following the signing of the peace agreement, the council unanimously decided to temporarily delist farc for six months, and sanctions against the farc leadership have been dropped. the decision regarding delisting is conditional and is to be terminated immediately if farc does not deliver on its promises of no violence and full disarmament. i suggest that the issue of the delisting of farc be high on the agenda of high representative mogherini.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the resolution on international financial reporting standards: ifrs 9. the global financial crisis has put the importance of international financial reporting standards for financial stability and growth on the g20 and eu agendas. the newly developed standard (ifrs 9) will become effective on 1 january 2018 and will replace international accounting standard (ias) 39. the new standard is much more advanced, as it moves from a model of impairment based on 'experimental loss' to one based on 'predicted loss'. this is a solution to the problem of too little and too late action in the procedure for recognising loan losses. in its resolution, parliament calls on the commission, together with the esas, to closely monitor the implementation of ifrs 9 in the eu and to prepare an impact assessment and submit it to the european parliament by june 2019.

in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the food contact materials (fcm) regulation. fcms are largely used in everyday life as food packaging, kitchen utensils, tableware, etc. when put in contact with food, different materials may behave differently, transferring their constituents to the food. in such cases, chemicals emanating from fcms may endanger human health. fcms are subject to legally binding rules at eu level, which are currently laid down in framework regulation (ec) no 1935/2004. this sets out general safety requirements that are applicable to all possible food contact materials. it also foresees the possibility to adopt specific measures for the 17 materials listed in the regulation, but so far specific eu measures have only been adopted for four fcms: plastic, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. i welcome the recommendations of this report to adopt the specific eu measures for the remaining 13 materials, giving priority to those that constitute a particular risk to human health, and to urgently tackle shortcomings in the implementation and enforcement of the legislation in place. in this respect, the focus should be on four major areas: risk assessment, traceability, enforcement and controls of compliance.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the regulation on raw materials and articles intended to come into contact with food. food contact materials are often used in everyday life as packaging, kitchen utensils, cutlery and other items. when in contact with food, and depending on their composition and properties, different substances may react differently to release their constituents into food. in such cases, the chemicals released by food contact materials may endanger human health or adversely affect the composition of food. as food is considered to be one of the main routes by which chemicals affect humans, legally binding eu-level rules currently set out in the framework regulation apply to food contact materials. the legislation aims to maintain a high level of consumer protection while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market for food contact materials. this regulation lays down common safety requirements for all materials and articles which may come into contact with food. to date, specific measures at eu level have been adopted for only four food contact materials, namely plastics (including recycled plastics), ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. for other food contact materials, member states may adopt specific measures at national level.
in writing. ‒ i support the ep report on the regulation on raw materials and articles intended to come into contact with food. the legislation aims to maintain a high level of consumer protection while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market for food contact materials.
in writing. - i voted for this report. i think it's very relevant. we use food packaging, tools that come in direct contact with food, every day. often little thought is given to the effects that these substances may have on our food and, in time, on our health. it is therefore necessary to have legislation aimed at maintaining a high level of consumer protection. the communication also calls for the development of safe, reusable and recyclable food-contact materials and products, thus contributing to the eu's efforts to create a more efficient circular economy.
in writing. i welcome research and innovation initiatives to develop new materials for use in wmd that have been shown to be safe for human health. i believe that further concrete measures at eu level would encourage businesses to develop safe, reusable and recyclable weee and thus contribute to the eu's efforts to create a more efficient circular economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on monitoring the application of union law, concerning the 2014 annual report. this, the commission’s 32nd annual report on the subject, contains information on the actual implementation and practical application of eu law. while environment, transport and the internal market and services remained the policy areas in which most infringement cases were open in 2014, the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased in the last five years. despite the positive change, which in commission’s view reflects the effectiveness of dialogue with member states, it is clear from the annual report that the enforcement of eu law is still not sufficiently transparent. i supported the report as it not only notes that but also calls on the commission to make compliance with eu law a real political priority. i also appreciate the position that the european parliament should play a more structured role in the analysis of how accession countries and countries with association agreements with the european union comply with eu law, as well as in developing appropriate support in relation to those countries.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the commission's report on the monitoring of the application of european union law. the report indicates that environment, transport and internal market and services were the policy areas where most infringement procedures were initiated in 2014. the report also highlights the decrease in the number of formal infringement procedures over the past five years. according to the commission, this demonstrates the effectiveness of the dialogue between member states under the 'eu pilot' procedure. however, given that parliament still has limited access to information on the eu pilot procedure and pending cases, it is difficult to assess to what extent the decrease in the number of formal infringement procedures actually reflects a greater compliance by member states with eu law rather than a compromise between the commission and the member state that has infringed eu law. the report therefore concludes that the implementation of eu law is still not sufficiently transparent. the proposals of the new working group on administrative law set up by the legal affairs committee could thus be a valuable source of inspiration for the commission, as they demonstrate the usefulness and feasibility of a regulation on eu administrative procedure.

in writing. i agree with the report. it is important that member states properly comply with the requirements of eu law and better implement them in national policies, and that compliance is improved and possible irregularities are quickly remedied, in the interests of citizens and businesses. environment, transport and the internal market and services remain the areas where most infringement proceedings have been initiated. attention should be drawn to the importance of a structured dialogue, which should be conducted before the initiation of an infringement procedure. trust in the eu institutions needs to be built. particular attention should be paid to petitions, as they are a fundamental right enshrined in the lisbon treaty and at the same time an important secondary tool for monitoring the application of eu law and identifying possible gaps in citizens' direct expression of their views.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the draft commission implementing decision concerning the placing on the market for cultivation of genetically modified maize bt11 seeds. pursuant to directive 2001/18/ec, the cultivation of genetically modified maize bt11 is prohibited in states of the european union such as bulgaria, denmark, greece, france, croatia, italy, cyprus, latvia, lithuania, etc. the draft commission implementing decision is not consistent with union law as it is not compatible with the objective of directive 2001/18/ec, which is to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states and to protect human health and the environment when carrying out the deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified organisms for any other purposes than placing on the market within the community and placing on the market genetically modified organisms as or in products within the community. having in mind also that the risk management recommendations proposed by the commission are inadequate, i supported resolution’s call on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision.

in writing. ‒ given that the eu-china dialogue on migration and mobility is the framework for the exchange of views and discussion of cooperation between the two sides, it was agreed to open negotiations on a reciprocal visa-free regime for holders of diplomatic passports in 2013. i agree that visa waiver will reduce time spent in consulates and reduce travel related costs. it will also facilitate people-to-people exchanges, which are essential for the development of economic, cultural and scientific links on a level playing field.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the people's republic of china on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. china is one of the countries whose nationals are required to be in possession of a visa for entry into the schengen area, in accordance with council regulation (ec) no 539/2001. eu citizens travelling to china also need a visa. in addition, the visa information system (vis) was officially launched in china on 12 october 2015 and from that date all chinese applicants are required to submit their biometric data when applying for a schengen visa. the eu-china dialogue on migration and mobility provides a framework for the exchange of views and for the discussion of opportunities for cooperation on issues of mutual interest related to their respective migration policies. this dialogue was launched in october 2013 and, as part of its development, it was agreed to open negotiations on an agreement on a reciprocal visa-free regime for holders of diplomatic passports. to this end, on 14 september 2015, the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations and discuss negotiating directives for an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports.

in writing. ‒ the eu-china dialogue on migration and mobility is a very important process that is in the interest of both sides to develop. i welcome and support the initiative of both countries to lift the short-stay visa requirement for holders of diplomatic passports. i also deeply regret that the european union negotiators were unable to agree on visa-free travel for eu citizens to china. i am well aware and pleased that china is taking the initiative to allow eu citizens to enjoy up to 5 days visa-free transit at certain points, but i am convinced that a visa-free regime is essential for a wider dialogue between the two economic poles, at least for eu citizens. that is what i call on the european commission to do.
in writing. ‒ during the financial and economic crisis, member states adopted austerity measures to balance their budgets. greece and cyprus are experiencing particularly severe economic problems. in this context, it is therefore necessary to ensure the implementation of the main eu funding instruments, and in particular the european structural and investment funds (esif). the objective of articles 24 and 120 (3) of the general provisions regulation (gpr) is to help member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties and receiving financial assistance to make the most of the investment opportunities provided for under the european structural and investment funds in the 2014-2020 programming period. i therefore agree that, in the light of the economic situation in the countries concerned, the period during which additional support may be granted could be extended.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the general provisions regulation (gpr) which allows the commission to pay higher payments to countries in economic difficulties (the so-called 'supplementary payments'). the financial and economic crisis has weighed heavily on national economies, leading member states to take drastic austerity measures to balance their budgets. in this context, it is important to ensure the smooth implementation of the main eu funding instruments, namely the european structural and investment funds (esif). as national budgets are heavily burdened, it can be difficult for countries experiencing budgetary difficulties to find sufficient funds for national co-financing of regional policy projects. the general provisions regulation aims to help member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties and receiving financial assistance to make the most of the investment opportunities provided by the european structural and investment funds for the 2014-2020 programming period. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties on the measures in force. on 27 june 2016, the commission submitted a legislative proposal to the european parliament and the council on that extension.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the current proposal would allow the commission to continue making increased payments to any member state which will benefit from financial assistance after 30 june 2016 for the period it will be under this support mechanism, without modifying the overall the european structural and investment funds allocation in 2014-2020. until now programme implementation has been often challenging, not least as a result of the liquidity problems resulting from fiscal consolidation. this is particularly the case for those member states which have been most affected by the crisis.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed amendments to the regulation as they will help member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties and receiving financial support to make the most of investment opportunities.
in writing. ‒ this short but much-needed regulation will help member states in difficulty to balance their public finances. this is particularly important given that eu investments are co-financed by the member states, which often invest their own money first and only then recover part of it from eu funds. this creates significant budgetary pressures, especially in countries such as cyprus, which not only suffers from financial difficulties but has also moved from one cohesion policy group to another due to its level of economic development. i therefore support this legislation as an example of european solidarity and a precedent which i hope other eu member states in difficulty will be able to take advantage of.

in writing. ‒ members of the european parliament may not be questioned, detained or prosecuted for opinions expressed or votes cast in the course of their duties, but this right does not give them the freedom to defame, insult, incite hatred or insult their honour. the pre-trial judges of the paris district court have requested the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of jean-marie le pen, accused of inciting racial hatred in a video posted online in 2014. in view of this, and the fact that there is no link between the statements of jean-marie le pen at issue and his parliamentary activities, and that he was not acting in his capacity as a member of the european parliament, i support the ep's proposal to waive jean-marie le pen's immunity and thus to allow the law enforcement authorities to investigate the case.
in writing. ‒ accusations of incitement to hatred are extremely serious, especially when they are made against a member of the european parliament. we cannot allow european immunity to help us hide from responsibility for inciting hatred, especially when there is footage to support such accusations. i therefore vote in favour and hope that the french judiciary will quickly clarify the merits of these allegations.
in writing. ‒ at the plenary session of 11 may 2016, the president informed that he had received a request from jane collins on 3 may 2016 to uphold her immunity. on the basis of the explanatory statement of the action as amended by judge m.d.j. warby's order of 29 april 2015, mr collins made and published a speech at the uk independence party conference in doncaster on 26 september 2014 which was published in the media and in the public domain (including a live broadcast of the event on the bbc parliamentary tv channel) and which insulted the honour and dignity of the members of the united kingdom parliament who brought the action. given that there is no direct and obvious link between the disputed statements and the duties of jane collins as a member of the european parliament, since they are not related to her activities as a member of the european parliament or to the policy areas of the european union and were made in the course of national political debates, it has been decided not to protect the privileges and immunities of jane collins.

in writing. ‒ the council and parliament agreed that the most effective and cost-effective way to avoid duplication of work between eurostat, the commission and the european union agency for railways is to strengthen the work of these institutions and to ensure that statistics relating to eu policies are easily accessible to eu citizens and stakeholders. these mous are not only important tools for optimising the use of existing information and reducing administrative burden, but also ensure that the legislative requirements for better use of rail transport statistics are met. they will provide easily accessible data and reliable information on the progress of eu rail policy to all categories of consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted on this recommendation on the council position with a view to adopting a regulation on rail transport statistics provisions relating to the collection of data on freight, passengers and traffic events. in its discussions with the council, the european parliament decided that the scope of the regulation on rail transport statistics should be extended to include infrastructure data, in particular on the deployment of the european rail traffic management system (ertms), which was one of the priorities of the trans-european transport network (ten-t). parliament stressed that it was crucial to have a clear picture of how ertms is being developed in the union, as the eu has spent millions of euros to finance this type of infrastructure, but because of inconsistent deployment and delays in deployment, there are no concrete results in terms of technical requirements for the use of the system. parliament also decided that eurostat should provide statistics on stations accessible to persons with reduced mobility and disabled persons, and on the use of crossborder railway infrastructure. as regards the accidents which the commission proposed to remove from the scope of the regulation, parliament considered that the statistics on railway accidents should remain within the scope of the regulation and even be extended to include accidents and incidents involving the transport of dangerous goods and accidents in transit. parliament considers it essential that eu citizens have easy access to data relating to the implementation of eu policies, in accordance with the principle of a single window.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation. the european parliament has decided that the scope of the regulation on rail transport statistics should be expanded to include data on infrastructure because it is extremely important to get a clear impression of how the eu has developed the european rail traffic management system. also, parliament has stated that statistics on rail accidents should remain within the scope of the regulation, which can even be extended to include accidents involving dangerous goods and disasters. it is important that eu citizens should have easy access to data related to the implementation of eu policies.
in writing. ‒ i have supported the ep's report on amendments to the regulation in the field of rail transport statistics. on the basis of those amendments, the scope of the regulation should be extended to include infrastructure data, in particular the deployment of the european rail traffic management system (ertms), which was one of the priorities of the trans-european transport network (ten-t). this will help to give a clear impression of the development of ertms in the union, as the eu has spent millions of euros to finance this type of infrastructure, but due to inconsistent deployment and delays in deployment, no concrete results have been achieved so far in terms of the technical requirements for the use of the system.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. in particular, greater efforts are needed to establish a well-functioning internal market that will help to revive the railway sector. rail freight and passenger services must become more competitive and attractive. they should also be involved as much as possible in the diversified transport sector. the proper monitoring and development of the common transport policy and the creation of a common railway area require accurate and objective statistics on rail freight and passenger transport. in order to reduce the administrative burden, statistics should be transparent, public and accessible to the public. in addition, the legal framework for european rail transport statistics should be updated, optimised and simplified to the greatest extent possible in order to make it flexible and able to adapt appropriately to changing conditions.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the positions of the parliament and the council on the harmonisation of the rail statistics regulation were easily reconciled. indeed, the adoption of this document will reduce the workload of statistical collection, as the railway agency and eurostat will no longer have to do the same work. at the same time, it is good that the scope of such an important task as the collection of information on accidents has not been reduced. i believe that this document will directly contribute to both better regulation and the creation of better railways in europe.
in writing. ‒ at first reading, parliament extended the scope of the regulation on statistics on inland waterway transport of goods to include passenger transport. the parliament believes that a successful policy to strengthen inland waterway transport in the transport sector should be based on reliable statistics covering both freight and passenger transport. the extension of the scope of the regulation currently in force would apply to inland waterway transport the same conditions as for the maritime, air and road transport sectors, where statistics are collected covering both goods and passengers. parliament also limited and clarified the powers conferred on the commission.

in writing. ‒ although the customs union is considered one of the cornerstones of the european union and the backbone of the single market, there is still a lack of equal treatment of customs legislation and enforcement of sanctions. this means that the rules are the same but the penalties for infringement are very different, i.e. a company may lose its status as an authorised economic operator in one member state for the same infringement, but not in another. these differences result in a lack of trust between administrations, and customs trust and cooperation are essential for the good administration of the customs union and the protection of the eu's financial interests. i therefore support the view of the committee on legal affairs that the legal basis for the directive on breaches of union customs law and sanctions should be articles 33 and 114 tfeu in the legal framework, which would help to remove obstacles to the free movement of goods or the freedom to provide services or distortions of competition and improve the system of cooperation between customs authorities.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines the legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions in the european union. on 13 december 2013, the european commission published a proposal for a directive on the legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions in the union. although the customs union is considered one of the cornerstones of the european union and the backbone of the single market, there is still a lack of a uniform approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including sanctions. this means that the rules are the same, but the penalties for breaching them are very different. the customs union and trade policy are an exclusive competence of the european union and only the eu can develop a common approach to ensure the implementation of customs legislation. the member states have undertaken to pursue two objectives, namely the effective interaction and functioning of the customs administrations as if they were one single administration, ensuring controls that produce uniform results and support legitimate business activities, but also ensuring the necessary protection of the financial interests of the union. however, it is sufficiently clear that without an integrated approach to enforcement, including sanctions, it is not possible to achieve the functioning of the customs administrations of the member states as one, in particular in view of the significant differences in the sanctioning systems of the member states as shown in the 2010 report of the customs sanctions project group.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's proposed amendments to the directive on the legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions in the union. the commission proposal establishes a common legal framework for the assessment and sanctioning of customs infringements, laying down common rules and thus closing the gaps created by the differences in legal regimes. this contributes to the uniform assessment of economic operators in the eu and enhances the effective protection of the financial interests of the union and the enforcement of customs law.
in writing. ‒ the issue of infringements of the eu customs legislation and the sanctions legal framework is a complex one and it seems that a compromise between the two parties to the legislative process will not be reached for some time. at the same time, i hope that the council and the commission will listen to the arguments of the representatives of eu citizens, particularly in relation to the need to strengthen the harmonisation of the customs systems of the member states, to make the application of penalties for infringements uniform. at the same time, i would also like to express my doubts about the appropriateness of parliament's sufficiently rigorous position, in particular the requirement that member states be given the possibility to apply criminal rather than non-criminal sanctions in accordance with national law and union law, where this is necessary because of the nature and gravity of the infringement concerned, in order to ensure that the sanctions applied are dissuasive, effective and proportionate. i would think that the commission's proposal, which provides for a detailed gradation of penalties, was much more balanced.

in writing. ‒ the indeed, the very notion of human rights becomes very doubtful when there are no states left and when the individual is dissolved in the waves of migration caused by unrest. the international community therefore faces an important challenge to ensure that the eu's core value of human rights remains protected, regardless of the international situation. i agree with the report. i would also like to point out that there is still a need to focus more on prevention rather than treatment. we should therefore talk more about how the eu can help prevent or manage conflicts. this will also mean that less attention will be paid to refugee issues, simply because of the decrease in the number of refugees.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report on corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries. public limited companies are one of the key players in economic globalisation, financial services and international trade and are obliged to comply with all applicable and valid legislation and international agreements and to respect human rights. i therefore agree that the eu and the member states should continue to pursue the objective of ensuring the best possible protection of human rights by using the most effective means, rather than simply overloading them with administrative and bureaucratic formal rules.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which deals with corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries. the european parliament notes that the increasing globalisation and internationalisation of business activities and supply chains will contribute to the increasing importance of the role of public limited companies in ensuring respect for human rights and will create a situation in which international norms, rules and cooperation are essential to prevent human rights violations by public limited companies and business enterprises in third countries. parliament is deeply concerned about human rights violations by individuals, public companies, non-state actors and states in third countries, including those resulting from decisions taken by public companies and business enterprises. it also reminds business actors of their responsibility to respect human rights in their global operations, regardless of the location of their users and regardless of whether the host country respects its human rights obligations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. increasing globalisation and internationalisation of business activities and supply chains will make the role that corporations play in ensuring respect for human rights more important and create a situation in which international norms, rules and cooperation are crucial to avoid human rights abuses in third countries. however, i am very concerned by cases of human rights violations committed in third countries, including of some eu corporations and business enterprises management decisions. if companies are found to have caused or contributed to harm, they should take moral but also legal responsibility and must provide effective remedy processes for the individuals and communities affected.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. it is necessary to strengthen the liability of companies for serious human rights violations in third countries. particular attention shall be paid to the implementation of the united nations basic principles on business and human rights worldwide. it is also essential that each member state properly discharge its duty to respect and adequately protect human rights. the importance of corporate social responsibility should be emphasised. companies should assume not only moral but also legal responsibility and properly implement restitution, compensation, rehabilitation and a guarantee that the damage will not be repeated. the commission should also take urgent action to establish binding rules and mechanisms for the application and monitoring of sanctions. any trade and investment agreement must be assessed in terms of its human rights impact. in addition, these agreements must include provisions on human rights and guarantees to mitigate possible threats and adverse effects.
in writing. ‒ committed to the protection of human rights, the european union cannot ignore the violations of human rights in third countries by european companies. this not only undermines the very concept of human rights, as if there were two kinds of people, but also hinders the harmonious development of these countries, and only undemocratic regimes can tolerate the human rights violations committed by transnational corporations. i welcome and support the report. i think that this is a subject that needs to be brought to the attention of european society and the world at large. the same large corporations cannot be left behind, since in many cases human rights violations in their branches in third countries are also the result of the companies' own lack of social responsibility and the lack of appropriate local legal regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategy for the use and storage of liquefied natural gas. the eu is currently facing a serious crisis of competition in the gas sector. one of the objectives of the eu lng utilisation and gas storage strategy is to achieve the eu's ambition to move rapidly towards elements of a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system and away from dependence on external gas suppliers. this is a very important factor in reducing dependence on russian gas.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the european union's strategy for the use and storage of liquefied natural gas. the european parliament welcomes the commission communication on an eu strategy for the use and storage of liquefied natural gas and considers that an internal energy market fully integrating the use and storage of liquefied natural gas will play an important role in achieving the ultimate goal of a resilient energy union. the eu lng and gas storage strategy is one of the elements of the energy union, which aims to deliver on the eu's ambition to move rapidly towards a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system, and to move away from dependence on external gas suppliers. parliament stressed that one of the objectives of the energy union is to make the eu a world leader in renewable energy. parliament also considers that the most effective way of ensuring energy security is through better coordination of national energy policies, the creation of a genuine energy union with a common energy market and a common energy policy, and cooperation between member states in this area, in accordance with the principles of solidarity and trust.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the eu strategy for lng and gas storage is one element of the energy union, which aims to gives concrete expression to the eu’s ambition to bring about a quick transition to a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system, and also aims to end dependence on external gas suppliers. therefore it is crucial that lng and storage operators, in cooperation with national regulatory authorities, would develop new flexible products and services, compliant with the eu current legislation, in order to make lng regasification and storing more attractive and maximise the utilisation of existing lng and storage facilities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu strategy for the use and storage of liquefied natural gas. liquefied natural gas (lng) offers europe the opportunity to increase competitiveness and security of supply by reducing the price of natural gas. the role of lng and gas storage, together with increased consumption efficiency and the use of renewable energy sources, is crucial in reducing dependence on russian gas.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. a common and robust strategy for the use and storage of lng in the eu should be implemented to help break the energy isolation and reduce the eu's dependence on gas in the long term. in particular, there is a need for better coordination of national energy policies, as further integration of energy policies is in the interests of all member states, taking into account their interests and those of their citizens. it should be noted that the existing and planned lng terminals need to be used as efficiently as possible. the diversification and flexibility of the eu gas system is necessary to ensure security of gas supply, competitiveness and resilience of the supply system. particular attention should be paid to the project to double the capacity of the nord stream pipeline under the baltic sea and its threat to the eu's energy security as a whole.
in writing. ‒ the the question has a double meaning. on the one hand, the report itself should be seen as written from a purely economic perspective, without taking into account the environmental impact of the increase in the use of natural gas. it is a pity that the rapporteur has failed to take account of the constructive proposals of the greens. on the other hand, the report emphasises the very important issue of energy independence and mentions the prospects for the creation of a natural gas market. this is particularly important for energy markets still isolated from the rest of the eu, such as the baltic states. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment and the environmentally sound use of energy is a very important one.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the harmonisation of fisheries controls in europe. fishermen often complain that they are subject to much stricter fisheries controls than other fishermen in another member state or in other types of fishing. i therefore support the idea that eu fisheries rules should apply equally to all fishermen. it is also necessary to extend controls to cover the whole production chain and to assign inspection at sea to a single authority in order to avoid duplication of controls.

in writing. ‒ the i voted for this report on how to harmonise fisheries controls in europe, which was also supported by the ep. the fisheries sector is one of the most important sectors for those interested in the sustainable management of the seas and oceans. eu rules are applied in a substantially different way across member states, as each member state has its own separate legal system and administrative structures, and these differences are inevitably reflected. therefore, in order to strengthen the control of products entering the eu from illegal, undeclared fishing, it is necessary to ensure a uniform level of fisheries control in all member states by harmonising the legal framework. the ep calls on the member states and their respective maritime fisheries control authorities to set up specialised groups of fisheries inspectors and to promote greater cooperation between member states in order to exchange information, control methods and data. the ep believes that the member states, the european fisheries control agency and the commission need to cooperate and coordinate more closely.
in writing. ‒ the issue of harmonising fisheries controls is of particular relevance, as it reflects the dichotomy between the north and the south, i.e. the more prosperous and advanced countries, and the east and the west, i.e. the old and the new eu member states. i am convinced that the speediest possible harmonisation of these economic activities, while ensuring the environmental component of fishing, such as the observance and control of the fishing gear regime, the uniform regulation of nets and other fishing gear, and the provision of flexibility for specific areas and waters, would make a significant contribution to the creation of a more integrated europe.
in writing. ‒ connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure have a major impact on economic growth, competitiveness, employment and territorial cohesion in the eu and its regions. i agree that the ep should support the process of building this trans-european transport network (ten-t) and continue to address the outstanding issues of transport infrastructure connections and accessibility in the eu's central and eastern europe region, connecting estonia, latvia, lithuania, poland, the czech republic, slovakia, hungary, slovenia, croatia, romania and bulgaria. it is clear that the member states and the commission must focus in particular on how to bridge the gap, remove obstacles and ensure a single link for both passenger and freight transport.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the improvement of connectivity and access to transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. quality transport highways are crucial for economic activity in europe and for the quality of life of our citizens. easily accessible and well-connected transport networks, which take account of local, regional, national and cross-border aspects of passenger and freight transport, are the basis for promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion within and between eu member states. at european level, the trans-european transport network (ten-t) aims to develop an integrated multimodal transport network across the eu, thereby promoting the interconnection and interoperability of national networks and access to this network. the ten-t guidelines and the european infrastructure networks instrument were developed in 2013 and set out the main pillars for the implementation of the eu transport infrastructure policy until 2020. in the design and implementation of projects, member states and the eu will need to pool their resources and work closely together to complete the strategic core network by 2030 and the comprehensive transport network by 2050. the european parliament believes that now is the time for parliament to support the process of building this trans-european transport network and to continue to address the outstanding issues of transport infrastructure connections and accessibility in the eu's central and eastern europe region by connecting estonia, latvia, lithuania, poland, the czech republic, slovakia, hungary, slovenia, croatia, romania and bulgaria.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. it is the right time for the european parliament to keep up the momentum of the new ten-t process and further address open challenges regarding the accessibility and connectivity of the transport infrastructure in the member states of the central and eastern european part of the eu, bringing together estonia, latvia, lithuania, poland, the czech republic, slovakia, hungary, slovenia, croatia, romania and bulgaria. the transport infrastructure in member states of this part of the eu has certainly undergone substantial modernisation and improvements, with constant help by the eu, from the pre-accession period to date.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep report on transport infrastructure connections and accessibility in central and eastern europe. connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure have a significant impact on economic growth and competitiveness. as the improvement of transport infrastructure will continue to require significant investments, it is important that the member states of central and eastern europe and the commission further strengthen the comprehensive coordination of transport policy and project planning at all stages. it is also important to exploit the full synergies of the financing of the european structural and investment funds and the european infrastructure networks instrument, as well as the resources of the european investment bank and the european bank for reconstruction and development.
in writing. ‒ the the text of the communication is, as it were, a motivation in itself to support it. unfortunately, central and eastern europe does not yet have the same quality of transport infrastructure as western europe. and naturally, eu support is very valuable here. on the other hand, the report makes it clear that it proposes rather different projects, such as the construction of motorways in a well-developed italy, the construction of motorways through protected areas and many other activities with very uncertain prospects. i therefore refrained from supporting this report, noting that it very accurately reflected the need to complete the transport links currently under way, such as rail baltica, and that its quality was significantly reduced by the high level of enthusiasm for the construction of new highways.
in writing. ‒ the i supported the report by mep porąba because it unequivocally recommends improving transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe, which also includes lithuania. transport development is essential to the quality of life of our citizens and the efficient movement of goods. the report rightly calls on the ep to speed up the legislative process to improve existing and create new links from estonia via lithuania and poland to romania and bulgaria. the restoration of this area is essential to improve the currently inefficient cross-border links. this will also improve connectivity and access to the territories located in the eastern regions of the union. cooperation under macro-regional strategies will certainly help to solve many problems in transport policy.
in writing. ‒ currently there are insufficient instruments to ensure that the core european values laid out in article 2 of the treaty on european union are upheld. when countries join the eu it is ensured that they adhere to the eu values, but as illustrated by the recent developments in poland and hungary, once they are members there is no mechanism to guarantee that these values continue to be maintained. therefore, there is a need to establish a mechanism on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. this mechanism will oversee the implementation of eu values and will help prevent and correct any breaches made by member states. this mechanism must be applied to all member states equally, it should be a permanent mechanism, objective and evidence-based, and finally, there needs to be close involvement of member state governments. this drf pact will lead to a more united european union as it will strengthen the common core values shared among the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the establishment of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. although europe has a long tradition of democracy, the rule of law and civil liberties, the commission, as guardian of the treaties, has been reluctant to acknowledge or even completely refuse to recognise the commonly agreed rules and the eu's powers to enforce them when it tries to remind a member state of its obligations. the eu has a range of instruments to ensure respect for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, but the instruments are limited in scope and ineffective in themselves. i therefore agree that it is necessary to create a framework that enables the eu to address not only specific breaches of eu law, but also cases of (risk) threats to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the establishment of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. europe has a long tradition of democracy, the rule of law and civil liberties. moreover, democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights are also the fundamental principles and objectives enshrined in the first articles of the treaties of the european union and one of the criteria for eu membership. on the issues of substance, the european union has a number of measures to ensure compliance with its legislation and the treaties. the european commission can instruct member states to adjust their budgets, public health systems or taxation decisions to comply with eu law. in such cases, member states do not argue that they are obliged to comply with eu law under the eu treaties. however, the situation is different when it comes to the obligations laid down in the treaties in the fields of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the european commission, as guardian of the treaties, has been reluctant to acknowledge or refused to acknowledge the commonly agreed rules and the eu's powers to enforce them, when it reminds a member state of its obligations. the commission's actions in this area have been timid and not always taken. it is therefore necessary to establish a framework that enables the eu to address not only specific breaches of eu law, but also threats to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the new eu mechanism should ensure that all eu member states respect the values enshrined in the eu treaties and set clear, evidence-based and non-political criteria for assessing their records on democracy, rule of law and fundamental rights (drf) in a systematic way and on an equal footing. therefore the aim is to incorporate existing drf tools in a single instrument and ensure that they are used to the full.
mr president, vice-president of the commission. a few offers, maybe more christmas. first, it is the european union's identity crisis. we cannot stand any longer at the crossroads between a federal european union and a european union of nation states. and the decision must be swift and clear: it is necessary to forget any federalist ambitions, to abandon the ideology of globalism and the attempt to bulldoze the citizens of the european states with solutions of dubious value. two: change the way we think about immigration policy. abandon the quotas by distributing refugees among the countries of the european union. strengthen the european union's external borders by sending a clear message that they will be closed to economic migrants from third countries. and actually close them. and the third. democracy is not a dictate from the brussels institutions to the community's members, disguised as concern for its fate. restoring trust in the institutions, restoring trust in commissioners and taking decisions for the good of society - this is the best thing the european commission could start doing without waiting for 2017.

in writing. i am very pleased that all member states have finally agreed on this very important directive. websites and mobile applications of ministries, hospitals, courts and other public institutions will be made more accessible to disabled and older people. they can use aids such as screen readers, alternative text or audio information to help them navigate the internet. we in the european parliament have made it possible for the new rules to cover mobile applications. the websites will have to publish information on their compliance with the new eu rules, as well as what content does not comply and why. browsers will have the possibility to notify website owners of non-compliance with accessibility requirements. some of the content of the websites, such as the formats of software files, pre-recorded video or audio clips or archived content, may not be compatible with them, but this information must be provided to the user in an appropriate manner and format upon request. this provision was also introduced by parliament. the rules have now been agreed with the eu council, removing the obstacles to their entry into force. eu countries will have almost two years to transpose these rules into their own law. by then, the newly developed websites will have to be adapted to the new requirements in another two years, the newly developed websites in one year and all mobile applications in almost three years.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on plant protection products and amending the regulations of the european parliament and of the council. the general objective of the regulation is to halt the risks posed by new pests and diseases in the plant health sector, which are the result of global trade and climate change. the objective is to modernise plant health measures relating to trade both within the eu and with third countries, with a focus on risk-based approaches.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which deals with plant protection measures. plant health is of key importance for plant production, for mosses, for natural natural habitats and planted areas, for natural ecosystems, for ecosystem services and for biodiversity in the union. species harmful to plants and plant products are a threat to plant health and the threat of their introduction into the european union is currently increased by the globalisation of trade and climate change. in order to combat this threat, it is necessary to adopt measures to identify and reduce to an acceptable level the phytosanitary risk posed by those pests. the need for such measures has long been recognised. criteria should therefore be established to identify pests for which measures are necessary to prevent their introduction into and spread throughout the eu. such pests are referred to as european union quarantine pests. criteria for the identification of pests for which it is necessary to adopt control measures applicable only to one or more parts of that site should also be laid down. such pests are referred to as protected zone quarantine pests. where those pests are plants, particular attention should be paid in the implementation of this regulation to those plants which are parasitic on other plants and are the most harmful to plant health.
in writing. ‒ the i supported the recommendation of the ep on amendments to the plant health regulations. the current eu plant health regulatory framework aims to protect the european agricultural and forestry sectors from harmful organisms by preventing their entry into and spread within the eu. the increase in imports in recent years has led to a large number of hotbeds of dangerous pests, which have caused serious damage to forestry. the evaluation of the system put in place in 2010 has shown that amendments to the basic legislation are needed to cover all aspects of this increased risk. the amendments adopted give greater emphasis to prevention, establish a classification of harmful organisms by importance at eu level and in all 28 member states, establish more effective measures to control the emergence and spread of harmful organisms, and improve the regulatory measures for intra-eu movement.
in writing. ‒ the european economic outlook for spring 2016 forecasts that the eu economy will grow more slowly than expected, with euro area gdp expected to grow by only 1.6% and reach 1.8% in 2017. the eu also faces challenges related to a deteriorating international environment and the failure to implement sustainable reforms. i therefore welcome the commission's focus in its 2016 country specific recommendations on three key priorities for further boosting economic growth: investment in innovation, support for growth and job creation, implementation of structural reforms and promotion of sound public financial management. however, the commission should make greater efforts to promote fiscal sustainability in line with the stability and growth pact, while fully applying its flexibility provisions in line with the commission communication of 13 january 2015.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines the implementation of the priorities of the european semester for the coordination of economic policies 2016. while we are striving for growth and jobs throughout the european union, the situation is still not improving in many member states, particularly in the areas of social affairs, employment and education. child poverty has increased particularly in europe, with some 20 million children living in or near poverty. i therefore call on the commission and the member states to create the child guarantee, a specific instrument with a specific budget to ensure that every child in europe has access to free health and childcare, education, decent housing and adequate nutrition. the commission and the member states should therefore ensure and implement in their policy programmes, taking into account the recommendations made by the ep, that all people have access to the necessary and adequate social protection, health and social services. increased integration of vulnerable groups into the labour market, reduction of working poverty, promotion of gender equality are needed. it is also necessary to promote health and safety at work, strengthen the rights of workers in precarious employment and in non-standard employment contracts and provide for greater social protection for the self-employed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the eu economy will grow less than expected on the basis of the european economic spring forecast 2016, as gdp in the eurozone is expected to increase by only 1.6%, reaching 1.8% by 2017. however, the eu responsible institutions should focus on three main priorities to further strengthen economic growth: supporting investment for innovation, growth and job creation, pursuing socially balanced structural reforms and encouraging responsible public finance.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed the report prepared by the ep which reviews the implementation of the priorities of the european semester for economic policy coordination 2016. i welcome the fact that the commission, in its country-specific recommendations, gives high priority to the three main priorities for growth: investment in innovation, growth and jobs, and structural reforms. however, i believe that the commission should do more to promote fiscal sustainability in line with the stability and growth pact, and take new effective measures to combat social inequality, exclusion and poverty.
in writing. ‒ food products, which are mostly processed, contain trans fats that can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, alzheimer's disease or diabetes, and also promote obesity. also, even a third of consumers are unaware of trans fats, even though they are listed on food labels. in this context, i agree that, in addition to the labelling of products, a maximum level of these fats in food should be established at eu level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because the issue of fatty acid transistors (fats) is a priority for parliament and it reiterates its concern about the risks to human health posed by fats. the european parliament underlines that the us has already informed that, in view of the conclusion of 2015 that transisomers of fatty acids are generally not considered safe, food manufacturers will have to remove partially hydrogenated oils from products sold on the us market from mid-2018. parliament also stresses that many eu citizens, especially the most vulnerable, lack information on fatty acid transistors and their health effects, which may hinder consumers from making informed choices about products. according to the world health organisation (who), therefore, the implementation of labelling of fatty acid transistors is likely to be the main cost and the financial impact of the insurance in countries that have implemented the ban on fatty acid transistors has been minimal, given the low cost of implementation and monitoring. the european parliament requests that such a proposal be accompanied by an impact assessment assessing the costs of industrial restructuring resulting from the mandatory threshold and the possibility of passing those costs on to consumers. it also asked the commission to cooperate with the member states to raise awareness of nutrition issues and to enable consumers to make healthier choices, and to cooperate with industry to encourage the substitution of healthier ingredients in their products.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. with the given resolution the eu places mandatory limits on industrially-produced trans-fatty acids (tfa) which may increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer’s, diabetes and obesity for consumers. denmark was the first eu member state to limit the content of trans fats in oils and fats by law in 2003. the statistics showed that it was a successful legal decision because it significantly reduced deaths caused by cardiovascular disease.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the ep resolution on fatty acid transisomers (fat). industrial trans fats are used in a wide range of food products, from fast food and margarine to chips and sweets. however, studies indicate that excessive consumption may lead to cardiovascular disease, diabetes, atherosclerosis, and obesity. heart disease kills 660,000 people in the eu each year, or 14% of all deaths in the eu. the aim of this resolution is therefore to call for a limitation of the use of these artificial fats. there is currently no regulation at eu level on the restriction or labelling of trans fats. however, some measures are provided for in individual member states. for example, in 2006, food manufacturers in the united states were required to indicate on labels whether their products contained trans fats. this has led the food industry to significantly reduce their use. the introduction of mandatory restrictions is the most effective solution and would help to reduce the impact of the main sources of trans fats and save lives.
it has been rightly noted that it is necessary to restore the confidence of our citizens in the institutions of the european union, and the role of the court of auditors in this process is very important. for several years now, they have stressed in their reports the need for better financial management at both the commission and the member states' level. however, this year it was found that the high level of errors persisted in 2015, in particular in the cost compensation schemes. this situation is not satisfactory and the commission and the member states are not making sufficient efforts to change the principles of payment and control. it should be noted that a growing number of financial instruments, such as the fund for strategic investments, are not financed from the budget of the european union and are not subject to audit. this poses a serious threat to financial reporting and distorts the principles of sound financial management and control. the commission must reform the financial management of the european union to ensure that it delivers real added value and enhances credibility for the whole of the european union and its citizens.

the political situation in belarus still does not correspond to the principles of democracy, the rule of law, transparent and free elections, freedom of the media, respect for human rights and the abolition of the death penalty, which we support and promote. the recent parliamentary elections again failed to meet osce standards and cannot be considered transparent and fair. we hear both criticism and praise in the press for lukashenka's break with 12 years of ruling party monopoly in parliament: the two appointed, not elected, opposition seats in the parliament do not in any way prove belarus's determination to move towards greater democracy. the unstable geopolitical situation in the region and the growing pressure from russia on the eastern partnership countries, the construction of the astravyansk power plant, force us to seek dialogue with this country. we need to have a very clear strategy for moving belarus in a european direction and for finding a rational balance between what is happening in the country and the long-term prospects for belarus, bringing it closer to europe, especially after the end of the current administration. i think we have to find ways and solutions now to gain the trust of the belarusian public in europe. at the same time, cooperation with opposition political parties, non-governmental organisations, civil society and other institutions in belarus that show a willingness to pursue a democratic path should be strengthened.
the steps taken by minsk to regain the favour of the european union can be welcomed. but let us ask ourselves, how much are the promises of belarus worth? for example, as far back as 2011, belarus made a political commitment to carry out so-called 'stress tests' at the newly built astrakhan nuclear power plant. almost five years have passed, the atomic monster is visible from the lithuanian hills, and the stress tests have not yet begun. moreover, following a visit by a commission representative to astrava last month, it became clear that belarus had not yet decided whether it would carry out these 'stress tests' in full, in accordance with the european union methodology. they won't send a final answer until the end of the month. and today is october 26th. i therefore ask what pressure measures the commission is prepared to apply by the end of october if we still do not receive concrete confirmation that belarus will carry out 'stress tests' at full capacity at the new nuclear power plant. thank you. thank you.

in writing. ‒ currently, 191 states are parties to the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons, including five states that are recognised as nuclear weapons states: the united states, the united kingdom, russia, france and china. the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons is a landmark international treaty aimed at preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons and weapons technology. i therefore agree that the nuclear non-proliferation goals must provide the basis for a global effort to prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons, to promote the safe and peaceful use of nuclear energy for civilian purposes and to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, which deals with nuclear safety and non-proliferation. the european parliament is deeply concerned about the deteriorating security environment around the european union and beyond its neighbourhood, as nuclear weapons could once again be used as active deterrents and acquired by state and non-state actors, and is deeply concerned about the lack of effective disarmament and non-proliferation measures. it therefore calls on all nuclear-weapon states to take concrete interim measures to reduce the risk of nuclear weapons detonating, including by reducing the use status of nuclear weapons and moving them from deployment sites to storage sites, reducing the role of nuclear weapons in military doctrines and rapidly reducing the stock of all types of nuclear weapons. parliament endorses the 2016 nuclear security summit, which recognised that the illicit trade in and use of nuclear materials poses a direct and significant threat to global security, and expects full traceability and physical protection of all weapons-grade materials to be pursued.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour. a deep concern was expressed about the deterioration of the security environment around the european union and beyond its neighbourhood, which could lead to the re-emergence of nuclear weapons. therefore i support the 2016 nuclear security summit, recognising that the unauthorised trade in and use of nuclear materials is an immediate and serious threat to global security, and it is important to achieve the complete tracking and physical securing of all weapons-grade materials.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this resolution. the security environment in the world, including in the eu, is becoming increasingly volatile, unstable and unpredictable. we cannot help but notice the deterioration of relations between nuclear-armed nations, such as the russian federation and the united states, india and pakistan. we are following with concern the reports of north korea's nuclear tests. the deployment of nuclear-capable iskander missile systems in the kaliningrad area by russia in military exercises simulating the use of nuclear weapons against poland is also of particular concern. in view of these and many other aspects, the european parliament regrets that nuclear weapons are again playing an important role in the strategic plans of the states possessing them. the resolution calls for dialogue with all nuclear-weapon states and for a common agenda aimed at the gradual reduction of nuclear warhead stockpiles. parliament recommends the establishment of nuclear-weapon-free zones, which would be a positive step towards a world without nuclear weapons and contribute to the creation of overall stability. parliament also called on the united nations general assembly to convene in 2017 a negotiating conference open to all states on a legally binding instrument to prohibit nuclear weapons, with a view to their ultimate abolition. it is expected that this will reinforce the non-proliferation and disarmament objectives and commitments set out in the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons and help to facilitate global security.
