in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, which deals with the european voluntary service and the promotion of volunteering in europe. the european parliament recognises that voluntary activity is an expression of solidarity, freedom and responsibility and that such activity contributes to the strengthening of active citizenship and personal development, and that it is a crucial tool for social inclusion and cohesion, training, education and intercultural dialogue, and that it contributes significantly to the dissemination of european values. furthermore, stresses that its value as a strategic tool for promoting mutual understanding and intercultural contacts is also recognised in voluntary activities related to third countries. parliament stressed the importance of establishing a european voluntary service framework as a legal framework to define the status of voluntary service (with the corresponding rights and obligations), facilitate mobility and recognition of skills. it therefore calls on the member states that have yet to establish a legal environment for volunteers to use the recommendations set out in the european voluntary policy agenda and the european charter on the rights and responsibilities of volunteers. calls on the commission to continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on the prevention of and fight against fraud, corruption and organised crime, and to report regularly on the implementation of the union's policy on the prevention of and fight against fraud;

in writing. ‒ agriculture covers most of europe's territory, but is currently only a small part of the working population in rural areas. moreover, the majority of cap direct payments go to the richest farms and in 2014 only 13% of beneficiaries received 74% of cap direct payments. i think that this is not helping to create jobs in agriculture and small farms need more labour, because 53% of farm workers are working on farms that are classified as small economically. i therefore support the need to better distribute cap payments to small farmers.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines how the implementation of the common agricultural policy (cap) can improve job creation in rural areas. the european parliament underlines the importance of the agricultural and agri-products sector for social and territorial cohesion, given its role in sustainable economic growth, the creation of quality jobs and the preservation of rural communities. stresses also the need to preserve the cap budget and to strengthen its social and economic role, with particular attention to micro and small farms and taking into account the specificities of the regions; it is also essential that the effective implementation of the cap contributes to social inclusion in rural areas, ensuring decent living and working conditions and good prospects for the future. parliament stresses the importance of territorial cohesion in the eu and that it should be implemented through economic development policies that respond to the challenges facing rural areas. notes, moreover, the strong link between rural systems, small communities and municipalities, and therefore calls for better synergies between cohesion policy instruments and the cap; parliament called on the member states to encourage young farmers to participate in vocational training under the erasmus+ programme, in particular the part devoted to practical training, in order to encourage them to acquire new technical and linguistic skills abroad.

in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report on 'how the implementation of the common agricultural policy (cap) can improve job creation in rural areas'. the report contains a number of provisions that criticise the eu's negotiations on free trade agreements (ttip, ceta, mercosur). i believe that free trade agreements can open up particularly large and profitable markets in the united states, canada and south america for the products of our farmers.
in writing. ‒ europe's rural areas are in crisis. a crisis that is manifested not only in fluctuating prices, in farmers' incomes that do not cover the costs, in the abuse of intermediaries, but also in the rapidly decreasing number of people living in rural areas and working in agriculture. between 2000 and 2012, almost 5 million jobs in european agriculture disappeared. the small farms are being replaced by 'mega-farms'. is this the kind of european agriculture we want? as a shadow rapporteur, i can say that this report is very well written. it provides a vision of what the european countryside needs from the current cap reform and the new cap. i can only emphasise further that we must aim for a more rural and quality food, clean environment oriented european cap. we must also seek a level playing field for farmers, in particular through the harmonisation of direct payments.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for mr andriessen's report. i agree that the cap should facilitate job creation in rural areas. the economic development of these areas needs to be analysed and understood in relation to their social and demographic development. this requires greater support for families living in rural areas and the search for new solutions in the labour market, for example through greater promotion of services in the agricultural sector. the cap is one of the main instruments that should be used to this end in order to give european agriculture the chance to emerge from the unprecedented crisis in which it is currently found.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the annual report 2015 of the european central bank. the euro area is still characterised by high unemployment, excessively low inflation and large macroeconomic imbalances, including a current account deficit. in addition, euro area countries are characterised by low productivity growth, driven by a lack of investment, failure to implement structural reforms and weak domestic demand. i agree with the ecb president, mr draghi, that monetary policy alone cannot boost aggregate demand growth and that it must be complemented at member state level by sound fiscal policies and broad and socially balanced structural reform programmes. the demographic situation in europe should also be fully taken into account in the implementation of socially balanced structural economic and labour market reforms and a more balanced demographic policy should be promoted. it is also important that the ecb carefully assess the risk of future asset and housing price bubbles arising from the ecb's ultra-low (negative) interest rate policy, given the significant increase in borrowing and the disproportionate rise in property prices, especially in some large cities. i agree with the position that national economic policies should be coordinated, particularly in the euro area, in order to achieve economic growth.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. we must admit that the security situation in europe has deteriorated considerably. it has become more complex, more dangerous, and more unpredictable. traditional and hybrid threats are posed by state and non-state actors, originate from the south and the east and have different effects on member states. the security of eu member states is closely interlinked, but their responses to common threats and risks are uncoordinated and inconsistent. the lack of coordination is one of the weaknesses of the union's action, which has been successfully exploited by the aggressors. europe also lacks the resilience to effectively counter hybrid threats. i agree with the rapporteur that for these reasons a thorough and substantial review of the csdp is needed to enable the eu and its member states to make a decisive contribution to the security of the union, to international crisis management and to demonstrate the eu's strategic autonomy. clearly, no country can cope with the current security challenges on its own. it is therefore necessary to achieve that the csdp is based on a strong principle of collective defence and effective financing and is implemented in coordination with international institutions in the field of security and defence, fully complementing nato. the eu should encourage member states to adhere to the nato-defined capability level requiring a minimum of 2% of gdp for defence spending, as reaffirmed at the wales and warsaw summits.
in writing. ‒ these past years have sadly marked a shift in europe’s security environment. we face tensions from russian aggression, terrorist threats in our own region, and the uncertainty left after the uk referendum and the us elections. all of these issues call upon us to work together in one of the most vital cornerstones of any society – its safety and security. which is why this time provides us the best window of opportunity to implement the common security and defence policy that would in no way compete with a similar transnational structure – nato – but on the contrary, would complement and strengthen its current agenda. this policy is not one of militarising europe, but rather increasing its readiness and capabilities for its defence. a large part of the report focuses on the sheer capabilities that the eu currently lacks in the defence sector, which is why it also calls for investments in defence research in order to catch up with the quickly advancing technologies all around the world. only through these strategies will we be able to independently ensure the safety and security of our citizens in these turbulent times.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. the security environment in europe has significantly deteriorated and become less stable, more complex, more dangerous and less predictable. europe currently lacks the resilience to effectively counter hybrid threats, which are often cross-border in nature. i therefore agree that a review of the common security and defence policy (csdp) is necessary to enable the eu and its member states to make a strong contribution to the security of the union, to international crisis management and to demonstrate the eu's strategic autonomy.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is a report which parliament is putting forward on the implementation of a common security and defence policy in the european union. the european security environment has significantly deteriorated and has become less stable, more complex, more dangerous and less predictable, with threats that are both traditional and hybrid, posed by state and non-state actors, originating from the south and the east, and affecting member states differently. parliament recalled that the security of the eu member states is closely interlinked and noted that their response to common threats and risks has so far been uncoordinated and inconsistent, making it difficult and impeding a more general approach. such a lack of coordination is one of the weaknesses of union action. europe lacks the resilience to effectively counter hybrid threats, which are often cross-border in nature. terrorism against europe by radical islamist organisations and individuals is unprecedented and is putting pressure on the european way of life. parliament stressed that this had made personal safety a priority and blurred the traditional distinction between the external and internal aspects of such safety. calls therefore on the eu to adapt to these security challenges, in particular by making more effective use of the existing csdp instruments and by coordinating them with other external and internal instruments, and calls for greater cooperation and coordination between member states, in particular in the fight against terrorism;
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's report. in view of the complex geopolitical situation, we must make every effort to ensure our security and to strengthen cooperation and mutual understanding between european member states in the field of csdp.
in writing. ‒ the i believe that the military component of the common security and defence policy should not be increased and developed. the most important objective for european states today is not only to strengthen their own armed forces but also to pursue a much wider political and diplomatic dialogue. only a more united and therefore more effective european foreign and security policy can make a decisive contribution to the de-escalation of the armed conflict in iraq and syria and to the fight against the islamic state. in addition, a stronger preventive policy based on comprehensive deradicalization programmes, a more effective response to the spread of extremist content online and a stronger judicial cooperation between criminal justice systems are needed. the eu cannot be allowed to finance the defence sector and defence research. i do not support the proposal to deploy eu combat teams for any crisis management task. i believe that a new arms race or new military arrangements are by no means a way of escaping ever-growing tensions. they can only be catalysts for greater tensions. if we cannot properly address social problems because of the additional funding needed for new military needs, we may find that these problems flare up in the most disgusting ways.
in writing. ‒ the the report is an important topic in the implementation of the eu's common security and defence policy, but it is rather weak. i think it focuses too much and even overly sensitive on the threat of terrorism and too little on the issue of the eu's defence capability against conventional military threats. the threat of terrorism has always been and remains a police function, which should not be confused with the role of the military. at the same time, more provisions could be included in the text on strengthening military cooperation between eu member states, reducing technological backwardness compared to the us, and assessing factors such as the russian threat. part of these provisions are contained in the proposed amendments. if they are rejected, this resolution will become a weak document, not in keeping with its original aims.
in writing. i note with concern that the terrorism directed against europe by radical islamist organisations and individuals is of unprecedented scale and is putting pressure on the european way of life; i stress that this has made personal security a priority and the traditional distinction between external and internal aspects of such security is disappearing.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on eu strategic communication to counteract propaganda by third parties against the eu and its member states. i support the concern expressed in the resolution about the rapidly growing kremlin disinformation and propaganda in europe, including disinformation and propaganda to maintain or increase russian influence and with the aim of weakening and dividing the eu. one of the kremlin's propaganda aims is to portray certain european states as traditionally belonging to the russian sphere of influence, thus undermining their sovereignty and european identity. the fight against kremlin discourse therefore requires raising awareness of the crimes committed by the communist regime, public information campaigns and the use of education systems and support for research and document examination activities in the eu member states. it is also essential that the eu acts in a united and coordinated way in applying the means and instruments to combat propaganda. this is particularly important for the baltic states, which are becoming the front line of russia's information warfare. in lithuania, the kremlin is using a complex strategy of propaganda and disinformation, seeking to imply that traditional lithuanian values and the rest of western european values are different, and to show that lithuania is unassailable and therefore not worth defending. the national security services need to be brought together to counter the kremlin's propaganda, but i would like to stress that their autonomy must be maintained in order to ensure effective information gathering and the safeguarding of state secrets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on eu strategic communication to counteract propaganda against it by third parties. european society is facing an active campaign of disinformation, propaganda and growing radicalisation. at present, strategic communication and information warfare are not only an external but also an internal issue for the eu. i therefore support the need to adopt an eu strategic communication action plan to counter propaganda, disinformation and growing radicalisation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is the one in which parliament spoke about the eu's strategic communication to counteract propaganda against it by third parties. the eu, its member states and its citizens are facing increasing systemic pressure to act on information, disinformation and disinformation campaigns and propaganda from countries and non-state actors such as cross-border terrorist or criminal organisations in the eu's neighbourhood. anti-eu propaganda takes many forms and uses a variety of means, often tailored to the specificities of eu member states, in order to distort the truth, create doubt, antagonise member states, promote strategic isolation between eu and nato partners and paralyse decision-making, discredit the eu institutions and transatlantic partnerships, which are of recognised importance to the european security system and economic structure, in the eyes and minds of citizens of the eu and its neighbouring countries, and undermine or challenge european political discourse based on democratic values, human rights and the rule of law. parliament therefore calls on the eu institutions to recognise that strategic communication and information warfare are not only an external but also an internal issue for the eu, and expresses concern at the limited perception in some member states of being audiences and arenas for propaganda and disinformation.
in writing. - i voted for this report. in recent years, european countries have been confronted with particularly intensive campaigns of propaganda and disinformation aimed at undermining the fundamental democratic values that europe cherishes, undermining the unity of the eu member states and fomenting destruction. the russian federation has been involved in the recruitment and use of foreign fighters in the drc. the most effective european response to these campaigns is to raise public awareness of the specific nature of these campaigns, their sponsors, their sources of funding and the real motives behind them. education is the most important factor in enabling citizens to critically analyse media content and react to disinformation.
in writing. ‒ the we must take comprehensive action to combat radicalisation and terrorist propaganda. in particular, greater attention must be paid to measures for closer cooperation between the member states and the eu. action to counter the threat of terrorism must be strengthened, while respecting human rights and the rule of law. however, in the fight against anti-eu propaganda and disinformation, constructive relations with third countries should be pursued. it should be noted that the promotion of wider political and diplomatic dialogue and peaceful cooperation arrangements with neighbouring third countries is necessary to alleviate tensions. it is necessary to prevent daesh from receiving financing and funds from oil or arms trafficking. some member states should therefore review their relations with certain third countries accordingly, as this is particularly important to prevent radicalisation and protect eu values.
in writing. ‒ we live in an information society, where publicly communicated knowledge is of paramount importance. not only does this facilitate the rapid spread of knowledge, skills and experience, but it also makes our society highly vulnerable to attacks, lies and propaganda from hostile forces. the document under consideration is very timely and necessary to help combat lies and propaganda. i'm unambiguously in favor of it. i would also like to point out that even the best legislation will not solve these problems once and for all. the only long-term and sustainable solution is an active, well-informed civil society, able to stand up and resist lies and propaganda. it is the support for the strengthening of such a society that must be a key part of the eu's information policy and a priority of strategic communication.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the resolution on sign language and professional sign language interpreters. all persons with disabilities, in particular women and children, as well as deaf and hard of hearing persons, shall enjoy the same rights and shall have the right to dignity of the person, to independent living, to self-determination and to full participation in the life of the community. i therefore agree that there is a need for qualified professional sign language interpreters whose status must be guaranteed by official recognition of national and regional sign languages in the member states and the eu institutions, by formal training (university or similar, equivalent to 3 years of full-time study and meeting the requirements for the training of spoken language interpreters), by registration (official accreditation and quality control system, e.g. through continuous professional development), and by official recognition of the profession. i agree that sign language translation is a professional service that should be properly remunerated.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on sign languages and professional sign language interpreters. there are about 1 million sign language users in the eu and 51 million citizens with hearing impairments, many of whom also use sign language. citizens with hearing impairments have the right to autonomy and full participation in public life, and sign language interpreters are essential to ensure this. however, the situation of sign language interpreters varies widely between member states: in some cases they are informal family helpers, in others they are fully qualified university-trained professional interpreters. there is also a shortage of qualified professional sign language interpreters in all member states. i therefore agree that it is necessary to ensure that there are qualified sign language professionals and that they are adequately remunerated. all sign language users must also have access to the same information and means of communication as everyone else, by ensuring sign language translation, subtitling, voice-to-text services and/or alternative means of communication.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution because it was the one in which parliament spoke in favour of strengthening the profession of sign language and sign language interpreters in the european union. the resolution calls for the recognition of sign languages as official languages in the european union and for the strengthening of the profession of sign language interpreter. almost 52 million people in the european union use sign languages, but the profession of sign language interpreter is not recognised in all member states and in many it is not yet taught at university. i believe that deaf and blind people and people with hearing impairments should have access to the same information, communication and learning opportunities as everyone else. we have to provide sign language translation, subtitling, voice-to-text services, and interpreters.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution. sign language users must have better access to information and conditions ensuring their full participation in public life. the training of qualified professional sign language interpreters and the provision of working conditions for them is also of particular importance for these purposes.
in writing. ‒ the i support the motion for a resolution. it should be noted that accessibility is a prerequisite for the full participation of deaf, deaf-blind and hard of hearing people in society, with full autonomy and equal rights. they must have access to the same information and means of communication as everyone else. in this context, it is necessary to provide for increased aid and more specific measures. all the better, sign language should be included in educational programmes to raise awareness and promote the use of sign languages. the necessary accommodation measures, including the provision of professional sign language interpreters, must be in place to ensure equal opportunities in employment, education and training. in addition, national and regional sign language (s) should be officially recognised in the member states and in the eu institutions and working conditions for sign language interpreters should be improved.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the renewal of the authorisation of the active substance benzatone, as the assessment of the representative use of the active substance benzatone was not sufficient to conclude that the plant protection product containing the active substance would not adversely affect human or animal health or groundwater or would not have an unacceptable impact on the environment. as there is still insufficient information on the safety of benzatone, i cannot support the amendments by colleague pavel poc, which call on the commission to approve benzatone by 31 july 2024, i.e. for 7.5 years. the amount of harmful substances already present in our environment is such that the use of another harmful substance cannot be tolerated. since the pavel poc amendment was nevertheless adopted, i had to vote against the entire resolution. i hope that the commission will receive the missing information and make a thorough assessment before adopting the decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the objection under rule 106 of the rules of procedure: renewal of the authorisation of the active substance benzatone. by commission implementing regulation of 8 april 2016, the approval of the active substance benzazone was extended until 30 june 2017 as a consequence of a deferred assessment of the substance. however, following the comments received in the expiry review report, it was decided that efsa should carry out an expert consultation and conclude whether the active substance benthazone can be expected to meet the conditions laid down in the regulation of the european parliament and of the council. based on the efsa conclusions, it was concluded that the evaluation of the representative use of the active substance benzodiazepine was not sufficient. i therefore agree that the commission infringed the provisions of the regulation and the precautionary principle by applying the active substance benthazone.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution because it asks the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft to the committee. this implementing regulation was submitted in response to the renewal of the authorisation of the active substance benzatone. the active substance bentazone acts as a selective herbicide against weeds that have already emerged on the open ground, suitable for many crops and commonly used in agriculture. the active substance benthazone has a high potential for direct leakage to groundwater due to its characteristic properties. according to the uk environment agency, the active substance benthazone is the most commonly detected approved pesticide in uk groundwater, and can also be found on the surface of water, with a similar situation across europe. following the consideration of the comments received in the review report on the renewal, it was decided to request additional information from the applicants. the parliament also noted that the consumer risk assessment was not completed as the proposed sediment definitions for the assessment of the risk to plants and the impact on domestic animals were considered to be non-exhaustive due to the data gaps identified.
in writing. - i voted for the motion for a resolution. i agree with the experts that the commission failed to take all circumstances into account and to apply the precautionary principle when renewing the approval of the active substance benzazone. i agree with the provisions of the resolution which call on the commission to gather and evaluate the missing information before taking a decision. for these reasons, the european parliament asks the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft to the committee.
in writing. ‒ the i support the motion for a resolution. careful and careful selection of plant protection products is necessary to avoid the risks to human health and the environment from pesticides and to avoid contamination of water bodies, groundwater and soil. in my view, the authorisation of the active substance benzatone should not be renewed, given the adverse effects on the environment and human health of that substance. it should be noted that the commission's decision to approve an active substance at the same time as requesting data to confirm its safety will allow it to be placed on the market before the commission has all the data necessary to support that decision. such activities may have adverse effects on human or animal health, the environment and groundwater. in view of this, i think that the commission should withdraw its draft implementing regulation and submit a new draft to the committee. in addition, before adopting a decision to approve, the commission must request and assess the missing information.
in writing. i urge the commission to request and assess the missing information before taking a decision.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the development of the definitive vat system and the fight against fraud vat, other vat is a significant and growing source of eu revenue, generating almost €1 trillion in 2014. it accounts for about 7% of the eu's gross domestic product and is also one of the sources of the eu's own resources. the current vat system was not fraud-proof from the outset. despite various initiatives, fraud has not yet been reduced. the main obstacle to reforming the vat system is the need for unanimity among member states. the implementation of substantial reforms has been delayed or blocked by member states that continue to use their old primary systems and do not adequately fulfil their anti-fraud responsibilities and controls. i agree with the rapporteur that the establishment of a definitive vat system will contribute to the fight against vat fraud and that the proposed extension and application of the reverse charge system to all business transactions throughout the eu could be beneficial for a sustainable vat system. the application of this model would eliminate the need for the entire deduction and refund procedure, reduce distortions of competition and the financing and administrative burden on entrepreneurs.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the eu action plan to combat illegal wildlife trade. the trade in wild plants and animals has become a multi-billion euro criminal industry run by organised crime networks. the risk of detection is low and the financial reward is high - this encourages criminal groups to use wildlife caught and transported illegally to finance their criminal activities. i believe that the new 2016-2020 action plan will strengthen the eu's role in the global fight against wildlife trafficking through the priorities of prevention, enforcement, cooperation and recognition of the eu as a destination market and point of origin and transit for wildlife products. i agree with the rapporteurs that eu member states must take on a shared responsibility and make greater efforts to tackle this challenge and halt the rapid extinction of some of the most protected species. by doing so, we will not only preserve biodiversity for future generations, but also improve and support the eu's security system, improve the lives of local communities, accelerate sustainable development and strengthen the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ europe has been one of the biggest destination markets and transit points for illegal wildlife smuggling. not only do these practices take many endangered species to the brink of extinction, but they also create a security problem in many countries. because it is easy to harnessing, wildlife trafficking is preferred by many organized crime groups and terrorist organizations over smuggling such things as drugs, cigarettes or migrants. this action plan calls for three major goals and priorities. the first is start battling wildlife trafficking at its roots; this can be done through the many tools available to the european union already, such as those focusing on combating corruption or awareness raising campaigns. secondly, the action plan calls for more scrutiny and transparency when it comes to seizure information and data in member states. the third point focuses on global partnerships and how we should amend trade deals and incorporate clauses in future ones about wildlife trafficking and measures to stop it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the communication on goods temporarily removed from the customs territory of the union by sea or air amending regulation (eu) no 952/2013 establishing the union customs code. the relevant authorities in the member states have no legal basis under the current article 136 to apply the provisions specifically in the case of goods temporarily removed from the customs territory of the union by sea or air on a direct route between two places within that territory without a stop outside the union. in the absence of a clear legal basis to require the presentation of these goods to the customs authorities, the effective exercise of their customs supervision duties is therefore impeded. i therefore agree that it is necessary to remedy this shortcoming and thus ensure a level playing field for goods and to restore the legal basis established by the previous customs code.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it sets out parliament's position on amendments to the union customs code concerning goods temporarily removed from the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the 2016 review of the union customs code, its implementation and the delegated acts have shown that the text of the regulation contains certain loopholes the relevant authorities in the member states do not have a legal basis to apply certain provisions under the current article 136. these provisions relate to lodging the entry summary declaration, notification of arrival of the seagoing vessel or aircraft, delivery and presentation of the goods to customs after unloading or transhipment, waiting for the authorisation to be issued before unloading or transhipment, and temporary storage. these amendments address the deficiencies in the union customs code mentioned above.

in writing. i agree with the report. the first priority is to close the existing loopholes and ensure effective enforcement of the regulation. it should be noted that the customs union is an exclusive competence of the eu and that the responsibility for the implementation of customs legislation lies primarily with the member states. at present, member states are facing certain difficulties in applying certain customs provisions. in order to ensure the effective exercise of customs supervision duties, the authorities concerned should be empowered to apply the provisions of the eu customs code more broadly and effectively to goods temporarily removed from the customs territory of the union by sea or air.

in writing. i support the motion for a resolution. the recent earthquakes in italy have created an exceptional and very serious situation which needs to be addressed immediately and effectively. in particular, prevention should be an increasingly important stage in disaster management and should be given greater social importance. it is necessary to strengthen disaster prevention measures and to carry out the necessary scientific research in order to prevent adverse effects, manage crises and minimise the impact of disasters. the commission should consider offering the italian authorities all the assistance they need to ensure adequate living conditions for homeless people. in this context, the eu solidarity fund has a special role to play, as it must be a reliable and flexible instrument for demonstrating solidarity and providing adequate and rapid assistance to those affected by major natural disasters. in this context, i believe that the extension of the existing methods for calculating the solidarity fund should be considered. moreover, the commission should exclude investments in material recovery and earthquake-resistant construction when calculating the national deficit under the stability and growth pact.
in writing. ‒ the it is good to see that things are getting better in italy. the resolution under discussion today contains many important provisions, including a proposal to pay greater attention to both building seismic resistance and building supervision. the eu has also contributed to this end by providing for a temporary derogation from the methodology for calculating the budget deficit. at the same time, i would point out that the attempt by some italian politicians to enshrine provisions that these exemptions should remain permanent and that member states' expenditure on building seismic resistance should be excluded from the budget deficit calculation is likely to have the opposite effect: most of this expenditure will not reach its intended recipients and confidence in the eu's financial discipline policy will be completely undermined.
in writing. i draw attention to the predictability problems associated with earthquake systems and to the high seismic activity.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the guidelines for declarations of interests by members of the commission. annex xvi to the rules of procedure of the european parliament, the 'guidelines for the approval of the commission', provides that 'parliament may request any information necessary to enable it to take a decision on the suitability of the commissioners-designate. it expects to be disclosed all information relating to their financial interests. declarations of interests by the members of the commission appointed shall be referred to the committee responsible for legal affairs. unfortunately, that provision does not define precisely the scope of the inquiry by the committee on legal affairs, in particular as regards the question whether that inquiry should be limited to a formal examination of the information provided or, on the contrary, to an in-depth inquiry. i therefore support the rapporteur's proposal to define the scope of the examination of declarations of interests by the committee on legal affairs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which discusses the guidelines for declarations of interests by members of the commission. the european parliament proposes to define the scope of the examination of declarations of interests by the committee on legal affairs. this should include, in particular, the european parliament's internal procedures for the appointment of the new commission and its term of office and the transparency requirements for the members of the commission. the parliament considers that the verification of the absence of a conflict of interest cannot be equated with the assessment of the competence of a candidate and must therefore be a necessary precondition for the hearing. it also considers that the concept of conflict of interest must cover only objective and verifiable factors which can only be assessed in the light of a specific area of responsibility. parliament therefore concludes that the committee on legal affairs must both assess the possibility of a conflict of interest and, if necessary, recommend how to eliminate it. it may be recommended to waive certain financial interests or to change the area of responsibility of a commissioner. in order to ensure the effectiveness of the inquiry, the rapporteur considers that the committee on legal affairs should request additional information if the declaration raises doubts, is incomplete or contradictory.
in writing. - i voted yes. the european parliament's recommendation on guidelines for declarations of interests of commissioners aims to ensure an open, fair and consistent evaluation of all commissioners-designate and to prevent potential conflicts of interest.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. in order to ensure the independence and integrity of the members of the commission, it is necessary to increase the effectiveness of the application of declarations of interests. the commission should amend the code of conduct and declarations of interests of its members and ensure that sufficient information is included therein. in order to increase public confidence in the eu institutions, the verification of declarations of interests must be a necessary precondition for a hearing. it is necessary to strengthen the role of the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament and to define the scope of the examination of declarations of interests. furthermore, the concept of conflict of interest should cover only objective and verifiable factors which can be assessed in the light of a specific area of responsibility. it is of particular importance that the restrictions on the recruitment of commissioners after their term of office be extended for a period of at least three years, which should not be less than the period during which former members of the commission are entitled to a transitional allowance.
in writing. ‒ as the example of the former president of the commission shows, not all commissioners are inclined to declare their interests honestly or to comply with the requirements of fair dealing. sadly, it seems that this club of dubious reputation has recently been joined by another former commissioner who has moved to the world bank an institution which, according to media reports, has recently secured significantly increased eu funding flows. we must therefore seek to regulate more effectively the activities of the eu's most highly paid officials - the members of the commission. and, of course, the application of higher moral standards would also be a welcome recommendation to the member states nominating the members of the commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on liability and compensation for offshore oil and gas operations and their financial security. following the deepwater horizon oil spill in april 2010, the maritime safety directive was adopted to set minimum requirements for the prevention of major accidents in the eu's oil and gas operations and to limit the consequences of such accidents. i therefore support the rapporteur's claim that the commission must work more closely with the member states to ensure that the appropriate legal framework governing any activity at sea is in place before a serious accident occurs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which deals with liability and compensation for offshore oil and gas operations and their financial security. the european parliament stresses that the effective application of the polluter pays principle to offshore oil and gas operations should cover not only the prevention and remediation of environmental damage, as is currently done to some extent under the safety at sea and environmental liability directives, but also the costs associated with meeting the requirements for compensation for traditional damage, as provided for under the precautionary principle and the principle of sustainable development. parliament therefore calls on the commission to consider the possibility of creating a legislative mechanism for compensation for damage caused by accidents at sea similar to that provided for in the norwegian act on oil-related activities and applicable at least to those sectors which may suffer significant negative impacts, such as fisheries, coastal tourism and other sectors of the blue economy. in this context, it recommends that the problems or accidents encountered by companies in the course of their activities be assessed from a quantitative and qualitative point of view and that any secondary effects on the parties concerned be identified. also underlines the differences and shortcomings in the transposition and application of the environmental liability provisions of the environmental liability directive, as also pointed out by the commission in its second implementation report.
in writing. - i voted yes. in its resolution on liability and compensation for oil and gas operations at sea and their financial security, the european parliament calls on the commission and the member states to develop additional measures to ensure the safety of oil and gas operations at sea more effectively in the event of a major disaster. for example, the directive currently in force does not provide for civil liability for damage to natural or legal persons, nor for criminal liability for accidents at sea, possible fines and other non-custodial penalties. although safety at sea offences are covered by the criminal code in many countries, there is no harmonised definition of the offence, nor is there any harmonised definition of the minimum nature and level of sanctions at eu level. the introduction of criminal liability at eu level could become another deterrent, which does not include civil liability, and thus could ensure better environmental protection and compliance with safety measures.
in writing. in particular, civil and criminal liability for damage caused by accidents arising from offshore oil and gas exploration, exploitation and production must be established at eu level. in addition, a balanced decision on the mandatory financial guarantee and a uniform and comprehensive compensation mechanism must be adopted. it is necessary to provide for compensation for claims by third parties for traditional damage, as well as for an effective compensation mechanism to administer the relevant payments. the parties responsible must be obliged to pay, in a timely and appropriate manner, the compensation which they are legally entitled to for damage and losses suffered by natural or legal persons and for damage caused to the environment. it is important to ensure that operators or other responsible parties have sufficient financial resources to meet claims for compensation. in order to implement the envisaged measures, the commission should cooperate more closely with the member states and ensure that the compensation and financial security systems applicable to offshore oil and gas operations in the eu are developed and implemented as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ the issue of liability for accidents at sea related to hydrocarbon extraction is quite complex and, in my opinion, not sufficiently regulated. i therefore welcome this initiative to extend the existing legal framework while making it clearer.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the european order for payment procedure. this procedure will make it easy for creditors to seek an order for the recovery of uncontested civil and commercial claims. moreover, this procedure can be requested in writing or, in some cases, by electronic means, and does not require the assistance of a lawyer, and is mandatory in another member state and does not require any additional formalities.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines the application of the european order for payment procedure. the purpose of the european order for payment procedure is to facilitate the recovery of sums in cross-border judicial proceedings. this procedure is optional: this means that it can be used as an alternative to the various national procedures applicable in cross-border cases. in simple terms, this procedure will make it easy for creditors to seek an order to recover uncontested civil and commercial claims. this procedure can be requested in writing or, in some cases, by electronic means and does not require the assistance of a lawyer, and is carried out in another member state without any additional formalities. the european order for payment shall be issued automatically on the basis of a request only, but the debtor may lodge an objection within 30 days. in the event of such an objection, the order procedure shall be terminated and a competitive judicial procedure may be initiated.
in writing. i agree with the report. in particular, the european order for payment procedure should be extended to the eu as a whole, as it allows for the settlement of debts owed by persons established in the member states of the european union in a cheap and expeditious manner. it should be noted that the european order for payment procedure is currently applied differently in different member states. this complicates and prolongs the process of dealing with monetary claims of an international nature and creates additional financial and administrative burdens. the commission has a special role to play in ensuring the effective implementation of this procedure in the eu. it shall provide timely and detailed implementation reports and take concrete steps to further inform all stakeholders. in addition, the european order for payment procedure should be made faster and more flexible in order to be applied effectively.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation on deep-sea fish stocks and their fisheries in the international waters of the north-east atlantic. the text of the agreement was put to the vote in the committee on fisheries on 12 july 2016 and approved by a large majority. since the council's position at first reading is in line with the agreement reached at the tripartite dialogue meetings, the rapporteur of the european parliament proposes that the committee endorse it without further amendments. the main aspects of this compromise would be that the european union would freeze the fishing impact indicator when setting the zones where deep-sea fishing would be allowed. this zone covers the area where targeted fishing took place in 2009-2011 in the north-east atlantic waters of europe. this geographical limitation will apply to deep-sea fishing vessels, i.e. those vessels whose deep-sea catch exceeds 8% of their total catch on at least one fishing trip per year. the european parliament also succeeded in introducing specific sanctions for vessels that infringe the deep sea fisheries regulation and in ensuring that a number of control rules are not subject to any exemption. parliament and council negotiators agreed to set a bathymetric limit of 800 m. the new provision aims to improve the protection of vulnerable marine ecosystems on the seabed.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on a sustainable eu policy for the cultural and creative industries. in the 21st century, as europe moves towards a digital economy, traditional production processes are increasingly being replaced or supplanted by the cultural and creative sectors (hereinafter referred to as 'ccps'). the cultural and creative industries are based on cultural values, individual creativity and skills and have the potential to create wealth and jobs through the value of intellectual property. cultural and creative activities are based on, among others, the following sectors: architecture, archives and libraries, crafts, cultural heritage, design. unlike other industries, the cfp has a dual intrinsic value: it plays a key role in preserving and supporting the diversity of european cultures and languages, it strengthens the sense of european and regional identity, it helps to transmit knowledge and values and it preserves the tangible and intangible european heritage for present and future generations. it is therefore strategically important to support an innovative and research-oriented european kic, which is capable of both preserving linguistic and cultural diversity and pluralism and offering innovative and high-quality services, especially in the context of market integration and globalisation. i voted in favour because i share the rapporteur's view that, in order to exploit the full potential of the sector, coordinated action is needed at national, regional and local level, as well as at eu level.

for the verts/ale group climate change, globalisation, market instability, unfair business practices these are just some of the causes of price volatility that we will continue to face in the future. in these circumstances, we must ensure that the smallest farms, especially family farms, survive, because they create jobs in remote regions and support rural vitality. as you know, direct payments are a forecast and fixed part of the income of the holding, which is particularly important in times of crisis. direct payments allow the farmer to plan this part of the income, the farmer knows exactly when and how much, what payments he will receive, but the current inequalities in direct payments distort the market. i regret that the report did not take account of the budget committee's essential observation that, in order to ensure a level playing field in the single market and a sustainable use of agricultural resources throughout the european union, direct payments must be harmonised between member states. production costs are similar across europe. is it not time to show that the european union is in solidarity and that it values the work of every farmer equally, no matter where he works? another important proposal is the education of farmers. in order to avoid crises, it is important to educate farmers on how to avoid crises, how to reduce their impact, how to choose the right measures and not waste resources, and how to ensure sustainable farming.
in writing. the agricultural market has always been characterised by volatility and price fluctuations. in recent years, due to rapid and significant changes in demand, supply and prices, it has become a structural feature of agriculture in europe, but also on a global scale. there are many reasons for this. climate change and pests in agriculture have a negative impact on agricultural production, which has a direct impact on prices. the european union's responsibility for contributing to food safety in europe must therefore be increased. european farmers, especially those from the new member states, as well as lithuania, are increasingly exposed to risks beyond their control. the eu should therefore increase its aid to farmers in these countries. the eu should guarantee stability in the agricultural sector, as price fluctuations create a high level of uncertainty for producers and consumers. low prices put producers at risk of losing their profits and investment capacity, while high food prices create difficulties in the purchase of basic foodstuffs, leading to a crisis situation. it is necessary to provide member states with additional tools and guarantee assistance in the field of crop, animal and plant protection, investment funds and a new income stabilisation instrument. this will help to eliminate the long-standing instability in the agricultural sector.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft european parliament resolution on the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of uzbekistan, of the other part, on bilateral trade in textile products. in december 2011, the european parliament adopted a preliminary report indicating that it would accept the agreement on the condition that the human rights situation in uzbekistan improved, in particular by abolishing child and forced labour in the cotton harvest. following the adoption of the abovementioned report, a dialogue was established with uzbekistan and annual hearings were organised with representatives of civil society, the uzbek authorities, the eu and other international institutions. close cooperation between uzbekistan and the international labour organisation (ilo) has also been established to assess the progress made towards the elimination of child and any other form of forced labour in the cotton harvesting sector in uzbekistan. the cotton harvesting monitoring mission (cms) was carried out in 2013, 2014 and 2015. the report of the last ilo monitoring mission shows that the use of child labour in the cotton harvest is practically eliminated. the ilo has confirmed that child labour has become a singular and socially unacceptable phenomenon. therefore, in the light of the ongoing dialogue and fruitful cooperation, the european parliament should support the efforts of the uzbek authorities in supporting the protocol to the agreement with uzbekistan on textile products, in view of the progress made by uzbekistan in this area.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the european parliament's draft legislative resolution on the eu-norway agreement on mutual access to fishing in the skagerrak strait. in the kattegat and skagerrak straits, swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together for the same fish since the middle ages. the fact that two countries have become eu member states has not changed the principle that fishermen from these three countries should enjoy historical fishing rights in the skagerrak and kattegat straits. the eu's common fisheries policy (cfp) provides a framework for the management of fish stocks in the waters covered by the policy. this policy supports the historical rights of fishermen. the new agreement gives danish, norwegian and swedish vessels exclusive fishing rights in their waters up to four nautical miles from the baselines. it provides for mutual access by the two eu member states and norway to the respective waters of the other contracting parties in the skagerrak and kattegat area on a permanent basis, while ensuring sound conservation and fisheries management measures in this area. it also allows for control measures in line with the principles of normal coastal state jurisdiction, such as those applicable to fisheries in the north sea. i supported this agreement because it contributes to supporting historic fishing rights in this area and it will also help to implement the improved cfp in the kattegat and skagerrak straits.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the recommendation on the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on the reciprocal access to the skagerrak for vessels flying the flags of denmark, norway and sweden. under this agreement, these three countries had reciprocal access to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat straits up to four nautical miles from their respective baselines. the agreement was initially valid for 35 years, until 2002, and was subsequently extended for two five-year periods, until 2012. however, norway has terminated the agreement in the light of recent developments in international fisheries law. after some time, norway entered into formal negotiations with the commission, which is negotiating on behalf of the european union, with a view to concluding an agreement on mutual access to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat area, replacing the previous agreement. as the new agreement is in conformity with the provisions of the un convention on the law of the sea and subsequent related agreements, i hereby approve the agreement.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation on the eu-norway agreement on mutual access to fishing in the skagerrak strait. the 1966 agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on mutual access to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat entered into force in 1967. under this agreement, which was supplemented in 1980 by a bilateral fisheries agreement between the european union and norway, the three countries had reciprocal access to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat straits up to four nautical miles from their respective baselines. the agreement also provides that for the purposes of such fishing, that area is to be considered as international waters. the agreement thus governed the relations between flag states and coastal states. in the light of recent developments in international fisheries law, and in particular after the entry into force of the 1982 un convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 un fisheries agreement, norway has concluded that the existing agreement is not compatible with the current provisions of the law of the sea. norway was most concerned about the control provisions. in addition, it considered that the agreement did not comply with the principles of normal coastal state jurisdiction under the un convention on the law of the sea and the current principles of conservation and management. the new agreement grants danish, norwegian and swedish vessels exclusive fishing rights in their waters up to four nautical miles from baselines.
in writing. ‒ fishing in the skagerrak is a small but important issue for the functioning of the european economic area. although the issue is essentially technical and does not raise major political objections, its rapid resolution demonstrates the efficiency of the functioning of the eea.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the eu-norway agreement on mutual access to fishing in the skagerrak strait. danish, norwegian and swedish fishermen have traditionally always fished together in the kattegat and skagerrak straits. the agreement proposes to continue to guarantee the historical fishing rights of danish, norwegian and swedish fishermen in the kattegat and skagerrak straits, without prejudice to the rights of other states' fishermen, while ensuring that appropriate fisheries management and conservation measures are taken in these waters. this agreement also contributes to the implementation of the reformed eu fisheries management system, taking into account the objectives and basic principles of the new common fisheries policy (cfp). this is particularly true for the application of mandatory measures to maintain stocks at levels that ensure sustainable fishing. in addition to these principles, i also agree with the need to emphasise that any third country's access to the internal market must be based on reciprocity. in addition, in the case of norway, the eu customs duties on food products, including fishery products, are in line with the agreement on the european economic area. the commission must ensure that the customs duties applicable to food and fishery products in the eu are set in a way that does not conflict with the principles of free trade in food products, including fishery products.

in writing. ‒ the i voted against the amendments which proposed to reject the council's position. i support the proposal to regulate the accounting of railway undertakings. the existing regulation no 1192/69 on the common rules for the organisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, which the commission proposes to repeal, allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for the payment obligations they assume, which other transport undertakings are not obliged to assume. these obligations may relate, for example, to special payments in the event of accidents at work (the railway undertaking is obliged to pay them, but the state pays them in the case of other transport undertakings). the regulation was adopted before the liberalisation of the railway market, i.e. when european rail transport was developing mainly in member states where integrated companies operating both rail services and rail infrastructure were operating. at that time, the regulation was intended to ensure that railway undertakings and other transport undertakings were treated equally in the burden-sharing of social costs. for the original purposes of the regulation, it contains a list listing the formerly state-owned railway companies. this list has been adjusted several times to take account of the accession of new member states and currently comprises 40 companies. however, the commission notes that this regulation no longer takes into account the current legal environment that discriminates against non-listed companies, since the possibility of receiving compensation is granted only to 40 companies listed in the annex to this regulation. i therefore support the proposals of the commission and the council to repeal that regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal on common accounting standards for railway undertakings. the purpose of the notification is to repeal regulation (ec) no 1192/69, which allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for payment obligations which other transport undertakings are not obliged to assume.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation on the accounting standards for railway undertakings. the regulation, which the commission proposes to repeal, allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for payment obligations they have assumed, which other transport undertakings are not obliged to assume. these obligations may relate, for example, to special payments for accidents at work (the railway undertaking is obliged to pay them, but the state pays them for other types of transport undertakings), pensions for railway workers who normally retire early because of certain heavy work, or payments for the cost of the transition infrastructure. at that time, the aim of the regulation was to ensure that railway undertakings and other transport undertakings were treated equally in the allocation of social and externalities costs. moreover, at that time the relationship between the governments and the mainly state-owned railway companies was not yet regulated by contracts and the two entities were linked by a much closer chain of ownership. for the original purposes of the regulation, it contains a list listing the formerly state-owned railway companies. this list has been adjusted several times to take account of the accession of new member states and currently comprises 40 companies. as the commission states in its proposal, this regulation no longer takes account of the current legal environment. parliament agrees that the current text of the regulation is discriminatory, since only 40 companies listed in the annex to this regulation are eligible for compensation, and that there is no way to keep this regulation in force unless the list of railway companies is kept up to date.
in writing. ‒ i supported the commission's proposal to repeal regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common accounting standards for railway undertakings, as the adoption of a large number of new documents regulating the railway sector means that the current legal environment is no longer taken into account by this regulation.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the research programme of the research foundation for coal and steel. the european union has been supporting research into coal and steel for more than 50 years. this started in 1951 with the signing of the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community (ecsc). when this contract expired in 2002, it was decided to transfer eapb's assets (and the related interest) to the research fund for coal and steel (apmtf). the programme is financed by the proceeds of the remaining (non-operating) assets of eapb. it shall be administered by the commission. the emff is complementary to horizon 2020 but is not managed under it. the emff allocates some eur 50 million to both the coal and steel sectors (72,8% for the steel sector and 27,2% for the coal sector). it brings together industrial partners, smes, the best research centres and universities from across the european union to develop knowledge and stimulate innovation in this field. the research funded covers production processes, resource use and conservation, environmental improvement and occupational safety in the relevant sectors. the commission proposes to facilitate access to funding for beneficiaries by simplifying the rules and aligning them proportionally with the rules of the horizon 2020 research framework programme, which are familiar to stakeholders in the coal and steel sectors.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposals to amend the council decision on the research programme of the research fund for coal and steel. the aim of this proposal is to facilitate access to funding for beneficiaries, to simplify the rules and to align them proportionately with the rules of the framework programme for research.
in writing. ‒ unfortunately, parliament adopted this very unbalanced text on the research programme of the research foundation for coal and steel and the multiannual technical guidelines for that programme. unfortunately, we have not been able to remove allusions to the support of shale gas extraction from the text. nor was it possible to include provisions on technologically advanced steel production methods or greater transparency in the work of the expert groups.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the so-called research programme on coal and steel because it is necessary to introduce better conditions and guidelines. the coal and steel sectors are important in the european integration process and play a key role in the overall structure of the union industry. but at the same time, working conditions in these sectors are very difficult and often have a negative impact on the health of workers and citizens. therefore, factories and enterprises should comply with all conditions related to civil liability, final decisions, mitigation of social restructuring or plant liquidation. where possible, the public partners should be consulted on issues related to public accountability and job protection.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the common agricultural policy (cap) measures to reduce price fluctuations in agricultural product markets. the dependence of farming on biological processes has led to uncertainty in related markets. the globalisation of trade in agricultural products also poses health risks (disease outbreaks) and risks of surges in supply or demand. they are driven by external factors related to the eu's external policies in the areas of trade, diplomacy or development cooperation, and thus entail even greater uncertainty and economic risks for the future. therefore, risk management measures in agriculture are receiving increasing attention. the growing interest in this topic is reflected in the gradual introduction of these measures into agricultural policy. the volatility of agricultural product prices is already a major factor in the current dramatic situation of many european farmers, and the current cap risk management measures are clearly not adapted to limit the impact of price volatility on farmers' incomes. the eu must find solutions to this phenomenon in the cap. in order to send a clear message to all citizens and to farmers in particular, the resolution seeks to limit itself to the fight against price volatility and clearly identifies three key steps needed to achieve this: strengthening the structure of supply chains and intensifying the conclusion of contracts; better protecting farmers' incomes by putting in place appropriate measures to manage the risk of price volatility; increasing market transparency by setting up price monitoring centres.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the cap measures to reduce price fluctuations in agricultural product markets. the cap has been characterised by strong market regulation. the cap was designed to guarantee prices. the price regulation ensured that farmers were guaranteed minimum prices for their products in the event of a crisis. however, over time, the cap has been reformed cyclically, and price regulation has changed significantly. the new risk management package is provided for in the second pillar (rural development) of the cap after the 2013 reform. the current risk management measures for the second pillar of the cap are therefore clearly not adapted to limit the impact of price fluctuations on farmers' incomes. in this context, i support parliament's recommendation to strengthen the current second pillar measures to increase the competitiveness of european agriculture and to involve producer organisations more closely in the implementation process.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the measures of the common agricultural policy (cap) to reduce price fluctuations on the markets for agricultural products. farming depends on biological processes and is therefore strongly affected by climatic conditions and plant and animal diseases. these natural factors are beyond the farmer's control. the development of farm performance is therefore much more difficult to define than for enterprises in other sectors of the economy. income uncertainty is particularly detrimental to investment and innovation and may therefore threaten the economic viability of farms. in addition, the seasonality of agricultural production leads to an inherent tendency for agricultural markets to fluctuate. it is widely recognised that too much volatility is not good for producers (market signals are expressed and therefore income is contingent) or for consumers (the choice of food products is altered). variability is a complex phenomenon with diverse and sometimes controversial origins. following a sharp rise in agricultural prices on world markets in 2007/08, they began to fluctuate strongly. this phenomenon has also been placed on the international political agenda because of its potential impact on global food security. in 2011, the g20 therefore adopted an action plan to reduce food price volatility and for agriculture, which led to the establishment of an agricultural product market information system to increase transparency in agricultural products markets. the market is likely to experience further uncertainty and increased economic and climate risks in the future.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on cap measures to reduce price volatility in agricultural product markets. i hope they will help to ensure price stability, food security and the competitive position of european farmers on the world market.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the eu has done a great deal of work in securing measures that have helped to increase the stability of agricultural prices. of course, the work is not yet complete and will have to continue, especially in the preparation of the new cap beyond 2020.
in writing. i welcome the fact that additional market monitoring measures have been extended to other sectors.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive on third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas or whose nationals are exempt from that requirement (revision of the suspension mechanism). visa policy is an essential element of the european union, affecting both external action and internal security. the evolution of the political and migration situation has led to the need to review the suspension of the visa waiver mechanism in order to make it more favourable and flexible, while ensuring that the eu is able to respond to a variety of exceptional circumstances arising from: a significant and sudden increase in the number of illegal third-country nationals residing illegally on eu territory; an increase in the number of unjustified asylum applications from third-country nationals; threats to security in the european territory. at the same time, it should be borne in mind that the renewal of the visa requirement for third-country nationals is one of the most stringent policy measures that can be taken. i agree that this measure must be applied in conjunction with strong guarantees and the protection of human rights, including on the basis of statistical reports provided by european agencies and competent forces and law enforcement authorities. this will ensure the rights of third-country nationals and guarantee the application of the principles of the community visa policy. the amendments to regulation (ec) no 539/2001 of the european parliament and of the council adopted on 11 december 2013 have identified essential aspects, such as the suspension of the visa waiver mechanism, which is now being amended.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the lists of third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and those whose nationals are exempt from that requirement (revision of the suspension mechanism). visa policy is an essential element of the european union, affecting both external action and internal security. it is so important that it clearly establishes that in the legislative field the legislators share competence through the ordinary legislative procedure. the reciprocity mechanism, which outweighs the suspension mechanism, was amended by an interinstitutional agreement, the legality of which was confirmed by the court of justice of the eu on 16 july 2015. this court judgment provides the basis for the proper use of delegated and implementing acts, thus ensuring an institutional balance. the evolution of the political and migration situation, in particular in the light of the recent visa liberalisation processes, has led to the need to reconsider the suspension of the visa waiver to make it more favourable and flexible. it is clear that elements must be provided to enable the eu to respond to a variety of special circumstances. however, this flexibility must be accompanied by robust safeguards and human rights safeguards, as well as statistical reports from european agencies and competent forces and law enforcement authorities. only in this way will it be possible to safeguard the rights of third-country nationals and guarantee the application of the principles of the community visa policy.
