in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on aid for people affected by thalidomide. since 1957, when the german pharmaceutical company chemie grünenthal placed thalidomide, an anti-nausea medicine also intended for pregnant women, on the european market, at least 20 000 children have been born with severe physical defects as a result of its exposure. in europe, there are more than 4 000 people affected by thalidomide, including 2 800 in germany, 450 in italy, 400 in the united kingdom, 400 in spain, 103 in sweden and about 90 in austria. the findings of the 2015 study 'health, quality of life and employment of thalidomide victims in the united kingdom' reveal the increasing physical and psychological problems faced by thalidomide victims over time, as well as their specific medical, financial and social needs. i voted in favour of the resolution on the need to fully recognise the claims of thalidomide survivors in europe in order to ensure their autonomy, access to healthcare and maintain a good quality of life. i support the need for victims to be compensated for the necessary but costly and growing costs of their health care.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the european parliament draws attention to the fact that the parliament and the european commission are now able and willing to remedy, in the light of ethical and humanitarian standards, the damage caused by the failure of pharmaceutical controls and subsequent suppression of evidence, which led to the thalidomide tragedy. the parliament also notes that in june 2016 the german federal government recognised the need and the possibility to amend the german legislation on the thalidomide fund by january 2017. parliament therefore urges the member states and the commission to take coordinated action and measures to officially recognise and compensate those affected by thalidomide. calls furthermore on the german federal government to make use of the possibility provided by the forthcoming legislation on the partial amendment of the thalidomide fund to allow thalidomide victims recognised as such under court-appointed trust schemes or beneficiaries of national government schemes to access the special german health fund thalidomide fund for the disabled. parliament also urged the commission to develop a framework protocol at european level to provide equal compensation to all european citizens affected by thalidomide, regardless of their member state of origin, and to develop an eu programme of aid and support (including financial and social support provisions) for thalidomide victims and their families.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on support for people affected by thalidomide. the resolution calls for the use of this medicine to ensure access to health care services for those affected and to maintain a good quality of life, and for compensation to cover the necessary but costly and growing costs of their health care.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the regulation on paediatric medicines. the paediatric regulation has had a major impact on the development of paediatric medicines, there has been a significant increase in paediatric clinical trials and paediatric research projects, and more quality information is now available on the use of approved medicines in paediatric medicine. the regulation has helped to improve the overall situation, with tangible benefits for the treatment of a wide range of childhood diseases. however, in some areas, notably paediatric oncology and neonatology, there has been insufficient progress. i therefore support the call in this resolution for the commission to submit in a timely manner the report provided for in article 50 of the paediatric medicines regulation and the request that this report describe in detail and thoroughly examine the current barriers to innovation in paediatric medicines. i also voted in favour of calling for amendments to the regulation, based on those conclusions, taking due account of the development plans for paediatric medicines, which are based not only on the type of disease but also on the mechanism of action of the medicinal product, on disease and drug prioritisation models, taking into account unmet medical needs in paediatrics, and finally on incentives to encourage more research and to better meet the needs of the paediatric population, ensuring the evaluation of the costs of research and development and full transparency of clinical outcomes.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on international aviation agreements. in the european aviation strategy, the commission proposed to open negotiations on eu-level aviation security agreements with japan and china and eu-level air services agreements with china, turkey and the six gulf cooperation council member states, armenia and asean. international agreements in the field covered by the ordinary legislative procedure require parliament's consent. similarly, when the commission negotiates agreements between the union and third countries or international organisations, parliament must be kept promptly and fully informed at all stages of the negotiation procedure for international agreements. in order to be able to decide whether or not to give its consent at the end of the negotiations, parliament must monitor the process from the outset. i am of the opinion that parliament should be kept informed at all stages of the negotiations on a regular basis and, if necessary, in confidence, from the outset, of the progress of the process and that this information should be made available to parliament in such a way as to allow it sufficient time to express its opinion if necessary. parliament, in turn, must ensure that the full confidentiality of the negotiations in progress is maintained when it receives confidential information.
